Painel de Análise do Editor Acompanhe toda a atividade do seu repositório com um resumo detalhado de downloads que exibe o total de downloads de todos os Models e Datasets publicados pela sua organização. Alterne entre as visualizações “All Time” e “Last Month” para obter insights sobre seus repositórios em diferentes períodos. Detalhamento por repositório Explore as métricas de repositórios individuais com a tabela de detalhamento por repositório. Utilize o recurso de busca integrado para localizar rapidamente repositórios específicos. Cada linha também apresenta um gráfico de série temporal que ilustra a tendência de downloads ao longo do tempo. Exportar Analytics do Publisher como CSV Baixe um arquivo CSV abrangente contendo análises de todos os seus repositórios, incluindo a atividade de download de modelos e conjuntos de dados. Você também pode acessar esses dados programaticamente por meio do seguinte endpoint de API: Copiado curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \ "https://huggingface.co/organizations/YOUR_ORG_NAME/settings/publisher-analytics/download-breakdown" \ --output breakdown.csv Estrutura da Resposta O arquivo CSV é composto por registros de download diários para cada um dos seus modelos e conjuntos de dados. Copiado repoType ,repoName,total,timestamp,downloads model ,huggingface/CodeBERTa-small-v1, 4362460 , 2021 - 01 - 22 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 4 model ,huggingface/CodeBERTa-small-v1, 4362460 , 2021 - 01 - 23 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 7 model ,huggingface/CodeBERTa-small-v1, 4362460 , 2021 - 01 - 24 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 2 dataset ,huggingface/documentation-images, 2167284 , 2021 - 11 - 27 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 3 dataset ,huggingface/documentation-images, 2167284 , 2021 - 11 - 28 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 18 dataset ,huggingface/documentation-images, 2167284 , 2021 - 11 - 29 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 7 Estrutura de Objeto do Repositório Cada registro no CSV contém: repoType : O tipo de repositório (por exemplo, “model”, “dataset”) repoName : Nome completo do repositório, incluindo a organização (por exemplo, “huggingface/documentation-images”) total : Número acumulado de downloads para este repositório timestamp : data formatada em ISO 8601 (UTC) downloads : Número de downloads naquele dia Os registros são ordenados cronologicamente e fornecem uma visão diária detalhada da atividade de download para cada repositório. Os números de download não são deduplicados por usuário. Se você precisar de contagens de download únicas, consulte a próxima seção. Baixadores exclusivos e logs mais granulares Este recurso é um complemento para o plano Enterprise Plus . Como um recurso avançado, o Hugging Face pode exportar logs de acesso anônimos, no nível de requisição, para todos os modelos e conjuntos de dados publicados pela sua organização. Cada linha representa uma única requisição relacionada a download, oferecendo granularidade total sobre os dados de download dos seus modelos e conjuntos de dados. Sua equipe é responsável por ingerir esses logs e executar cálculos neles. A exportação inclui intencionalmente códigos de status HTTP brutos e métodos para que você possa classificar padrões de solicitação como HEAD , conteúdo parcial, redirecionamento e outros, com base nas suas próprias necessidades de análise. Coluna Descrição timestamp Carimbo de data e hora da solicitação status Código de status HTTP (por exemplo, 200 , 206 , 302 , 307 , 304 ) method Método HTTP (por exemplo, GET , HEAD ) repoName Nome completo do repositório (ex.: nvidia/segformer-b0 ) repoType Tipo de repositório: model , dataset ou space hashedUserId Hash não reversível do ID do usuário (se autenticado) hashedIp Hash não reversível do endereço IP (se não autenticado) country Código ISO do país region Nome da região ou cidade userAgent Cabeçalho HTTP User-Agent Como é necessário configurar um pipeline de exportação de dados personalizado do nosso lado (índice Elastic personalizado, etc.), isso está disponível apenas como um complemento para o Enterprise Plus. datasets and Spaces Faster examples with accelerated inference Switch between documentation themes Sign Up to get started Copy page قائمة التحقق من إصدار النموذج/النماذج يُعدّ Hugging Face Hub المنصة المرجعية لمشاركة نماذج تعلّم الآلة. يمكن للإصدار المنفَّذ باحترافية أن يعزّز ظهور نموذجك وتأثيره. تغطي هذه القسم الخطوات الأساسية لإصدار نموذج موجز ومفيد وسهل الاستخدام. هل تنوي الإصدار باستخدام وكيل برمجي؟ ثبّت مهارة hf سطر الأوامر ليتمكن وكيلك من التعامل عنك مع عملية الرفع وبطاقة النموذج والبيانات الوصفية. ⏳ تجهيز نموذجك للإصدار رفع أوزان النموذج عند رفع النماذج إلى Hub، اتبع أفضل الممارسات التالية: استخدام مستودعات منفصلة لأوزان نماذج مختلفة : أنشئ مستودعات فردية لكل متغير من نفس البنية. يتيح لك ذلك تجميعها في مجموعة ، وهي أسهل في التنقل من قوائم المجلدات. كما يحسّن هذا الظهور لأن لكل نموذج عنوان URL خاصًا به ( hf.co/org/model-name )، ويجعل البحث أسهل، ويوفر عدد مرات التنزيل لكل نموذج من نماذجك. مثال رائع على ذلك هو مجموعة Qwen3-VL الحديثة التي تضم متغيرات مختلفة من بنية VL. يُفضَّل استخدام safetensors بدلاً من pickle لتسلسل الأوزان. : safetensors أكثر أماناً وسرعة من pickle أو pth في بايثون. إذا كان لديك ملف pickle بصيغة .bin ، فاستخدم أداة تحويل الأوزان لتحويله. اكتب بطاقة نموذج شاملة بطاقة نموذج مُصمَّمة بعناية (ملف README.md في مستودعك) ضرورية للعثور على النموذج، وإعادة إنتاج نتائجه، ومشاركته بفعالية. تأكد من تضمين ما يلي: إعداد البيانات الوصفية : يُعدّ قسم البيانات الوصفية (YAML) في أعلى بطاقة النموذج عنصراً أساسياً للبحث والتصنيف. يتضمن: تم النسخ --- pipeline_tag: text-generation # Specify the task library_name: transformers # Specify the library language: - en # List languages your model supports license: apache-2.0 # Specify a license datasets: - username/dataset # List datasets used for training base_model: username/base-model # If applicable (your model is a fine-tune, quantized, merged version of another model) tags: # Add extra tags which would make the repo searchable using the tag - tag1 - tag2 --- إذا أنشأت README.md في واجهة الويب، فسترى نموذجًا يحتوي على أهم حقول البيانات الوصفية التي نوصي بها 🤗. نموذج البيانات الوصفية في واجهة مستخدم Hub وصف تفصيلي للنموذج : قدّم شرحًا واضحًا لما يفعله نموذجك، وبنيته المعمارية، وحالات الاستخدام المقصودة. ساعد المستخدمين على اتخاذ قرار سريع بشأن ما إذا كان يناسب احتياجاتهم. أمثلة على الاستخدام : قدّم مقاطع كود واضحة يمكن نسخها وتشغيلها مباشرةً للاستدلال أو الضبط الدقيق أو المهام الشائعة الأخرى. قلّل إلى الحد الأدنى التعديلات التي يحتاج المستخدمون إلى إجرائها. مكافأة إضافية : أضف notebook.ipynb منظمًا بشكل جيد في المستودع يعرض الاستدلال أو الضبط الدقيق، بحيث يمكن للمستخدمين فتحه مباشرة في Google Colab و Kaggle Notebooks . أزرار الاستخدام في Google وKaggle المواصفات التقنية : تضمّن معاملات التدريب، ومتطلبات الأجهزة، وأي تفاصيل أخرى تساعد المستخدمين على تشغيل النموذج بفعالية. مقاييس الأداء : شارك نتائج الاختبارات المرجعية والتقييم. شمل مقاييس كمية وأمثلة نوعية لإظهار نقاط القوة والقيود. القيود والتحيزات : وثّق القيود والتحيزات والمقاييس الأخلاقية المعروفة حتى يتمكن المستخدمون من اتخاذ قرارات مستنيرة. لجعل العملية أكثر سلاسة، انقر على استيراد قالب بطاقة النموذج لملء ملفات README.md مسبقًا بمواقع نائبة. زر استيراد قالب بطاقة النموذج قسم من القالب المستورد تحسين قابلية اكتشاف النماذج وسهولة استخدامها لتحقيق أقصى قدر من الانتشار وسهولة الاستخدام: تكامل المكتبات : أضِف دعمًا لإحدى المكتبات المتكاملة مع Hugging Face Hub (مثل transformers ، diffusers ، sentence-transformers ، timm ). يزيد هذا التكامل بشكل كبير من إمكانية الوصول إلى نموذجك، ويوفّر للمستخدمين مقتطفات أكواد للتعامل مع نموذجك. على سبيل المثال، لتحديد أن نموذجك يعمل مع مكتبة transformers : تم النسخ --- library_name: transformers --- تبويب مقتطف الشيفرة يمكنك أيضًا تسجيل مكتبة نماذجك الخاصة أو إضافة دعم Hub إلى مكتبتك وقاعدة الكود الخاصة بك، حتى يعرف المستخدمون كيفية تنزيل أوزان النماذج من Hub. لقد كتبنا دليلاً شاملاً حول أفضل الممارسات في عملية الرفع هنا . يُتيح لك استخدام مكتبة مسجّلة أيضًا تتبع تنزيلات نموذجك بمرور الوقت. بيانات وصفية صحيحة : وسم خط الأنابيب: اختر وسم خط الأنابيب الصحيح حتى يظهر نموذجك في عمليات البحث والوحدات المناسبة. أمثلة على وسوم خطوط الأنابيب الشائعة: text-generation - لنماذج اللغة التي تولّد النص text-to-image - لنماذج توليد الصور من النص image-text-to-text - لنماذج الرؤية واللغة (VLMs) التي تولّد النص text-to-speech - للنماذج التي تولّد الصوت من النص الترخيص: معلومات الترخيص بالغة الأهمية للمستخدمين لفهم كيفية استخدام النموذج. أوراق البحث : إذا كان لديك أوراق بحثية مرتبطة بنموذجك، فاستشهد بها في بطاقة النموذج. سيتم ربطها تلقائيًا . تم النسخ ## References * [ Model Paper ]( https://huggingface.co/papers/xxxx.xxxxx ) المجموعات : إذا كنت تنوي إصدار عدة نماذج أو متغيرات ذات صلة، فقم بتنظيمها في مجموعة . تساعد المجموعات المستخدمين على اكتشاف النماذج ذات الصلة وفهم العلاقات بين الإصدارات. التجارب التفاعلية : أنشئ مساحة Hugging Face تتضمن تجربة تفاعلية. يتيح ذلك للمستخدمين تجربة نموذجك دون كتابة أي أكواد. كما يمكنك ربط النموذج من المساحة ليظهر في واجهة صفحة النموذج. تم النسخ ## Demo Try this model directly in your browser: [ Space Demo ]( https://huggingface.co/spaces/username/model-demo ) عند إنشاء عرض توضيحي، حمّل النموذج من مستودعه على Hub (وليس من مصادر خارجية مثل Google Drive). يربط هذا بين المخرجات ويحسّن من مستوى الظهور الإصدارات المُكمّاة : فكّر في رفع الإصدارات المُكمّاة (مثل GGUF) في مستودع منفصل لتحسي

search_index.content: Чек-лист выпуска модели(ей) · Hugging Face Hub documentation Чек-лист выпуска модели(ей) Hub 🏡 View all docs AWS Trainium & Inferentia Accelerate Bitsandbytes CLI Chat UI Dataset viewer Datasets Deploying on AWS Diffusers Google Cloud Google TPUs Gradio Hub Hub Python Library Huggingface.js Inference Endpoints (dedicated) Inference Providers Kernels LeRobot Leaderboards Lighteval Microsoft Azure OpenEnv Optimum PEFT Reachy Mini Safetensors Sentence Transformers TRL Tasks Text Embeddings Inference Tokenizers Trackio Transformers Transformers.js Xet smolagents timm Search documentation AR EN ES FR ID JA KO PT RU TR VI ZH API docs Join the Hugging Face community and get access to the augmented documentation experience Collaborate on models, datasets and Spaces Faster examples with accelerated inference Switch between documentation themes Sign Up to get started Copy page Чек-лист выпуска модели(ей) Hugging Face Hub — это основная платформа для обмена моделями машинного обучения. Качественный релиз способен повысить видимость и влияние вашей модели. В этом разделе описаны ключевые шаги для создания краткого, информативного и удобного для пользователя релиза модели. Выпускаете с помощью кодинг-агента? Установите hf CLI Skill , чтобы агент самостоятельно занимался загрузкой, карточкой модели и метаданными. ⏳ Подготовка модели к выпуску Загрузка весов модели При загрузке моделей в Hub следуйте этим рекомендациям: Используйте отдельные репозитории для разных весов моделей : Создавайте отдельные репозитории для каждого варианта одной и той же архитектуры. Это позволяет сгруппировать их в коллекцию , которая удобнее для навигации, чем список каталогов. Это также повышает видимость, поскольку у каждой модели есть свой URL ( hf.co/org/model-name ), упрощает поиск и предоставляет счётчики загрузок для каждой из ваших моделей. Отличный пример — недавняя коллекция Qwen3-VL , в которой представлены различные варианты архитектуры VL. Для сериализации весов предпочитайте safetensors вместо pickle . : safetensors безопаснее и быстрее, чем pickle или pth в Python. Если у вас есть pickle-файл .bin , используйте инструмент для конвертации весов , чтобы преобразовать его. Создание подробной карточки модели Хорошо оформленная карточка модели (файл README.md в вашем репозитории) необходима для обнаружения, воспроизводимости и эффективного обмена. Убедитесь, что вы охватили: Конфигурация метаданных : Раздел metadata (YAML) в начале вашей карточки модели имеет ключевое значение для поиска и категоризации. Включите: Скопировано --- pipeline_tag: text-generation # Specify the task library_name: transformers # Specify the library language: - en # List languages your model supports license: apache-2.0 # Specify a license datasets: - username/dataset # List datasets used for training base_model: username/base-model # If applicable (your model is a fine-tune, quantized, merged version of another model) tags: # Add extra tags which would make the repo searchable using the tag - tag1 - tag2 --- Если вы создадите README.md в веб-интерфейсе, вы увидите форму с наиболее важными полями метаданных, которые мы рекомендуем 🤗. Форма метаданных в интерфейсе Hub Подробное описание модели : Дайте четкое объяснение того, что делает ваша модель, какова ее архитектура и для каких задач она предназначена. Это поможет пользователям быстро определить, подходит ли она для их нужд. Примеры использования : Предоставляйте понятные фрагменты кода, которые можно скопировать и запустить для вывода, дообучения или других типовых задач. Минимизируйте количество правок, которые пользователям придётся вносить. Бонус : добавьте в репозиторий хорошо структурированный notebook.ipynb с примером инференса или дообучения, чтобы пользователи могли открыть его напрямую в Google Colab и Kaggle Notebooks . Кнопки использования Google и Kaggle Технические характеристики : Включите параметры обучения, требования к аппаратному обеспечению и другие сведения, которые помогут пользователям эффективно запускать модель. Метрики производительности : Делитесь результатами бенчмарков и оценок. Включайте количественные метрики и качественные примеры, чтобы показать сильные стороны и ограничения. Ограничения и предвзятость : Опишите известные ограничения, предвзятость и этические аспекты, чтобы пользователи могли принимать обоснованные решения. Чтобы сделать процесс более плавным, нажмите Import model card template , чтобы автоматически заполнить README.md с помощью плейсхолдеров. Кнопка для импорта шаблона карточки модели Раздел импортированного шаблона Улучшение обнаруживаемости и удобства использования моделей Чтобы максимально расширить охват и повысить удобство использования: Интеграция с библиотеками : Добавьте поддержку одной из множества библиотек, интегрированных с Hugging Face Hub (например, transformers , diffusers , sentence-transformers , timm ). Эта интеграция значительно повышает доступность вашей модели и предоставляет пользователям фрагменты кода для работы с ней. Например, чтобы указать, что ваша модель работает с библиотекой transformers : Скопировано --- library_name: transformers --- Вкладка с фрагментом кода Вы также можете зарегистрировать собственную библиотеку моделей или добавить поддержку Hub в свою библиотеку и кодовую базу, чтобы пользователи знали, как скачивать веса моделей из Hub. Мы написали подробное руководство по лучшим практикам загрузки здесь . Использование зарегистрированной библиотеки также позволяет отслеживать количество загрузок вашей модели во времени. Правильные метаданные : Метка конвейера: Выберите правильную метку конвейера , чтобы ваша модель отображалась в соответствующих поисковых запросах и виджетах. Примеры распространённых тегов конвейеров: text-generation - для языковых моделей, генерирующих текст text-to-image - для моделей генерации изображений по тексту image-text-to-text — для моделей «зрение-язык» (VLM), генерирующих текст text-to-speech — для моделей, генерирующих аудио из текста Лицензия: Информация о лицензи

Панель аналитики издателя Отслеживайте всю активность в вашем репозитории с помощью подробного обзора загрузок, который показывает общее количество загрузок всех моделей и наборов данных, опубликованных вашей организацией. Переключайтесь между видами «За всё время» и «За последний месяц», чтобы получать аналитику по вашим репозиториям за разные периоды. Разбивка по репозиториям Изучайте метрики отдельных репозиториев с помощью таблицы детализации по репозиториям. Используйте встроенный поиск, чтобы быстро найти конкретные репозитории. Каждая строка также содержит график временного ряда, демонстрирующий динамику загрузок во времени. Экспорт аналитики издателя в CSV Скачайте подробный файл CSV с аналитикой по всем вашим репозиториям, включая активность загрузок моделей и наборов данных. Вы также можете получить доступ к этим данным программно через следующий API-эндпоинт: Скопировано curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \ "https://huggingface.co/organizations/YOUR_ORG_NAME/settings/publisher-analytics/download-breakdown" \ --output breakdown.csv Структура ответа Файл CSV содержит записи о ежедневных загрузках для каждой из ваших моделей и наборов данных. Скопировано repoType ,repoName,total,timestamp,downloads model ,huggingface/CodeBERTa-small-v1, 4362460 , 2021 - 01 - 22 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 4 model ,huggingface/CodeBERTa-small-v1, 4362460 , 2021 - 01 - 23 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 7 model ,huggingface/CodeBERTa-small-v1, 4362460 , 2021 - 01 - 24 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 2 dataset ,huggingface/documentation-images, 2167284 , 2021 - 11 - 27 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 3 dataset ,huggingface/documentation-images, 2167284 , 2021 - 11 - 28 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 18 dataset ,huggingface/documentation-images, 2167284 , 2021 - 11 - 29 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 7 Структура объекта репозитория Каждая запись в CSV содержит: repoType : тип репозитория (например, «model», «dataset») repoName : Полное имя репозитория с указанием организации (например, “huggingface/documentation-images”) total : накопленное количество загрузок этого репозитория timestamp : дата в формате ISO 8601 (UTC) downloads : количество загрузок за этот день Записи упорядочены по хронологии и обеспечивают ежедневный детальный обзор активности загрузок для каждого репозитория. Диаграммы загрузок не дедуплицируются по пользователям. Если вам нужны уникальные количества загрузок, обратитесь к следующему разделу. Уникальные загрузчики и более детальные журналы Эта функция является дополнением к плану Enterprise Plus . В качестве расширенной функции Hugging Face позволяет экспортировать анонимизированные журналы доступа на уровне запросов для всех моделей и наборов данных, опубликованных вашей организацией. Каждая строка представляет собой отдельный запрос, связанный с загрузкой, что обеспечивает полную детализацию данных о загрузках ваших моделей и наборов данных. Ваша команда отвечает за сбор этих журналов и выполнение вычислений на их основе. Экспорт намеренно включает необработанные коды состояния HTTP и методы, чтобы вы могли классифицировать запросы HEAD , частичного содержимого, перенаправления и другие паттерны запросов в соответствии с собственными аналитическими потребностями. Столбец Описание timestamp Метка времени запроса status Код состояния HTTP (например, 200 , 206 , 302 , 307 , 304 ) method HTTP-метод (например, GET , HEAD ) repoName Полное имя репозитория (например, nvidia/segformer-b0 ) repoType Тип репозитория: model , dataset или space hashedUserId Необратимый хэш идентификатора пользователя (если аутентифицирован) hashedIp Необратимый хэш IP-адреса (если пользователь не аутентифицирован) country Код страны ISO region Название региона или города userAgent Заголовок HTTP User-Agent Поскольку для этого необходимо настроить собственный конвейер экспорта данных на нашей стороне (собственный индекс Elastic и т. д.), эта функция доступна только как дополнение к Enterprise Plus. Um lançamento bem executado pode aumentar a visibilidade e o impacto do seu modelo. Esta seção aborda as etapas essenciais para um lançamento de modelo conciso, informativo e amigável ao usuário. Lançando com um agente de código? Instale a hf CLI Skill para que seu agente gerencie o upload, o model card e os metadados por você. ⏳ Preparando seu modelo para lançamento Carregar pesos do modelo Ao enviar modelos para o Hub, siga estas melhores práticas: Use repositórios separados para diferentes pesos de modelo : Crie repositórios individuais para cada variante da mesma arquitetura. Isso permite agrupá-los em uma coleção , que é mais fácil de navegar do que listagens de diretórios. Também melhora a visibilidade, pois cada modelo tem sua própria URL ( hf.co/org/model-name ), facilita a busca e fornece contagens de download para cada um dos seus modelos. Um ótimo exemplo é a recente coleção Qwen3-VL , que apresenta diversas variantes da arquitetura VL. Preferir safetensors em vez de pickle para serialização de pesos. : safetensors é mais seguro e rápido que o pickle ou pth do Python. Se você tiver um arquivo pickle .bin , use a ferramenta de conversão de pesos para convertê-lo. Escreva um cartão de modelo abrangente Um cartão de modelo bem elaborado (o README.md no seu repositório) é essencial para a descoberta, a reprodutibilidade e o compartilhamento eficaz. Certifique-se de abordar: Configuração de metadados : A seção de metadados (YAML) no topo do seu cartão de modelo é fundamental para busca e categorização. Inclua: Copiado --- pipeline_tag: text-generation # Specify the task library_name: transformers # Specify the library language: - en # List languages your model supports license: apache-2.0 # Specify a license datasets: - username/dataset # List datasets used for training base_model: username/base-model # If applicable (your model is a fine-tune, quantized, merged version of another model) tags: # Add extra tags which would make the repo searchable using the tag - tag1 - tag2 --- Se você criar o README.md na interface web, verá um formulário com os campos de metadados mais importantes que recomendamos 🤗. Formulário de Metadados na Interface do Usuário do Hub Descrição detalhada do modelo : Forneça uma explicação clara sobre o que seu modelo faz, sua arquitetura e seus casos de uso pretendidos. Ajude os usuários a decidirem rapidamente se ele atende às suas necessidades. Exemplos de uso : Forneça trechos de código claros, prontos para copiar e executar, para inferência, ajuste fino ou outras tarefas comuns. Mantenha ao mínimo as edições necessárias por parte dos usuários. Bônus : Adicione um notebook.ipynb bem estruturado no repositório mostrando inferência ou ajuste fino, para que os usuários possam abri-lo diretamente no Google Colab e Kaggle Notebooks . Botões de uso do Google e Kaggle Especificações técnicas : Inclua os parâmetros de treinamento, as necessidades de hardware e outros detalhes que ajudem os usuários a executar o modelo de forma eficaz. Métricas de desempenho : Compartilhe benchmarks e resultados de avaliação. Inclua métricas quantitativas e exemplos qualitativos para demonstrar pontos fortes e limitações. Limitações e vieses : Documente as limitações, os vieses e as considerações éticas conhecidas para que os usuários possam tomar decisões informadas. Para tornar o processo mais fluido, clique em Import model card template para preencher os README.md s com espaços reservados. O botão para importar o modelo de cartão de modelo Uma seção do modelo importado Melhorar a descoberta e a usabilidade de modelos Para maximizar o alcance e a usabilidade: Integração de bibliotecas : Adicione suporte a uma das muitas bibliotecas integradas ao Hugging Face Hub (como transformers , diffusers , sentence-transformers , timm ). Essa integração aumenta significativamente a acessibilidade do seu modelo e fornece aos usuários trechos de código para trabalhar com ele. Por exemplo, para especificar que seu modelo funciona com a biblioteca transformers : Copiado --- library_name: transformers --- Aba de trecho de código Você também pode registrar sua própria biblioteca de modelos ou adicionar suporte ao Hub à sua biblioteca e base de código, para que os usuários saibam como baixar os pesos dos modelos do Hub. Escrevemos um guia extenso sobre melhores práticas de upload aqui . O uso de uma biblioteca registrada também permite que você acompanhe os downloads do seu modelo ao longo do tempo. Metadados corretos : Tag de pipeline: Escolha a tag de pipeline correta para que seu modelo apareça nas buscas e widgets adequados. Exemplos de tags comuns de pipeline: text-generation - Para modelos de linguagem que geram texto text-to-image - Para modelos de geração de texto para imagem image-text-to-text - Para modelos de visão-linguagem (VLMs) que geram texto text-to-speech - Para modelos que geram áudio a partir de texto Licença: As informações de licença são cruciais para que os usuário

O serviço é operado pelos Inference Providers, com créditos mensais inclusos para usuários PRO e organizações Team & Enterprise. Os Inference Providers oferecem aos desenvolvedores um acesso simplificado e unificado a centenas de modelos de machine learning, impulsionado pelos melhores parceiros de inferência serverless. 👉 Para a documentação completa, visite a Documentação dos Inference Providers . Provedores de Inferência no Hub Inference Providers é profundamente integrado ao Hugging Face Hub e pode ser usado de algumas maneiras diferentes: Widgets interativos - Teste modelos diretamente nas páginas de modelos com widgets interativos que usam Inference Providers por baixo dos panos. Veja a página do modelo DeepSeek-R1-0528 para um exemplo. Inference Playground - Teste e compare facilmente modelos de conclusão de chat com seus prompts. Confira o Inference Playground para começar. Busca - Filtre modelos por provedor de inferência na página de modelos para encontrar modelos disponíveis por meio de provedores específicos. Data Studio - Use IA para explorar conjuntos de dados no Hub. Experimente o Data Studio no seu conjunto de dados favorito. Construa com provedores de inferência Você pode integrar os Inference Providers aos seus próprios aplicativos usando nossos SDKs ou clientes HTTP. Aqui está uma introdução rápida com Python e JavaScript; para mais detalhes, consulte a Documentação dos Inference Providers . python javascript Você pode usar nosso SDK em Python para interagir com os Inference Providers. Copiado from huggingface_hub import InferenceClient import os client = InferenceClient( api_key=os.environ[ "HF_TOKEN" ], provider= "auto" , # Automatically selects best provider ) # Chat completion completion = client.chat.completions.create( model= "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324" , messages=[{ "role" : "user" , "content" : "A story about hiking in the mountains" }] ) # Image generation image = client.text_to_image( prompt= "A serene lake surrounded by mountains at sunset, photorealistic style" , model= "black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev" ) Ou, você pode simplesmente usar o cliente compatível com a API da OpenAI. Copiado import os from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( base_url= "https://router.huggingface.co/v1" , api_key=os.environ[ "HF_TOKEN" ], ) completion = client.chat.completions.create( model= "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324" , messages=[ { "role" : "user" , "content" : "A story about hiking in the mountains" } ], ) O cliente compatível com a API da OpenAI não é suportado para geração de imagens. Você pode usar nosso SDK em JavaScript para interagir com os Inference Providers. Copiado import { InferenceClient } from "@huggingface/inference" ; const client = new InferenceClient (process. env . HF_TOKEN ); const chatCompletion = await client. chatCompletion ({ provider : "auto" , // Automatically selects best provider model : "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324" , messages : [{ role : "user" , content : "Hello!" }] }); const imageBlob = await client. textToImage ({ model : "black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev" , inputs : "A serene lake surrounded by mountains at sunset, photorealistic style" , }); Ou, você pode simplesmente usar o cliente compatível com a API da OpenAI. Copiado import { OpenAI } from "openai" ; const client = new OpenAI ({ baseURL : "https://router.huggingface.co/v1" , apiKey : process. env . HF_TOKEN , }); const completion = await client. chat . completions . create ({ model : "meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct" , messages : [{ role : "user" , content : "A story about hiking in the mountains" }], }); O cliente compatível com a API da OpenAI não é suportado para geração de imagens. Você precisará de um token do Hugging Face com permissões de inferência. Crie um em Configurações > Tokens . Como o Inference Providers funciona Para aprofundar-se nos Inference Providers, consulte a Documentação dos Inference Providers . Aqui estão alguns recursos principais: Início rápido Guia de Preços e Faturamento Detalhes da Integração com o Hub O que era a API HF-Inference? A API HF-Inference é um dos provedores disponíveis por meio dos Inference Providers. Anteriormente chamada de “Inference API (serverless)”, ela é impulsionada por Inference Endpoints por baixo dos panos. Para mais detalhes sobre o provedor HF-Inference especificamente, confira sua página dedicada . Update on GitHub ← Exemplos de Widgets Estatísticas de download de modelos →

A well-executed release can boost your model’s visibility and impact. This section covers essential steps for a concise, informative, and user-friendly model release. Releasing with a coding agent? Install the hf CLI Skill to let your agent handle the upload, model card, and metadata for you. ⏳ Preparing Your Model for Release Upload Model Weights When uploading models to the Hub, follow these best practices: Use separate repositories for different model weights : Create individual repositories for each variant of the same architecture. This lets you group them into a collection , which are easier to navigate than directory listings. It also improves visibility because each model has its own URL ( hf.co/org/model-name ), makes search easier, and provides download counts for each one of your models. A great example is the recent Qwen3-VL collection which features various variants of the VL architecture. Prefer safetensors over pickle for weight serialization. : safetensors is safer and faster than Python’s pickle or pth . If you have a .bin pickle file, use the weight conversion tool to convert it. Write a Comprehensive Model Card A well-crafted model card (the README.md in your repository) is essential for discoverability, reproducibility, and effective sharing. Make sure to cover: Metadata Configuration : The metadata section (YAML) at the top of your model card is key for search and categorization. Include: Copied --- pipeline_tag: text-generation # Specify the task library_name: transformers # Specify the library language: - en # List languages your model supports license: apache-2.0 # Specify a license datasets: - username/dataset # List datasets used for training base_model: username/base-model # If applicable (your model is a fine-tune, quantized, merged version of another model) tags: # Add extra tags which would make the repo searchable using the tag - tag1 - tag2 --- If you create the README.md in the Web UI, you’ll see a form with the most important metadata fields we recommend 🤗. Metadata Form on the Hub UI Detailed Model Description : Provide a clear explanation of what your model does, its architecture, and its intended use cases. Help users quickly decide if it fits their needs. Usage Examples : Provide clear, copy-and-run code snippets for inference, fine-tuning, or other common tasks. Keep edits needed by users to a minimum. Bonus : Add a well-structured notebook.ipynb in the repo showing inference or fine-tuning, so users can open it in Google Colab and Kaggle Notebooks directly. Google and Kaggle Usage Buttons Technical Specifications : Include training parameters, hardware needs, and other details that help users run the model effectively. Performance Metrics : Share benchmarks and evaluation results. Include quantitative metrics and qualitative examples to show strengths and limitations. Limitations and Biases : Document known limitations, biases, and ethical considerations so users can make informed choices. To make the process more seamless, click Import model card template to pre-fill the README.md s with placeholders. The button to import the model card template A section of the imported template Enhance Model Discoverability and Usability To maximize reach and usability: Library Integration : Add support for one of the many libraries integrated with the Hugging Face Hub (such as transformers , diffusers , sentence-transformers , timm ). This integration significantly increases your model’s accessibility and provides users with code snippets for working with your model. For example, to specify that your model works with the transformers library: Copied --- library_name: transformers --- Code snippet tab You can also register your own model library or add Hub support to your library and codebase, so the users know how to download model weights from the Hub. We wrote an extensive guide on uploading best practices here . Using a registered library also allows you to track downloads of your model over time. Correct Metadata : Pipeline Tag: Choose the correct pipeline tag so your model shows up in the right searches and widgets. Examples of common pipeline tags: text-generation - For language models that generate text text-to-image - For text-to-image generation models image-text-to-text - For vision-language models (VLMs) that generate text text-to-speech - For models that generate audio from text License: License information is crucial for users to understand how they can use the model. Research Papers : If your model has associated papers, cite them in the model card. They will be cross-linked automatically . Copied ## References * [ Model Paper ]( https://huggingface.co/papers/xxxx.xxxxx ) Collections : If you’re releasing multiple related models or variants, organize them into a collection . Collections help users discover related models and understand relationships across versions. Demos : Create a Hugging Face Space with an interactive demo. This lets users try your model without writing code.

Publisher Analytics Dashboard Track all your repository activity with a detailed downloads overview that shows total downloads for all the Models and Datasets published by your organization. Toggle between “All Time” and “Last Month” views to gain insights across your repositories over different periods. Per-repo breakdown Explore the metrics of individual repositories with the per-repository drill-down table. Utilize the built-in search feature to quickly locate specific repositories. Each row also features a time-series graph that illustrates the trend of downloads over time. Export Publisher Analytics as CSV Download a comprehensive CSV file containing analytics for all your repositories, including model and dataset download activity. You can also access this data programmatically via the following API endpoint: Copied curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \ "https://huggingface.co/organizations/YOUR_ORG_NAME/settings/publisher-analytics/download-breakdown" \ --output breakdown.csv Response Structure The CSV file is made of daily download records for each of your models and datasets. Copied repoType ,repoName,total,timestamp,downloads model ,huggingface/CodeBERTa-small-v1, 4362460 , 2021 - 01 - 22 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 4 model ,huggingface/CodeBERTa-small-v1, 4362460 , 2021 - 01 - 23 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 7 model ,huggingface/CodeBERTa-small-v1, 4362460 , 2021 - 01 - 24 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 2 dataset ,huggingface/documentation-images, 2167284 , 2021 - 11 - 27 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 3 dataset ,huggingface/documentation-images, 2167284 , 2021 - 11 - 28 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 18 dataset ,huggingface/documentation-images, 2167284 , 2021 - 11 - 29 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 7 Repository Object Structure Each record in the CSV contains: repoType : The type of repository (e.g., “model”, “dataset”) repoName : Full repository name including organization (e.g., “huggingface/documentation-images”) total : Cumulative number of downloads for this repository timestamp : ISO 8601 formatted date (UTC) downloads : Number of downloads for that day Records are ordered chronologically and provide a daily granular view of download activity for each repository. Download figures are not deduplicated by user. If you need unique download counts, refer to the next section. Advanced Publisher Analytics: unique downloaders and more granular logs This feature is an add-on for the Enterprise Plus plan. As an advanced feature, Hugging Face can export anonymized, request-level access logs for all of the models and datasets published by your organization. Each line represents a single download-related request, giving you full granularity over your models and datasets’ download data. Your team is responsible for ingesting these logs and running computations on them. The export intentionally includes raw HTTP status codes and methods so you can classify HEAD , partial-content, redirect, and other request patterns based on your own analytics needs. Column Description timestamp Request timestamp status HTTP status code (for example 200 , 206 , 302 , 307 , 304 ) method HTTP method (for example GET , HEAD ) repoName Full repo name (e.g. nvidia/segformer-b0 ) repoType Repository type: model , dataset , or space hashedUserId Non-reversible hash of user ID (if authenticated) hashedIp Non-reversible hash of IP address (if unauthenticated) country Country ISO code region Region or city name userAgent HTTP User-Agent header As it requires setting up a custom data export pipeline on our side (custom Elastic index, etc), this is only available as an add-on to Enterprise Plus. Service is powered by Inference Providers, with monthly included credits for PRO users and Team & Enterprise organizations. Inference Providers give developers streamlined, unified access to hundreds of machine learning models, powered by the best serverless inference partners. 👉 For complete documentation, visit the Inference Providers Documentation . Inference Providers on the Hub Inference Providers is deeply integrated with the Hugging Face Hub, and you can use it in a few different ways: Interactive Widgets - Test models directly on model pages with interactive widgets that use Inference Providers under the hood. Check out the DeepSeek-R1-0528 model page for an example. Inference Playground - Easily test and compare chat completion models with your prompts. Check out the Inference Playground to get started. Search - Filter models by inference provider on the models page to find models available through specific providers. Data Studio - Use AI to explore datasets on the Hub. Check out Data Studio on your favorite dataset. Build with Inference Providers You can integrate Inference Providers into your own applications using our SDKs or HTTP clients. Here’s a quick start with Python and JavaScript, for more details, check out the Inference Providers Documentation . python javascript You can use our Python SDK to interact with Inference Providers. Copied from huggingface_hub import InferenceClient import os client = InferenceClient( api_key=os.environ[ "HF_TOKEN" ], provider= "auto" , # Automatically selects best provider ) # Chat completion completion = client.chat.completions.create( model= "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324" , messages=[{ "role" : "user" , "content" : "A story about hiking in the mountains" }] ) # Image generation image = client.text_to_image( prompt= "A serene lake surrounded by mountains at sunset, photorealistic style" , model= "black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev" ) Or, you can just use the OpenAI API compatible client. Copied import os from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( base_url= "https://router.huggingface.co/v1" , api_key=os.environ[ "HF_TOKEN" ], ) completion = client.chat.completions.create( model= "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324" , messages=[ { "role" : "user" , "content" : "A story about hiking in the mountains" } ], ) The OpenAI API compatible client is not supported for image generation. You can use our JavaScript SDK to interact with Inference Providers. Copied import { InferenceClient } from "@huggingface/inference" ; const client = new InferenceClient (process. env . HF_TOKEN ); const chatCompletion = await client. chatCompletion ({ provider : "auto" , // Automatically selects best provider model : "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324" , messages : [{ role : "user" , content : "Hello!" }] }); const imageBlob = await client. textToImage ({ model : "black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev" , inputs : "A serene lake surrounded by mountains at sunset, photorealistic style" , }); Or, you can just use the OpenAI API compatible client. Copied import { OpenAI } from "openai" ; const client = new OpenAI ({ baseURL : "https://router.huggingface.co/v1" , apiKey : process. env . HF_TOKEN , }); const completion = await client. chat . completions . create ({ model : "meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct" , messages : [{ role : "user" , content : "A story about hiking in the mountains" }], }); The OpenAI API compatible client is not supported for image generation. You’ll need a Hugging Face token with inference permissions. Create one at Settings > Tokens . How Inference Providers works To dive deeper into Inference Providers, check out the Inference Providers Documentation . Here are some key resources: Quick Start Pricing & Billing Guide Hub Integration Details What was the HF-Inference API? HF-Inference API is one of the providers available through Inference Providers. It was previously called “Inference API (serverless)” and is powered by Inference Endpoints under the hood. For more details about the HF-Inference provider specifically, check out its dedicated page . Update on GitHub ← Widget Examples Models Download Stats →

search_index.description: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
search_index.content: Collections · Hugging Face Hub documentation Collections Hub 🏡 View all docs AWS Trainium & Inferentia Accelerate Bitsandbytes CLI Chat UI Dataset viewer Datasets Deploying on AWS Diffusers Google Cloud Google TPUs Gradio Hub Hub Python Library Huggingface.js Inference Endpoints (dedicated) Inference Providers Kernels LeRobot Leaderboards Lighteval Microsoft Azure OpenEnv Optimum PEFT Reachy Mini Safetensors Sentence Transformers TRL Tasks Text Embeddings Inference Tokenizers Trackio Transformers Transformers.js Xet smolagents timm Search documentation AR EN ES FR ID JA KO PT RU TR VI ZH API docs Join the Hugging Face community and get access to the augmented documentation experience Collaborate on models, datasets and Spaces Faster examples with accelerated inference Switch between documentation themes Sign Up to get started Copy page Collections Use Collections to group repositories from the Hub (Models, Datasets, Spaces and Papers) on a dedicated page. Collections have many use cases: Highlight specific repositories on your personal or organizational profile. Separate key repositories from others for your profile visitors. Showcase and share a complete project with its paper(s), dataset(s), model(s) and Space(s). Bookmark things you find on the Hub in categories. Have a dedicated page of curated things to share with others. Gate a group of models/datasets (Team & Enterprise) This is just a list of possible uses, but remember that collections are just a way of grouping things, so use them in the way that best fits your use case. Creating a new collection There are several ways to create a collection: For personal collections: Use the + New button on your logged-in homepage (1). For organization collections: Use the + New button available on organizations page (2). It’s also possible to create a collection on the fly when adding the first item from a repository page, select + Create new collection from the dropdown menu. You’ll need to enter a title and short description for your collection to be created. Adding items to a collection There are 2 ways to add items to a collection: From any repository page: Use the context menu available on any repository page then select Add to collection to add it to a collection (1). From the collection page: If you know the name of the repository you want to add, use the + add to collection option in the right-hand menu (2). It’s possible to add external repositories to your collections, not just your own. Collaborating on collections Organization collections are a great way to build collections together. Members with Read-only access can view collections, but only members with Write (or higher) organization permissions can create collections or add, edit, and remove items. Use the history feature to keep track of who has edited the collection. Collection options Collection visibility Public collections appear at the top of your profile or organization page and can be viewed by anyone. The first 3 items in each collection are visible directly in the collection preview (1). To see more, the user must click to go to the collection page. Set your collection to private if you don’t want it to be accessible via its URL (it will not be displayed on your profile/organization page). For organizations, private collections are only available to members of the organization. Gating Group Collections (Team & Enterprise) You can use a collection to gate all the models/datasets belonging to it, allowing you to grant (or reject) access to all of them at once. This feature is reserved for Team & Enterprise subscribers: more information about Gating Group Collections can be found in our dedicated doc . Assigning a collection to a Resource Group (Team & Enterprise) Organization collections can be assigned to a Resource Group to control which members can access them, the same way repositories are. You can pick a Resource Group when creating an organization collection, and members with the appropriate permissions can move a collection to a different Resource Group later from the collection’s menu. Private collections that belong to a Resource Group are only visible to members of that group. This feature is reserved for Team & Enterprise subscribers. Assigning a collection to a Resource Group controls access to that specific collection . To restrict who can create or edit organization Collections at all, see Granular feature access (Enterprise plans and above). Ordering your collections and their items You can use the drag and drop handles in the collections list (on the left side of your collections page) to change the order of your collections (1). The first two collections will be directly visible on your profile/organization pages. You can also sort repositories within a collection by dragging the handles next to each item (2). Deleting items from a collection To delete an item from a collection, click the trash icon in the menu that shows up on the right when you hover over an item (1). To delete the whole collection, click delete on the right-hand menu (2) - you’ll need to confirm this action. Adding notes to collection’s items It’s possible to add a note to any item in a collection to give it more context (for others, or as a reminder to yourself). You can add notes by clicking the pencil icon when you hover over an item with your mouse. Notes are plain text and don’t support markdown, to keep things clean and simple. URLs in notes are converted into clickable links. Adding images to a collection item Similarly, you can attach images to a collection item. This is useful for showcasing the output of a model, the content of a dataset, attaching an infographic for context, etc. To start adding images to your collection, you can click on the image icon in the contextual menu of an item. The menu shows up when you hover over an item with your mouse. Then, add images by dragging and dropping images from your computer. You can also click on the gray zone to select image f

This help content & information General Help Center experience Close Next Help Center Community Gmail Collaborate with Gemini in Gmail With Gemini in Gmail, you get a collaborative inbox assistant that can help you do things like: Summarize : Synthesize long email threads into concise bullet points. Draft : Create new emails or refine existing drafts for tone and clarity. Organize: Ask Gemini to do things like delete multiple emails or add labels. Search : Find specific details, like flight times or package tracking. Schedule : Propose meeting times based on your availability in Google Calendar. Feature availability This feature requires an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan. Learn about Gemini features and plans . Learn about supported languages for Google Workspace with Gemini . This feature is available in Google Workspace Experiments, a trusted tester program for users with personal accounts to try new AI features. Learn how to get started with Google Workspace Experiments . In this article, learn how to: Find Gemini in Gmail Access Gemini in Gmail settings Things to ask Gemini in Gmail Find Gemini in Gmail On your computer, open Gmail . At the top right, click Ask Gemini . On the right, use the Gemini in Gmail interface to manage your emails: Prompt box : At the bottom, type your request and then click Submit . More options : At the top left, access your conversation history, Gems, and other settings. "More options" menu Action Description History To review previous conversations with Gemini in Gmail, click View all . Learn how to find and manage your Gemini in Workspace conversation history . More suggestions To explore additional ways Gemini can help in Gmail, click View all . Gems To access custom AI experts designed for specific roles or tasks, click View all . Settings Manage your preferences, such as personalization settings for Gemini in Gmail . Send feedback Share your thoughts on Gemini in Gmail with Google. Report Flag inaccurate or inappropriate responses. Learn how to report abuse in Gemini in Workspace apps . Things to ask Gemini in Gmail Ask questions from the web Important: To get answers from the web, make sure to include phrases like “Use Google Search” or “Using web search” in your prompt. “Write a paragraph describing the weather today in Mountain View, California using web search.” “Help me write a paragraph explaining if lightning can strike the same place twice using only information from the web.” Draft an email or chat message You can use Gemini in Gmail to draft email or chat responses. On your computer, open Gmail . At the top right, click Ask Gemini . Enter a prompt. For example: “Draft an email to Kevin summarizing our progress on Project Clover.” “Refine this chat message I am sending to Lori: ‘We are good to start Project Clover.’ Make sure it’s professional and concise.” Click Submit . Find information from previous emails Gemini can get information on reservations, flights, packages, and other emails sent to your inbox. For example: “When is my package arriving?” “What time is my next flight?” Generate a Google Docs document You can ask Gemini in Gmail to create a Google Docs document. On your computer, open Gmail . At the top right, click Ask Gemini . Enter a prompt, for example: “Create a meeting notes agenda.” “Generate a draft with a response to this email.” “Create a quick project coordination doc with a 30/60/90 plan section.” Click Submit . Generate a Google Sheets spreadsheet You can ask Gemini in Gmail to create a Google Sheets spreadsheet. On your computer, open Gmail . At the top right, click Ask Gemini . Enter a prompt, for example: “Create a sheet to track my monthly expenses with columns for date, category, amount, and notes.” “Create a table for a project tracker in Google Sheets with columns for task, assignee, deadline, and status.” “Create a 10-day itinerary for a first-time visitor covering Tokyo, Kyoto, and Osaka.” “Create a visual dashboard in Sheets of this sales data.” Click Submit . Generate a Google Slides presentation You can ask Gemini in Gmail to create a slide in Google Slides with a single prompt. On your computer, open Gmail . At the top right, click Ask Gemini . Enter a prompt. For example: “Create a slide on quantum computing for a general audience with a modern design.” Optional: To give your presentation the same style as an existing slide deck, you can use @<presentation name> to reference it. For example: “Create a presentation based on @old_project”. Click Submit . Keep the tab open until Gemini generates your presentation. This may take up to several minutes. You can switch to other tabs or windows, but do not close the existing tab. Once the presentation is generated, you can open it in Google Slides to view and edit. Learn more about how to generate presentations with Gemini in Google Slides . Generate images You can ask Gemini in Gmail to generate images. On your computer, open Gmail . At the top right, click Ask Gemini . At the bottom, type your prompt. Example: “Create an image of a dog with glasses.” You can also: Change your prompt: Click Edit prompt . search_index.title: Bringing Grok to Everyone | SpaceXSI
search_index.description: Grok is now faster, sharper, and has improved multilingual support. It is available to everyone on the 𝕏 platform.
search_index.content: Bringing Grok to Everyone | SpaceXSI Back to news Dec 12, 2024 Bringing Grok to Everyone Grok is now faster, sharper, and has improved multilingual support. It is available to everyone on the 𝕏 platform. Since launching Grok-2 in August, we have been hard at work improving Grok on 𝕏, adding new features like web search, citations, and our recent image generator, Aurora. Over the past few weeks we have been quietly testing a new version of the Grok-2 model, which is three times faster and offers improved accuracy, instruction-following, and multi-lingual capabilities. Today we are excited to announce that we are beginning to roll out this new version of Grok-2 to all users on 𝕏 for free. As always, Premium and Premium+ users get higher usage limits and will be the first to access any new capabilities in the future. Try Grok on 𝕏 Try Now on 𝕏 Search results and citations Grok leverages the 𝕏 platform to understand what's happening in the world in real time. We recently launched two additional features to enhance this experience even further: web search and citations. Now Grok draws upon posts from 𝕏 and webpages from the broader internet to provide timely and accurate answers to your queries. We also added citations, so you can easily dive deeper into a source to learn more or verify the information provided by Grok. Search results in 𝕏 Citations in 𝕏 Grok, draw me! Grok excels at crafting creative photos and amusing memes. Now it has gotten even better with Aurora, our cutting-edge autoregressive image generation model. Aurora brings a new level of photorealism to your Grok image generations and we are thrilled to see all the images and memes that you are sharing. As part of our integration with the X platform, we also recently released the “draw me” feature, which lets users generate reimagined versions of themselves using information from their 𝕏 profile. If you see another user’s “draw me” post on 𝕏 and want to try it yourself, just click the “Create your version with Grok” button! Draw me in a santa hat Create your own version with Grok Create yours Grok, analysis! Today we’re also introducing the Grok button, a new feature that will appear on posts across your home timeline. This button is designed to help you discover relevant context, understand real-time events, and dive deeper into trending discussions. API access One month ago we released the public beta of our enterprise API along with preview models grok-beta and grok-vision-beta . Today we are adding two new models coming to our API: grok-2-1212 and grok-2-vision-1212 . These models bring improvements in accuracy, instruction-following, and multi-lingual capabilities and offer a great option for developers looking for a highly-steerable and intelligent model. As a result of our efficiency improvements, we are also lowering the price of these models to $2 / 1M input tokens and $10 / 1M output tokens. You can currently sign up and use the API with $25 free credits. Please sign up here or find out more . Instruction following performance Average Multi-IFEval score across all languages over 3 turns All languages English Spanish Portuguese Russian Hindi Chinese Italian French Japanese Korean In the coming weeks, Aurora is also coming to our API, enabling developers to generate photorealistic images for their applications. Stay tuned as we continue to improve Grok and broaden its reach in the coming months. If you are interested in helping us create tools that let the world create and understand, apply for positions here .

search_index.title: WebBrain for websites — Add a free AI guide to your website
search_index.description: Paste one script tag and every visitor gets an AI guide that explains your pages, answers questions, and fills in forms when you allow it. Free.
search_index.content: WebBrain for websites — Add a free AI guide to your website WebBrain for websites Add an AI guide to your website. Paste one line of code and every visitor can ask about the page they're on. WebBrain reads the page, answers from it, and, if you allow it, fills in forms and clicks through for them. Your website address Get your script Free No credit card. Nothing for visitors to install. Try the live demo Embed code Paste it before </body>. embed.js · data-site-id index.html Script Buttons JavaScript <!-- WebBrain for websites --> <script src = "https://sites.webbrain.one/embed.js" data-site-id = "site_your_id" defer ></script> <!-- That's it. The launcher appears in the corner, styled the way you set it up. --> <!-- Any element can ask a question --> <button data-webbrain-ask = "Compare these plans for a team of 5" > Which plan fits me? </button> <!-- Or let WebBrain act, when Ask + Act is on --> <button data-webbrain-act = "Fill in the demo request form" > Fill it in for me </button> // Open the assistant from your own UI WebBrain. open (); // Ask about the current page WebBrain. ask ( 'Summarize this page in 3 points' ); // Let it act (sites with Ask + Act enabled) WebBrain. act ( 'Add the annual plan to my cart' ); // Pick up dashboard changes without a reload WebBrain. reloadConfig (); Your real site ID is in the dashboard. Copy Google and X do it. Your website can, too. They put AI right where people are already reading and working. Give your visitors that same kind of help, built into your own website. Gmail + Gemini Clean up email with a simple request. Ask Gemini to find and archive messages without leaving Gmail. Here, it prepares an inbox cleanup for the user to review and confirm. See how Google does it Google product demo. Open full image. X + Grok Ask about the post you're reading. On X, readers can open Grok from a post to ask for context and understand what they're seeing. The help starts with the content already in front of them. See how X does it xAI product demo. Open full image. Now bring it to your website. Help readers understand an article, shoppers choose a product, or customers complete a form. WebBrain for Websites adds an AI guide to the site you already have, with actions only when you enable them. See how to add it Live on your site in three steps. No SDK to install and no build step. WebBrain loads after your page does and stays out of your styles. Add your site Enter your site's address in the dashboard. You get a site ID and your script tag right away. Paste one line Put the script before </body> . Anything that lets you add a script tag works: static sites, CMS themes, and single-page apps. Visitors ask A launcher appears in the corner. Visitors ask about the page they're on, and WebBrain answers from what's actually there. You decide what it can do. Every setting lives in the dashboard and reaches your site the moment you save. Visitors never see a key, a model picker, or a setup screen. Ask, or Ask and Act Keep WebBrain read-only, or let it type, tick boxes, and click buttons for the visitor, with a visible glow and a Stop button while it works. The server enforces your choice. Your model, your key Use any OpenAI-compatible endpoint: OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, DeepSeek, Gemini, Together AI, xAI, or your own server. Keys stay on the server. Starter questions Put one-click questions in the drawer, like “Summarize this page” or “Compare the plans,” so visitors know what to ask. Buttons in your page Turn any element into a question with data-webbrain-ask , or add “Explain this” buttons to every matching section with a CSS selector. Highlight to ask When a visitor selects text, a small pill offers to explain exactly that passage. Your look Light, dark, or matching the visitor's system. Choose the launcher style, icon, label, accent color, and corner. It's free. WebBrain for websites is free to use. Paid tiers with extra features will come later, for teams that want more. Get your script A few things worth knowing. What WebBrain sees, what it can do, and what it costs. Is it really free? Yes. The dashboard, the script, and the assistant your visitors use cost nothing. Paid tiers with extra features will come later for those who want them. What does WebBrain see on my site? The page the visitor has open, read as an accessibility tree (the same structure screen readers use), plus the visitor's question. That goes to WebBrain's server and on to the model configured for your site. API keys stay on the server and never reach the browser. Can it change anything on my site? Only if you allow it. In Ask mode WebBrain reads and answers. In Ask + Act mode it can type into fields, tick boxes, click buttons, and scroll, with a visible glow, cursor, and Stop button. Everything happens in the visitor's own tab, on their behalf; it can't touch your site's code. Which AI models can I use? Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint: OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, DeepSeek, Google Gemini, Together AI, xAI, or your own OpenAI-compatible server. Set it once in the dashboard; visitors never see a key or a model picker. Will it work on my site? If you can add a script tag before </body> , yes: static sites, CMS themes, and single-page apps alike. The assistant draws itself in its own shadow DOM, so your styles and its styles don't collide. How is this different from the WebBrain extension? The browser extension helps you on any site you visit. WebBrain for websites helps your visitors on your site, and they don't need to install anything. Both are built on the same open-source WebBrain engine. Give every visitor a guide to your site. Get your script Try the live demo

search_index.title: Working with the npm registry - GitHub Docs
search_index.description: You can configure npm to publish packages to GitHub Packages and to use packages stored on GitHub Packages as dependencies in an npm project.
search_index.content: Working with the npm registry - GitHub Docs Skip to main content Skip to content Collapse sidebar Expand sidebar In this article Working with the npm registry You can configure npm to publish packages to GitHub Packages and to use packages stored on GitHub Packages as dependencies in an npm project. Copy markdown In this article Authenticating to GitHub Packages Note GitHub Packages only supports authentication using a personal access token (classic). For more information, see Managing your personal access tokens . You need an access token to publish, install, and delete private, internal, and public packages. You can use a personal access token (classic) to authenticate to GitHub Packages or the GitHub API. When you create a personal access token (classic), you can assign the token different scopes depending on your needs. For more information about packages-related scopes for a personal access token (classic), see About permissions for GitHub Packages . To authenticate to a GitHub Packages registry within a GitHub Actions workflow, you can use: GITHUB_TOKEN to publish packages associated with the workflow repository. A personal access token (classic) with at least read:packages scope to install packages associated with other private repositories ( GITHUB_TOKEN can be used if the repository is granted read access to the package. See Configuring a package's access control and visibility ). Authenticating in a GitHub Actions workflow This registry supports granular permissions. For registries that support granular permissions, if your GitHub Actions workflow is using a personal access token to authenticate to a registry, we highly recommend you update your workflow to use the GITHUB_TOKEN . For guidance on updating your workflows that authenticate to a registry with a personal access token, see Publishing and installing a package with GitHub Actions . Note The ability for GitHub Actions workflows to delete and restore packages using the REST API is currently in public preview and subject to change. You can use a GITHUB_TOKEN in a GitHub Actions workflow to delete or restore a package using the REST API, if the token has admin permission to the package. Repositories that publish packages using a workflow, and repositories that you have explicitly connected to packages, are automatically granted admin permission to packages in the repository. For more information about the GITHUB_TOKEN , see Use GITHUB_TOKEN for authentication in workflows . For more information about the best practices when using a registry in actions, see Compromised runners . You can also choose to give access permissions to packages independently for GitHub Codespaces and GitHub Actions. For more information, see Configuring a package's access control and visibility and Configuring a package's access control and visibility . Authenticating with a personal access token You must use a personal access token (classic) with the appropriate scopes to publish and install packages in GitHub Packages. For more information, see Introduction to GitHub Packages . You can authenticate to GitHub Packages with npm by either editing your per-user ~/.npmrc file to include your personal access token (classic) or by logging in to npm on the command line using your username and personal access token. To authenticate by adding your personal access token (classic) to your ~/.npmrc file, edit the ~/.npmrc file for your project to include the following line, replacing TOKEN with your personal access token. Create a new ~/.npmrc file if one doesn't exist. //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=TOKEN To authenticate by logging in to npm, use the npm login command, replacing USERNAME with your GitHub username, TOKEN with your personal access token (classic), and PUBLIC-EMAIL-ADDRESS with your email address. If you are using npm CLI version 9 or greater and are logging in or out of a private registry using the command line, you should use the --auth-type=legacy option to read in your authentication details from prompts instead of using the default login flow through a browser. For more information, see npm-login . If GitHub Packages is not your default package registry for using npm and you want to use the npm audit command, we recommend you use the --scope flag with the namespace that hosts the package (the personal account or organization to which the package is scoped) when you authenticate to GitHub Packages. $ npm login --scope=@NAMESPACE --auth-type=legacy --registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com > Username: USERNAME > Password: TOKEN Publishing a package Note Package names and scopes must only use lowercase letters. The tarball for an npm version must be smaller than 256MB in size. The GitHub Packages registry stores npm packages within your organization or personal account, and allows you to associate a package with a repository. You can choose whether to inherit permissions from a repository, or set granular permissions independently of a repository. When you first publish a package, the default visibility is private. To change the visibility or set access permissions, see Configuring a package's access control and visibility . For more information on linking a published package with a repository, see Connecting a repository to a package . You can connect a package to a repository as soon as the package is published by including a repository field in the package.json file. You can also use this method to connect multiple packages to the same repository. For more information, see Publishing multiple packages to the same repository . Note If you publish a package that is linked to a repository, the package automatically inherits the access permissions of the linked repository, and GitHub Actions workflows in the linked repository automatically get access to the package, unless your organization has disabled automatic inheritance of access permissions. search_index.title: Working with the Container registry - GitHub Docs
search_index.description: You can store and manage Docker and OCI images in the Container registry.
search_index.content: Working with the Container registry - GitHub Docs Skip to main content Skip to content Collapse sidebar Expand sidebar In this article Working with the Container registry You can store and manage Docker and OCI images in the Container registry. Copy markdown In this article About the Container registry The Container registry stores container images within your organization or personal account, and allows you to associate an image with a repository. You can choose whether to inherit permissions from a repository, or set granular permissions independently of a repository. You can also access public container images anonymously. About Container registry support The Container registry currently supports the following container image formats: Docker Image Manifest V2, Schema 2 Open Container Initiative (OCI) Specifications When installing or publishing a Docker image, the Container registry supports foreign layers, such as Windows images. Authenticating to the Container registry Note GitHub Packages only supports authentication using a personal access token (classic). For more information, see Managing your personal access tokens . You need an access token to publish, install, and delete private, internal, and public packages. You can use a personal access token (classic) to authenticate to GitHub Packages or the GitHub API. When you create a personal access token (classic), you can assign the token different scopes depending on your needs. For more information about packages-related scopes for a personal access token (classic), see About permissions for GitHub Packages . To authenticate to a GitHub Packages registry within a GitHub Actions workflow, you can use: GITHUB_TOKEN to publish packages associated with the workflow repository. A personal access token (classic) with at least read:packages scope to install packages associated with other private repositories ( GITHUB_TOKEN can be used if the repository is granted read access to the package. See Configuring a package's access control and visibility ). Authenticating in a GitHub Actions workflow This registry supports granular permissions. For registries that support granular permissions, if your GitHub Actions workflow is using a personal access token to authenticate to a registry, we highly recommend you update your workflow to use the GITHUB_TOKEN . For guidance on updating your workflows that authenticate to a registry with a personal access token, see Publishing and installing a package with GitHub Actions . Note The ability for GitHub Actions workflows to delete and restore packages using the REST API is currently in public preview and subject to change. You can use a GITHUB_TOKEN in a GitHub Actions workflow to delete or restore a package using the REST API, if the token has admin permission to the package. Repositories that publish packages using a workflow, and repositories that you have explicitly connected to packages, are automatically granted admin permission to packages in the repository. For more information about the GITHUB_TOKEN , see Use GITHUB_TOKEN for authentication in workflows . For more information about the best practices when using a registry in actions, see Compromised runners . You can also choose to give access permissions to packages independently for GitHub Codespaces and GitHub Actions. For more information, see Configuring a package's access control and visibility and Configuring a package's access control and visibility . Authenticating with a personal access token (classic) Note GitHub Packages only supports authentication using a personal access token (classic). For more information, see Managing your personal access tokens . Create a new personal access token (classic) with the appropriate scopes for the tasks you want to accomplish. If your organization requires SSO, you must enable SSO for your new token. Note By default, when you select the write:packages scope for your personal access token (classic) in the user interface, the repo scope will also be selected. The repo scope offers unnecessary and broad access, which we recommend you avoid using for GitHub Actions workflows in particular. For more information, see Compromised runners . As a workaround, you can select just the write:packages scope for your personal access token (classic) in the user interface with this url: https://github.com/settings/tokens/new?scopes=write:packages . Select the read:packages scope to download container images and read their metadata. Select the write:packages scope to download and upload container images and read and write their metadata. Select the delete:packages scope to delete container images. For more information, see Managing your personal access tokens . Save your personal access token (classic). We recommend saving your token as an environment variable. export CR_PAT=YOUR_TOKEN Using the CLI for your container type, sign in to the Container registry service at ghcr.io . $ echo $CR_PAT | docker login ghcr.io -u USERNAME --password-stdin > Login Succeeded Pushing container images This example pushes the latest version of IMAGE_NAME . docker push ghcr.io/NAMESPACE/IMAGE_NAME:latest Replace NAMESPACE with the name of the personal account or organization to which you want the image to be scoped. This example pushes the 2.5 version of the image. docker push ghcr.io/NAMESPACE/IMAGE_NAME:2.5 When you first publish a package, the default visibility is private. To change the visibility or set access permissions, see Configuring a package's access control and visibility . You can link a published package to a repository using the user interface or command line. For more information, see Connecting a repository to a package . When you push a container image from the command line, the image is not linked to a repository by default. This is the case even if you tag the image with a namespace that matches the name of the repository, such as ghcr.io/octocat/my-repo:latest . The easiest way to conne

To publish new gems, you need to authenticate to GitHub Packages with RubyGems by editing your ~/.gem/credentials file to include your personal access token (classic). Create a new ~/.gem/credentials file if this file doesn't exist. For example, you would create or edit a ~/.gem/credentials to include the following, replacing TOKEN with your personal access token. --- :github: Bearer TOKEN To install gems, you need to authenticate to GitHub Packages by updating your gem sources to include https://USERNAME:TOKEN@rubygems.pkg.github.com/NAMESPACE/ . To change the visibility or set access permissions, see Configuring a package's access control and visibility . For more information on creating your gem, see Make your own gem in the RubyGems documentation. Note If you publish a package that is linked to a repository, the package automatically inherits the access permissions of the linked repository, and GitHub Actions workflows in the linked repository automatically get access to the package, unless your organization has disabled automatic inheritance of access permissions. For more information, see Configuring a package's access control and visibility . Authenticate to GitHub Packages. For more information, see Authenticating to GitHub Packages . Build the package from the gemspec to create the .gem package. Replace GEM_NAME with the name of your gem. gem build GEM_NAME.gemspec Publish a package to GitHub Packages, replacing NAMESPACE with the name of the personal account or organization to which the package will be scoped and GEM_NAME with the name of your gem package.
