search_index.content: SSO gerenciado · Hugging Face Hub documentation SSO gerenciado Hub 🏡 View all docs AWS Trainium & Inferentia Accelerate Bitsandbytes CLI Chat UI Dataset viewer Datasets Deploying on AWS Diffusers Google Cloud Google TPUs Gradio Hub Hub Python Library Huggingface.js Inference Endpoints (dedicated) Inference Providers Kernels LeRobot Leaderboards Lighteval Microsoft Azure OpenEnv Optimum PEFT Reachy Mini Safetensors Sentence Transformers TRL Tasks Text Embeddings Inference Tokenizers Trackio Transformers Transformers.js Xet smolagents timm Search documentation AR EN ES FR ID JA KO PT RU TR VI ZH API docs Join the Hugging Face community and get access to the augmented documentation experience Collaborate on models, datasets and Spaces Faster examples with accelerated inference Switch between documentation themes Sign Up to get started Copy page SSO gerenciado Este recurso faz parte do plano Enterprise Plus . O SSO gerenciado substitui completamente o login do Hugging Face . Seu Provedor de Identidade se torna o único método de autenticação para os membros da sua organização em toda a plataforma do Hugging Face. A organização controla todo o ciclo de vida do usuário, desde a criação da conta até a desativação. Para uma comparação com o SSO básico, consulte a visão geral do SSO . Como funciona O SSO gerenciado substitui o login do Hugging Face. Seu IdP é a única forma de os usuários gerenciados se autenticarem no Hugging Face — não há um login separado do Hugging Face. Diferentemente do SSO Básico, os membros não precisam de uma conta pré-existente no Hugging Face. Quando um usuário se autentica pela primeira vez por meio do seu IdP, uma conta é criada automaticamente para ele. Seu IdP é a rota de autenticação obrigatória para todos os membros da sua organização que interagem com qualquer parte da plataforma Hugging Face. Os membros são obrigados a autenticar-se por meio do seu IdP para todos os serviços do Hugging Face, não apenas ao acessar repositórios privados ou organizacionais. Quando um usuário é desativado no seu IdP, a conta do Hugging Face dele também é desativada. Isso dá à sua organização controle total sobre identidade, acesso e governança de dados. Começando O SSO gerenciado não pode ser configurado de forma autônoma. Para habilitar o SSO gerenciado para a sua organização, por favor, entre em contato com a equipe da Hugging Face . A configuração é realizada em colaboração com a nossa equipe técnica para garantir uma transição tranquila para a sua organização. Se você está convertendo uma organização existente, leia primeiro Migrating to Managed SSO : as contas pessoais existentes dos membros não são convertidas, e cada membro deve liberar seu e-mail de trabalho antes de poder ser provisionado. Os protocolos SAML 2.0 e OIDC são suportados e podem ser integrados a provedores de identidade populares, como Okta, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) e Google Workspace. Provisionamento de usuários O SSO gerenciado introduz o provisionamento automatizado de usuários por meio do SCIM , que gerencia todo o ciclo de vida do usuário no Hugging Face. O SCIM permite que seu IdP comunique informações de identidade de usuário ao Hugging Face, habilitando a criação automática, atualizações (por exemplo, alterações de nome, alterações de papel) e desativação de contas de usuário conforme as mudanças ocorrem em seu IdP. Saiba mais sobre como configurar e gerenciar o SCIM em nosso guia dedicado . Recursos de SSO O SSO gerenciado oferece suporte a mapeamento de funções, mapeamento de grupos de recursos, tempo limite de sessão e colaboradores externos . Esses recursos são configuráveis nas configurações da sua organização. Restrições em contas gerenciadas Considerações importantes para contas gerenciadas. Para garantir o controle organizacional e a governança de dados, as contas de usuário gerenciadas possuem restrições específicas: Sem criação de conteúdo pessoal : usuários gerenciados não podem criar nenhum conteúdo (modelos, conjuntos de dados ou Spaces) no namespace de usuário pessoal. Todo o conteúdo deve ser criado dentro da organização. Colaboração vinculada à organização : usuários gerenciados são restritos a colaborar exclusivamente dentro da organização que os gerencia. Eles não podem se juntar a outras organizações nem contribuir para repositórios fora da organização que os gerencia. Visibilidade do conteúdo : O conteúdo criado por usuários gerenciados fica dentro da organização. Embora os usuários gerenciados não possam criar conteúdo público em seu perfil pessoal, eles podem criar conteúdo público dentro da organização se as configurações da organização permitirem. Perfil gerenciado pela organização : A organização gerenciadora é definida automaticamente como a organização principal do usuário gerenciado. Usuários gerenciados não podem editar seu perfil (nome, avatar, organização principal, página inicial, biografia, links sociais), alterar seu nome de usuário ou senha, sair da organização ou excluir sua conta. Esses itens são controlados pela organização e por seu provedor de identidade. Essas restrições mantêm as fronteiras de segurança da sua empresa. Para projetos pessoais ou colaboração mais ampla fora da sua organização, os membros devem usar uma conta separada e não gerenciada do Hugging Face. Managed SSO는 Hugging Face 로그인을 완전히 대체합니다 . Identity Provider가 Hugging Face 플랫폼 전체에서 조직 구성원의 유일한 인증 수단이 됩니다. 조직은 계정 생성부터 비활성화까지 사용자 수명 주기를 전체적으로 관리합니다. Basic SSO와의 비교를 보려면 SSO 개요 를 참조하세요. 작동 방식 Managed SSO는 Hugging Face 로그인을 대체합니다. 관리 대상 사용자의 경우 Hugging Face에서 인증하는 유일한 방법은 IdP입니다. 별도의 Hugging Face 로그인이 없습니다. Basic SSO와 달리, 멤버는 기존 Hugging Face 계정이 필요하지 않습니다. 사용자가 IdP를 통해 처음 인증하면 계정이 자동으로 생성됩니다. IdP는 Hugging Face 플랫폼의 모든 부분에 상호작용하는 조직의 모든 구성원에게 필수적인 인증 경로입니다. 구성원은 개인 또는 조직 저장소에 액세스할 때뿐만 아니라 모든 Hugging Face 서비스를 사용할 때 IdP를 통해 인증해야 합니다. 사용자가 IdP에서 비활성화되면 Hugging Face 계정 역시 비활성화됩니다. 이를 통해 조직은 신원, 액세스 및 데이터 거버넌스에 대한 완전한 제어권을 가질 수 있습니다. 시작하기 Managed SSO는 자체 설정할 수 없습니다. 조직에 Managed SSO를 활성화하려면 Hugging Face 팀에 문의 해 주세요. 설정은 기술 팀과 협력하여 진행되며, 조직의 원활한 전환을 보장합니다. 기존 조직을 전환하는 경우, 먼저 Managed SSO로 마이그레이션 을 읽어보세요. 멤버의 기존 개인 계정은 전환되지 않으며, 각 멤버는 프로비저닝되기 전에 업무용 이메일 주소를 해제해야 합니다. SAML 2.0과 OIDC 프로토콜 모두 지원되며, Okta, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), Google Workspace와 같은 인기 있는 ID 제공업체와 통합할 수 있습니다. 사용자 프로비저닝 Managed SSO는 SCIM 을 통해 자동화된 사용자 프로비저닝을 도입하여 Hugging Face에서 사용자 수명 주기의 전 과정을 관리합니다. SCIM은 IdP가 사용자 신원 정보를 Hugging Face에 전달할 수 있게 하여, IdP에서 변경 사항이 발생하면 사용자 계정의 자동 생성, 업데이트(예: 이름 변경, 역할 변경), 비활성화를 가능하게 합니다. SCIM 설정 및 관리 방법에 대한 자세한 내용은 전용 가이드 에서 확인하세요. SSO 기능 Managed SSO는 역할 매핑, 리소스 그룹 매핑, 세션 타임아웃, 외부 협업자 를 지원합니다. 이러한 기능은 조직 설정에서 구성할 수 있습니다. 관리 계정 제한 관리 계정 사용 시 중요한 고려 사항 조직의 통제 및 데이터 거버넌스를 보장하기 위해, 관리되는 사용자 계정에는 다음과 같은 특정 제한 사항이 적용됩니다: 개인 콘텐츠 생성 불가 : 관리 대상 사용자는 개인 사용자 네임스페이스에서 어떤 콘텐츠(모델, 데이터셋, Spaces)도 생성할 수 없습니다. 모든 콘텐츠는 조직 내에서 생성해야 합니다. 조직 기반 협업 : 관리 대상 사용자는 해당 사용자를 관리하는 조직 내에서만 협업할 수 있습니다. 다른 조직에 가입하거나 관리 조직 외부의 저장소에 기여할 수 없습니다. 콘텐츠 가시성 : 관리 대상 사용자가 생성한 콘텐츠는 조직 내에 저장됩니다. 관리 대상 사용자는 개인 프로필에 공개 콘텐츠를 생성할 수 없지만, 조직 설정이 허용하는 경우 조직 내에서 공개 콘텐츠를 생성할 수 있습니다 . 조직 관리 프로필 : 관리 조직은 관리 대상 사용자의 기본 조직으로 자동 설정됩니다. 관리 대상 사용자는 프로필(이름, 아바타, 기본 조직, 홈페이지, 자기소개, 소셜 링크)을 편집하거나 사용자 이름 또는 비밀번호를 변경하거나 조직을 탈퇴하거나 계정을 삭제할 수 없습니다. 이러한 항목은 조직과 해당 ID 제공자가 관리합니다. 이러한 제한 사항은 기업의 보안 경계를 유지합니다. 개인 프로젝트나 조직 외부의 더 넓은 협력이 필요한 경우, 멤버는 별도 관리되지 않는 Hugging Face 계정을 사용해야 합니다. Yönetilen SSO, Hugging Face oturum açma işlemini tamamen değiştirir . Kimlik Sağlayıcınız, Hugging Face platformunun tamamında organizasyonunuzun üyeleri için tek kimlik doğrulama yöntemi haline gelir. Organizasyon, hesap oluşturmaktan devre dışı bırakmaya kadar tüm kullanıcı yaşam döngüsünü kontrol eder. Basic SSO ile karşılaştırma için SSO genel bakışına bakın. Nasıl çalışır Yönetilen SSO, Hugging Face oturum açma işlevinin yerini alır. Yönetilen kullanıcıların Hugging Face üzerinde kimlik doğrulaması yapmasının tek yolu IdP'nizdir — ayrı bir Hugging Face oturum açma işlemi yoktur. Basic SSO'dan farklı olarak, üyelerin önceden mevcut bir Hugging Face hesabına sahip olmaları gerekmez. Bir kullanıcı IdP'niz üzerinden ilk kez kimlik doğrulaması yaptığında, onlar için bir hesap otomatik olarak oluşturulur. IdP'niz, Hugging Face platformunun herhangi bir bölümüyle etkileşime giren organizasyonunuzdaki tüm üyeler için zorunlu kimlik doğrulama yoludur. Üyeler, yalnızca özel veya kurumsal depolara erişirken değil, tüm Hugging Face hizmetleri için IdP'niz üzerinden kimlik doğrulaması yapmakla yükümlüdür. Kullanıcı IdP'nizde devre dışı bırakıldığında, Hugging Face hesabı da devre dışı bırakılır. Bu, kuruluşunuza kimlik, erişim ve veri yönetişimi üzerinde tam kontrol sağlar. Başlangıç Yönetilen SSO öz yapılandırma ile yapılamaz. Kuruluşunuz için Yönetilen SSO'yu etkinleştirmek için lütfen Hugging Face ekibiyle iletişime geçin . Kurulum, kuruluşunuz için sorunsuz bir geçiş sağlamak amacıyla teknik ekibimizle iş birliği içinde gerçekleştirilir. Mevcut bir kuruluşu dönüştürüyorsanız, önce Yönetilen SSO'ya Geçiş başlığını okuyun: üyelerin mevcut kişisel hesapları dönüştürülmez ve her üye, sağlama işlemi yapılabilecek kadar iş e-posta adresini boşaltmalıdır. Hem SAML 2.0 hem de OIDC protokolleri desteklenir ve Okta, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) ve Google Workspace gibi popüler kimlik sağlayıcılarıyla entegre edilebilir. Kullanıcı sağlama Managed SSO, SCIM aracılığıyla otomatik kullanıcı sağlama (provisioning) sunar ve bu, Hugging Face üzerindeki tüm kullanıcı yaşam döngüsünü yönetir. SCIM, IdP'nizin kullanıcı kimlik bilgilerini Hugging Face ile paylaşmasını sağlayarak, IdP'nizde değişiklikler oldukça kullanıcı hesaplarının otomatik olarak oluşturulmasına, güncellenmesine (ör. ad değişiklikleri, rol değişiklikleri) ve devre dışı bırakılmasına olanak tanır. SCIM'in nasıl kurulacağı ve yönetileceği hakkında daha fazla bilgi için özel rehberimize göz atın. SSO özellikleri Yönetilen SSO, rol eşleme, kaynak grubu eşleme, oturum zaman aşımı ve harici işbirlikçileri özelliklerini destekler. Bu özellikler, organizasyonunuzun ayarlarından yapılandırılabilir. Yönetilen hesaplara kısıtlamalar Yönetilen hesaplar için önemli hususlar. Kurumsal kontrol ve veri yönetişimini sağlamak için, yönetilen kullanıcı hesapları belirli kısıtlamalara tabidir: Kişisel içerik oluşturma yok : Yönetilen kullanıcılar, kişisel kullanıcı ad alanlarında herhangi bir içerik (model, veri seti veya Spaces) oluşturamaz. Tüm içerik, kuruluş içinde oluşturulmalıdır. Organizasyona bağlı iş birliği : Yönetilen kullanıcılar, yalnızca kendilerini yöneten organizasyon içinde iş birliği yapabilir. Diğer organizasyonlara katılamazlar veya yöneten organizasyonlarının dışındaki depolara katkıda bulunamazlar. İçerik görünürlüğü : Yönetilen kullanıcılar tarafından oluşturulan içerik, organizasyonun içinde kalır. Yönetilen kullanıcılar kişisel profillerinde herkese açık içerik oluşturamaz; ancak organizasyon ayarları buna izin veriyorsa organizasyon içinde herkese açık içerik oluşturabilirler . Organizasyon tarafından yönetilen profil : Yöneten organizasyon, yönetilen kullanıcının birincil organizasyonu olarak otomatik olarak ayarlanır. Yönetilen kullanıcılar profillerini (ad, avatar, birincil organizasyon, ana sayfa, biyografi, sosyal bağlantılar) düzenleyemez, kullanıcı adlarını veya şifrelerini değiştiremez, organizasyondan ayrılamaz veya hesaplarını silemez. Bunlar organizasyon ve kimlik sağlayıcısı tarafından kontrol edilir. Bu kısıtlamalar, kuruluşunuzun güvenlik sınırlarını korur. Kişisel projeler veya kuruluşunuz dışındaki daha geniş iş birlikleri için, üyelerin ayrı, yönetilmeyen bir Hugging Face hesabı kullanması gerekir. Publisher Analytics Dashboard Track all your repository activity with a detailed downloads overview that shows total downloads for all the Models and Datasets published by your organization. Toggle between “All Time” and “Last Month” views to gain insights across your repositories over different periods. Per-repo breakdown Explore the metrics of individual repositories with the per-repository drill-down table. Utilize the built-in search feature to quickly locate specific repositories. Each row also features a time-series graph that illustrates the trend of downloads over time. Export Publisher Analytics as CSV Download a comprehensive CSV file containing analytics for all your repositories, including model and dataset download activity. You can also access this data programmatically via the following API endpoint: Copied curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \ "https://huggingface.co/organizations/YOUR_ORG_NAME/settings/publisher-analytics/download-breakdown" \ --output breakdown.csv Response Structure The CSV file is made of daily download records for each of your models and datasets. Copied repoType ,repoName,total,timestamp,downloads model ,huggingface/CodeBERTa-small-v1, 4362460 , 2021 - 01 - 22 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 4 model ,huggingface/CodeBERTa-small-v1, 4362460 , 2021 - 01 - 23 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 7 model ,huggingface/CodeBERTa-small-v1, 4362460 , 2021 - 01 - 24 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 2 dataset ,huggingface/documentation-images, 2167284 , 2021 - 11 - 27 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 3 dataset ,huggingface/documentation-images, 2167284 , 2021 - 11 - 28 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 18 dataset ,huggingface/documentation-images, 2167284 , 2021 - 11 - 29 T00: 00 : 00 . 000 Z, 7 Repository Object Structure Each record in the CSV contains: repoType : The type of repository (e.g., “model”, “dataset”) repoName : Full repository name including organization (e.g., “huggingface/documentation-images”) total : Cumulative number of downloads for this repository timestamp : ISO 8601 formatted date (UTC) downloads : Number of downloads for that day Records are ordered chronologically and provide a daily granular view of download activity for each repository. Download figures are not deduplicated by user. If you need unique download counts, refer to the next section. Advanced Publisher Analytics: unique downloaders and more granular logs This feature is an add-on for the Enterprise Plus plan. As an advanced feature, Hugging Face can export anonymized, request-level access logs for all of the models and datasets published by your organization. Each line represents a single download-related request, giving you full granularity over your models and datasets’ download data. Your team is responsible for ingesting these logs and running computations on them. The export intentionally includes raw HTTP status codes and methods so you can classify HEAD , partial-content, redirect, and other request patterns based on your own analytics needs. Column Description timestamp Request timestamp status HTTP status code (for example 200 , 206 , 302 , 307 , 304 ) method HTTP method (for example GET , HEAD ) repoName Full repo name (e.g. nvidia/segformer-b0 ) repoType Repository type: model , dataset , or space hashedUserId Non-reversible hash of user ID (if authenticated) hashedIp Non-reversible hash of IP address (if unauthenticated) country Country ISO code region Region or city name userAgent HTTP User-Agent header As it requires setting up a custom data export pipeline on our side (custom Elastic index, etc), this is only available as an add-on to Enterprise Plus. Tokens Management enables organization administrators to oversee access tokens within their organization, ensuring secure access to organization resources. For the member experience when token management policies are in effect — including how to check token status, what errors to expect, and how denial and revocation affect a token — see Tokens in organizations with token management policies . Viewing and Managing Access Tokens The token listing feature displays all access tokens within your organization. Administrators can: Monitor token usage and identify or prevent potential security risks: Unauthorized access to private resources (“leaks”) Overly broad access scopes Suboptimal token hygiene (e.g., tokens that have not been rotated in a long time) Identify inactive or unused tokens Fine-grained tokens display their specific permissions: Revoked tokens are hidden from the listing by default. Use the Show revoked tokens toggle above the list to include them in the view. A REVOKED status badge is shown for any revoked token regardless of the organization’s token policy. PENDING , APPROVED , and DENIED badges only appear in organizations with the “Require administrator approval” policy enabled, as those states are only created by the approval flow. Token Policy Team & Enterprise organization administrators can enforce the following policies: Policy Unscoped (Read/Write) Access Tokens Fine-Grained Tokens Allow access via User Access Tokens (default) Authorized Authorized Only access via fine-grained tokens Unauthorized Authorized Require administrator approval Unauthorized Unauthorized without an approval (except for admin-created) Reviewing Token Authorization When token policy is set to “Require administrator approval”, organization administrators can review details of all fine-grained tokens accessing organization-owned resources and approve or deny access. When a new token enters the pending state, up to 50 organization administrators with confirmed email addresses receive a notification with a direct link to the token review page. No notification is sent when a token is auto-approved (e.g., because the creator is an org admin). Pending tokens are awaiting an administrator decision Approved tokens have been authorized and are active Denied tokens have been blocked from accessing organization resources When a token is approved or denied, the token owner receives an email notification. Denial is not permanent: a denied token can later be approved by an administrator, restoring its access. Likewise, an already-approved token can be denied at any time, which removes its approval-based access immediately. Token names are only visible to administrators when the “Require administrator approval” policy is enabled. What Members See When Blocked Members whose tokens are pending or denied receive a 403 error when accessing organization resources: “Due to the organization token policy, your token needs to be approved by the organization before you can access this resource.” The error message is the same for both pending and denied states. To see the status, members can navigate to the individual token’s edit page. The organization administrator token management settings page shows status badges for all member tokens. Deny vs. Revoke Administrators have two ways to remove a token’s access to an organization: Aspect Deny Revoke Plan Team & Enterprise Enterprise plan and above Scope Operates within the approval workflow Independent of the token policy Effect Blocks or removes approval-based access Forcefully removes access regardless of policy or token state Reversible? Yes — a denied token can later be approved No — revoked status persists even if the policy changes Token elsewhere No effect outside the org No effect outside the org Use deny when managing access within the approval workflow (the token transitions to a denied state and can be re-approved later). Use revoke when you need to permanently cut off a token’s access to the organization. Listing Tokens via API The token listing shown in the settings UI is also available programmatically: Copied # ORG_NAME should be your organization name and ADMIN_HF_TOKEN an admin's access token curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_HF_TOKEN} " \ "https://huggingface.co/api/organizations/ ${ORG_NAME} /settings/tokens" The response is an array of member access tokens. See the OpenAPI reference for the full schema: GET /api/organizations/<name>/settings/tokens By default, revoked tokens are hidden; pass q=status:all to include them, like the Show revoked tokens toggle in the UI. Revoking Tokens This feature is part of the Enterprise plan and above. Organization administrators can revoke any member’s access token from the token detail page. Revocation is available regardless of whether the organization uses the “Require administrator approval” policy. A revoked token can no longer access the organization’s resources, but continues to work elsewhere. The token owner receives an email notification upon revocation. Revoked tokens remain rev

Resource Groups allow organizations to enforce fine-grained access control to their repositories. This feature allows organization administrators to: Group related repositories together for better organization Control member access at a group level rather than individual repository level Assign different permission roles (no_access, read, contributor, write, admin, inherit) to team members Keep private repositories visible only to authorized group members Enable multiple teams to work independently within the same organization Configure which member roles are allowed to create new resource groups Share resource groups and their repositories with external collaborators Restrict organization features such as Blog, Collections, Jobs, Inference Endpoints and Inference Providers to the members of specific resource groups Attribute costs to specific resource groups for better budget management Cap monthly compute spend per resource group, in total or per product This Team & Enterprise feature helps organizations manage complex team structures and maintain proper access control over their repositories. inference Switch between documentation themes Sign Up to get started Copy page SSO المُدار تُعد هذه الميزة جزءًا من خطة Enterprise Plus . يستبدل SSO المُدار تسجيل الدخول إلى Hugging Face بالكامل . يصبح مزوّد الهوية الخاص بك وسيلة المصادقة الوحيدة لأعضاء مؤسستك عبر منصة Hugging Face بأكملها. تتحكم المؤسسة في دورة حياة المستخدم الكاملة، بدءًا من إنشاء الحساب وصولاً إلى تعطيله. لمقارنة مع SSO الأساسي، راجع نظرة عامة على SSO . كيف يعمل يستبدل تسجيل الدخول الموحّد المُدار (Managed SSO) تسجيل الدخول إلى Hugging Face. يُعد مزوّد الهوية الخاص بك الطريقة الوحيدة للمستخدمين المُدارين للتحقق من هويتهم على Hugging Face — فلا يوجد تسجيل دخول منفصل إلى Hugging Face. وعلى عكس تسجيل الدخول الموحّد الأساسي (Basic SSO)، لا يحتاج الأعضاء إلى حساب Hugging Face قائم مسبقًا. عند قيام مستخدم بالتحقق من هويته عبر مزوّد الهوية الخاص بك لأول مرة، يتم إنشاء حساب له تلقائيًا. يُعد مزوّد الهوية الخاص بك (IdP) مسار المصادقة الإلزامي لجميع أعضاء مؤسستك عند التفاعل مع أي جزء من منصة Hugging Face. يجب على الأعضاء المصادقة عبر مزوّد الهوية الخاص بك لجميع خدمات Hugging Face، وليس فقط عند الوصول إلى المستودعات الخاصة أو المستودعات المؤسسية. عند تعطيل مستخدم في مزوّد الهوية الخاص بك، يتم تعطيل حسابه على Hugging Face أيضًا. ومنح ذلك مؤسستك سيطرة كاملة على الهوية والوصول وإدارة البيانات. البدء لا يمكن إعداد SSO المُدار ذاتيًا. لتفعيل SSO المُدار لمنظمتك، يرجى التواصل مع فريق Hugging Face . يتم الإعداد بالتعاون مع فريقنا التقني لضمان انتقال سلس لمنظمتك. إذا كنت تقوم بتحويل منظمة قائمة، اقرأ الانتقال إلى SSO المُدار أولاً: لا يتم تحويل الحسابات الشخصية الحالية للأعضاء، ويجب على كل عضو تحرير بريده الإلكتروني للعمل قبل أن يتم تفعيل حسابه. تُؤمَّن بروتوكولا SAML 2.0 وOIDC، ويمكن دمجهما مع مزودي الهوية الشائعين مثل Okta وMicrosoft Entra ID (Azure AD) وGoogle Workspace. تجهيز المستخدمين يُقدّم SSO المُدار آليةً آليةً لإعداد المستخدمين عبر SCIM ، الذي يُدير دورة حياة المستخدم الكاملة على Hugging Face. يتيح SCIM لمزوّد الهوية الخاص بك (IdP) إرسال معلومات هوية المستخدم إلى Hugging Face، مما يُتيح إنشاء الحسابات تلقائيًا وتحديثها (مثل تغيير الاسم أو تغيير الدور) وتعطيلها عند حدوث أي تغييرات في مزوّد الهوية الخاص بك. تعرف على المزيد حول كيفية إعداد وإدارة SCIM في دليلنا المخصص . ميزات تسجيل الدخول الأحادي يدعم SSO المُدار تعيين الأدوار، وتعيين مجموعات الموارد، ونهاية صلاحية الجلسة، والمشاركين الخارجيين . يمكن تكوين هذه الميزات من إعدادات مؤسستك. قيود على الحسابات المُدارة اعتبارات مهمة للحسابات المُدارة. لضمان التحكم التنظيمي والحوكمة البيانات، تخضع حسابات المستخدمين المُدارة لقيود محددة: لا إنشاء محتوى شخصي : لا يمكن للمستخدمين المُدارين إنشاء أي محتوى (نماذج، مجموعات بيانات، أو مساحات) في مساحة المستخدم الشخصية الخاصة بهم. يجب إنشاء جميع المحتوى ضمن المنظمة. التعاون المرتبط بالمنظمة : يُقيَّد المستخدمون المُدارون بالتعاون حصريًا داخل المنظمة المُديرة لهم. ولا يمكنهم الانضمام إلى منظمات أخرى أو المساهمة في مستودعات خارج المنظمة المُديرة لهم. رؤية المحتوى : المحتوى الذي ينشئه المستخدمون المُدارون يظل داخل المنظمة. وعلى الرغم من أن المستخدمين المُدارين لا يمكنهم إنشاء محتوى عام في ملفهم الشخصي، إلا أنهم يمكنهم إنشاء محتوى عام داخل المنظمة إذا سمحت إعدادات المنظمة بذلك. الملف الشخصي المُدار من قبل المنظمة : يتم تعيين المنظمة المُديرة تلقائيًا كمنظمة أساسية للمستخدم المُدار. لا يمكن للمستخدمين المُدارين تعديل ملفهم الشخصي (الاسم، الصورة الرمزية، المنظمة الأساسية، الصفحة الرئيسية، السيرة الذاتية، الروابط الاجتماعية)، أو تغيير اسم المستخدم أو كلمة المرور، أو مغادرة المنظمة، أو حذف حسابهم. يتم التحكم في هذه العناصر من قبل المنظمة ومزوّد الهوية الخاص بها. تُحافظ هذه القيود على حدود الأمان الخاصة بمؤسستك. أما بالنسبة للمشاريع الشخصية أو التعاون الأوسع خارج مؤسستك، فيجب على الأعضاء استخدام حساب منفصل وغير مُدار على Hugging Face. Regions allow you to specify where your organization’s models, datasets, Spaces, and buckets are stored. For non-Team or Enterprise users, repositories are always stored in the US. This offers two key benefits: Regulatory and legal compliance Performance (faster download/upload speeds and lower latency) Currently available regions: US 🇺🇸 EU 🇪🇺 Coming soon: Asia-Pacific 🌏 Coming soon: GCC (KSA) 🇸🇦 Getting started with Storage Regions Organizations subscribed to a Team or Enterprise plan can access the Regions settings page to manage their repositories storage locations. This page displays: An audit of your organization’s repository locations Options to select where new repositories will be stored Some advanced compute options for Spaces, such as ZeroGPU, may not be available in all regions. Repository Tag Any repository (model or dataset) stored in a non-default location displays its Region as a tag, allowing organization members to quickly identify repository locations. Regulatory and legal compliance Regulated industries often require data storage in specific regions. For EU companies, you can use the Hub for ML development in a GDPR-compliant manner, with datasets, models, buckets and inference endpoints all stored in EU data centers. Performance Storing models and datasets closer to your team and infrastructure significantly improves performance for both uploads and downloads. This impact is substantial given the typically large size of model weights and dataset files. For example, European users storing repositories in the EU region can expect approximately 4-5x faster upload and download speeds compared to US storage. Spaces Both Spaces’s storage and runtime use the chosen region. Available hardware configurations vary by region, and some features may not be available in all regions. Contact your HF account team for specific requests. Update on GitHub ← Audit Logs Data Studio for Private datasets →

search_index.content: Spaces ZeroGPU: Dynamic GPU Allocation for Spaces · Hugging Face Hub documentation Spaces ZeroGPU: Dynamic GPU Allocation for Spaces Hub 🏡 View all docs AWS Trainium & Inferentia Accelerate Bitsandbytes CLI Chat UI Dataset viewer Datasets Deploying on AWS Diffusers Google Cloud Google TPUs Gradio Hub Hub Python Library Huggingface.js Inference Endpoints (dedicated) Inference Providers Kernels LeRobot Leaderboards Lighteval Microsoft Azure OpenEnv Optimum PEFT Reachy Mini Safetensors Sentence Transformers TRL Tasks Text Embeddings Inference Tokenizers Trackio Transformers Transformers.js Xet smolagents timm Search documentation AR EN ES FR ID JA KO PT RU TR VI ZH API docs Join the Hugging Face community and get access to the augmented documentation experience Collaborate on models, datasets and Spaces Faster examples with accelerated inference Switch between documentation themes Sign Up to get started Copy page Spaces ZeroGPU: Dynamic GPU Allocation for Spaces ZeroGPU is a shared infrastructure that optimizes GPU usage for AI models and demos on Hugging Face Spaces. It dynamically allocates and releases NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell GPUs as needed, offering: Free GPU Access : Enables cost-effective GPU usage for Spaces. Multi-GPU Support : Allows Spaces to leverage multiple GPUs concurrently on a single application. Unlike traditional single-GPU allocations, ZeroGPU’s efficient system lowers barriers for developers, researchers, and organizations to deploy AI models by maximizing resource utilization and power efficiency. Using and hosting ZeroGPU Spaces Using existing ZeroGPU Spaces ZeroGPU Spaces are available to use for free to all users. (Visit the curated list ). PRO users get x8 more daily usage quota, highest priority in GPU queues, and can go beyond their daily quota using pre-paid credits when using any ZeroGPU Spaces. Hosting your own ZeroGPU Spaces Free personal accounts: accounts in good standing (verified email, account older than 30 days) can host up to 2 ZeroGPU Spaces for free. PRO accounts: Subscribe to PRO to host up to 10 ZeroGPU Spaces under your account. Organizations: Subscribe to a Team or Enterprise plan to enable ZeroGPU Spaces for all organization members. Technical Specifications ZeroGPU supports two GPU sizes GPU size Backing hardware Vram Quota cost large (default) Half NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell 48GB 1× xlarge Full NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell 96GB 2× See GPU size selection to learn how to use sizes Compatibility ZeroGPU Spaces are designed to be compatible with most PyTorch-based GPU Spaces. While compatibility is enhanced for high-level Hugging Face libraries like transformers and diffusers , users should be aware that: Currently, ZeroGPU Spaces are exclusively compatible with the Gradio SDK . ZeroGPU Spaces may have limited compatibility compared to standard GPU Spaces. Unexpected issues may arise in some scenarios. Supported Versions Gradio : 4+ PyTorch : Almost all versions from 2.8.0 to latest are supported See full list 2.8.0 2.9.1 2.10.0 2.11.0 2.12.1 2.13.0 Python : 3.12.12 3.10.13 Getting started with ZeroGPU To utilize ZeroGPU in your Space, follow these steps: Make sure the ZeroGPU hardware is selected in your Space settings. Import the spaces module. Decorate GPU-dependent functions with @spaces.GPU . This decoration process allows the Space to request a GPU when the function is called and release it upon completion. The @spaces.GPU decorator is designed to be effect-free in non-ZeroGPU environments, ensuring compatibility across different setups. Example Usage Copied import spaces from diffusers import DiffusionPipeline pipe = DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(...) pipe.to( 'cuda' ) @spaces.GPU def generate ( prompt ): return pipe(prompt).images gr.Interface( fn=generate, inputs=gr.Text(), outputs=gr.Gallery(), ).launch() Model loading Even though a real GPU is only available inside @spaces.GPU functions, models must be placed on cuda at the root module level (as shown in the example above). Lazy-loading or moving models to CUDA inside @spaces.GPU is discouraged, as it is significantly less efficient (CUDA transfers are optimized for placements done during startup). Loading models on cuda at module level works because a PyTorch CUDA emulation mode is enabled outside @spaces.GPU functions, allowing CUDA operations without a real GPU. Inside @spaces.GPU , real CUDA is used. GPU size selection The default size used by @spaces.GPU is large (half NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell). You can explicitly request a full NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell by specifying size="xlarge" : Copied @spaces.GPU( size= "xlarge" ) def generate ( prompt ): return pipe(prompt).images xlarge consumes 2× more daily quota than large (e.g. a 45s effective task duration consumes 90s of quota) xlarge usually means higher queuing probability and longer wait times Only use xlarge when your workload truly benefits from the additional compute or memory Duration Management For functions expected to exceed the default 60-second of GPU runtime, you can specify a custom duration: Copied @spaces.GPU( duration= 120 ) def generate ( prompt ): return pipe(prompt).images This sets the maximum function runtime to 120 seconds. Specifying shorter durations for quicker functions will improve queue priority for Space visitors. Dynamic duration @spaces.GPU also supports dynamic durations. Instead of directly passing a duration, simply pass a callable that takes the same inputs as your decorated function and returns a duration value: Copied def get_duration ( prompt, steps ): step_duration = 3.75 return steps * step_duration @spaces.GPU( duration=get_duration ) def generate ( prompt, steps ): return pipe(prompt, num_inference_steps=steps).images Compilation ZeroGPU does not support torch.compile , but you can use PyTorch ahead-of-time compilation (requires torch 2.8+ ) Check out this blogpost for a complete guide on ahead-of-time compilation on ZeroGPU. You can even request a free upgrade if you are building a cool demo for a side project! Longer-term, we would also like to expose non-GPU hardware, like HPU, IPU or TPU. If you have a specific AI hardware you’d like to run on, please let us know (website at huggingface.co). As soon as your Space is running on GPU you can see which hardware it’s running on directly from this badge: Hardware Specs In the following tables, you can see the Specs for the different upgrade options. CPU Hardware CPU Memory GPU Memory Disk Hourly Price CPU Basic 2 vCPU 16 GB - 50 GB Free! CPU Upgrade 8 vCPU 32 GB - 50 GB $0.03 CPU Basic has no hourly cost, but creating a new Space that runs on compute (Gradio or Docker) requires a paid plan. Static Spaces are free for everyone. See the Spaces Overview for details. GPU Hardware CPU Memory GPU Memory Disk Hourly Price Nvidia T4 - small 4 vCPU 15 GB 16 GB 50 GB $0.40 Nvidia T4 - medium 8 vCPU 30 GB 16 GB 100 GB $0.60 1x Nvidia L4 8 vCPU 30 GB 24 GB 400 GB $0.80 4x Nvidia L4 48 vCPU 186 GB 96 GB 3200 GB $3.80 1x Nvidia L40S 8 vCPU 62 GB 48 GB 380 GB $1.80 4x Nvidia L40S 48 vCPU 382 GB 192 GB 3200 GB $8.30 8x Nvidia L40S 192 vCPU 1534 GB 384 GB 6500 GB $23.50 1x Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 23 vCPU 256 GB 96 GB 475 GB $2.75 2x Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 46 vCPU 512 GB 192 GB 950 GB $5.50 4x Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 92 vCPU 1024 GB 384 GB 1900 GB $11.00 8x Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 184 vCPU 2048 GB 768 GB 3800 GB $22.00 Nvidia A10G - small 4 vCPU 15 GB 24 GB 110 GB $1.00 Nvidia A10G - large 12 vCPU 46 GB 24 GB 200 GB $1.50 2x Nvidia A10G - large 24 vCPU 92 GB 48 GB 1000 GB $3.00 4x Nvidia A10G - large 48 vCPU 184 GB 96 GB 2000 GB $5.00 Nvidia A100 - large 12 vCPU 142 GB 80 GB 1000 GB $2.50 Nvidia H100 (removed December 2025) 8x Nvidia H100 (removed December 2025) 4x Nvidia A100 48 vCPU 568 GB 320 GB 4000 GB $10.00 8x Nvidia A100 96 vCPU 1136 GB 640 GB 8000 GB $20.00 Configure hardware programmatically You can programmatically configure your Space hardware using huggingface_hub . This allows for a wide range of use cases where you need to dynamically assign GPUs. Check out this guide for more details. Framework specific requirements Most Spaces should run out of the box after a GPU upgrade, but sometimes you’ll need to install CUDA versions of the machine learning frameworks you use. Please, follow this guide to ensure your Space takes advantage of the improved hardware. PyTorch You’ll need to install a version of PyTorch compatible with the built-in CUDA drivers. Adding the following two lines to your requirements.txt file should work: Copied --extra-index-url https: // download.pytorch.org /whl/ cu113 torch You can verify whether the installation was successful by running the following code in your app.py and checking the output in your Space logs: Copied import torch print ( f"Is CUDA available: {torch.cuda.is_available()} " ) # True print ( f"CUDA device: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(torch.cuda.current_device())} " ) # Tesla T4 Many frameworks automatically use the GPU if one is available. This is the case for the Pipelines in 🤗 transformers , fastai and many others. In other cases, or if you use PyTorch directly, you may need to move your models and data to the GPU to ensure computation is done on the accelerator and not on the CPU. You can use PyTorch’s .to() syntax, for example: Copied model = load_pytorch_model() model = model.to( "cuda" ) JAX If you use JAX, you need to specify the URL that contains CUDA compatible packages. Please, add the following lines to your requirements.txt file: Copied -f https: // storage.googleapis.com /jax-releases/ jax_cuda_releases.html jax[cuda11_pip] jaxlib After that, you can verify the installation by printing the output from the following code and checking it in your Space logs. Copied import jax print ( f"JAX devices: {jax.devices()} " ) # JAX devices: [StreamExecutorGpuDevice(id=0, process_index=0)] print ( f"JAX device type: {jax.devices()[ 0 ].device_kind} " ) # JAX device type: Tesla T4 TensorFlow The default tensorflow installation should recognize the CUDA device. Just add tensorflow to your requirements.txt file and use the following code in your app.py to verify in your Space logs. Copied import tensorflow as tf print (tf.config.list_physical_devices( 'GPU' )) # [PhysicalDevice(name='/physical_device:GPU:0', device_type='GPU')] Billing Billing on Spaces is based on hardware usage and is computed by the minute: you get charged for every minute the Space runs on the requested hardware, regardless of whether the Space is used. During a Space’s lifecycle, it is only billed when the Space is Starting or Running . This means that there is no cost during build. If a running Space starts to fail, it will be automatically suspended and the billing will stop. Los registros de auditoría permiten a los administradores de la organización revisar fácilmente las acciones realizadas por los miembros, que incluyen la membresía de la organización, la configuración de los repositorios y los cambios de facturación. Acceso a los registros de auditoría Los registros de auditoría son accesibles a través de la configuración de tu organización. Cada entrada de registro incluye: Quién realizó la acción Qué tipo de acción se tomó Una descripción del cambio Ubicación y dirección IP anonimizada Fecha y hora de la acción También puede descargar el registro de auditoría completo como un archivo JSON para un análisis más detallado. Exportar mediante API La exportación programática está disponible en: Copiado GET https: // huggingface.co /api/ organizations /{org}/ audit-log/export Autentíquese con un token de acceso de usuario o un token de cuenta de servicio que tenga el permiso Export the audit log ( org.auditLog.write ) para la organización. La respuesta es un array JSON de entradas de registro, idéntico al archivo descargado desde la página de configuración. Al igual que la exportación manual, la llamada a la API se registra como org.audit_log.export . El punto de acceso también está documentado en la referencia de OpenAPI . Qué eventos se rastrean Cada acción tiene un nombre de evento en el formato scope.action (por ejemplo, repo.create , collection.delete ). Este es el campo type en cada entrada de registro y en el JSON exportado; úsalo al buscar o filtrar registros. Gestión y seguridad de la organización Los eventos de cambios en la configuración que se indican a continuación solo están disponibles para las acciones realizadas después del 16 de junio de 2026. Los eventos anteriores a esa fecha utilizan un tipo de evento único org.update_settings . Cualquier integración que filtre o analice el campo type del evento para las organizaciones creadas antes del 16 de junio de 2026 debe manejar ambos. Core organization changes — Creación, eliminación, restauración y cambio de nombre. Eventos: org.create , org.delete , org.restore , org.rename Settings changes — Las actualizaciones de la configuración de la organización se registran como eventos granulares org.settings.* , por lo que puedes identificar exactamente qué configuración se modificó. Configuración general: perfil, regiones de almacenamiento, grupos de recursos y control de editores. Eventos: org.settings.profile , org.settings.regions , org.settings.resource_groups , org.settings.publisher_gating Proveedores de inferencia — Configuración del proveedor, adición/eliminación de claves API y ajustes de uso. Eventos: org.settings.inference_providers , org.settings.inference_providers.keys.add , org.settings.inference_providers.keys.remove , org.settings.inference_providers.usage SSO — Actualizaciones de la configuración de SSO, y activación o desactivación de SSO. Eventos: org.settings.sso , org.settings.sso.enable , org.settings.sso.disable Seguridad — Visibilidad predeterminada del repositorio, y activación o desactivación de la aplicación de 2FA, la incorporación automática y la privacidad de los miembros. Eventos: org.settings.security.repo_visibility , org.settings.security.2fa.enable , org.settings.security.2fa.disable , org.settings.security.auto_join.enable , org.settings.security.auto_join.disable , org.settings.security.members_privacy.enable , org.settings.security.members_privacy.disable Red — Actualizaciones de la configuración de red, y activación o desactivación de la restricción de acceso IP y la aplicación de la autenticación. Eventos: org.settings.network , org.settings.network.ip_restriction.enable , org.settings.network.ip_restriction.disable , org.settings.network.auth_enforcement.enable , org.settings.network.auth_enforcement.disable Security management Rotación de tokens de API de organización. Evento: org.rotate_token Sistema de aprobación de tokens — Activación o desactivación de la política, solicitudes de autorización, aprobaciones, denegaciones y revocaciones. Eventos: org.token_approval.enabled , org.token_approval.disabled , org.token_approval.authorization_request , org.token_approval.authorization_request.authorized , org.token_approval.authorization_request.revoked , org.token_approval.authorization_request.denied SSO — Inicios de sesión y altas a través de SSO, y miembros que autorizan o desautorizan sus tokens de acceso y claves SSH. Eventos: org.sso_login , org.sso_join , org.sso_credential.authorize , org.sso_credential.deauthorize Join settings — Acceso basado en dominio y configuración de incorporación automática. Evento: org.update_join_settings Membresía y control de acceso Member lifecycle — Agregar y eliminar miembros, cambios de rol y miembros que abandonan la organización. Eventos: org.add_user , org.remove_user , org.change_role , org.leave Account type — Convertir a un miembro en un colaborador externo , o volver a convertirlo en miembro. Evento: org.change_account_type Invitations — Envío de invitaciones, enlaces de invitación

Estas guías te ayudan a configurar SAML 2.0 y OpenID Connect (OIDC) con tu proveedor de identidad para SSO básico . Hugging Face Hub puede funcionar con cualquier proveedor de identidad compatible con SAML o OIDC. Si desea configurar Managed SSO , la configuración se realiza en colaboración con el equipo de Hugging Face. Por favor, contáctenos para comenzar. Método de autenticación del punto final de token de OIDC. Al intercambiar el código de autorización, Hugging Face se autentica en el punto final de token de su proveedor de identidad mediante el método client_secret_post . Si la aplicación de su IdP está configurada para esperar un método diferente (como client_secret_basic ), el inicio de sesión fallará con un error de invalid_client . Para resolverlo, configure el método de autenticación del punto final de token de la aplicación de su IdP como client_secret_post . search_index.content: SSO básico · Hugging Face Hub documentation SSO básico Hub 🏡 View all docs AWS Trainium & Inferentia Accelerate Bitsandbytes CLI Chat UI Dataset viewer Datasets Deploying on AWS Diffusers Google Cloud Google TPUs Gradio Hub Hub Python Library Huggingface.js Inference Endpoints (dedicated) Inference Providers Kernels LeRobot Leaderboards Lighteval Microsoft Azure OpenEnv Optimum PEFT Reachy Mini Safetensors Sentence Transformers TRL Tasks Text Embeddings Inference Tokenizers Trackio Transformers Transformers.js Xet smolagents timm Search documentation AR EN ES FR ID JA KO PT RU TR VI ZH API docs Join the Hugging Face community and get access to the augmented documentation experience Collaborate on models, datasets and Spaces Faster examples with accelerated inference Switch between documentation themes Sign Up to get started Copy page SSO básico Esta función forma parte de los planes Team & Enterprise . El SSO básico añade una capa de control de acceso sobre el inicio de sesión estándar de Hugging Face. Permite aplicar la autenticación a través de su proveedor de identidad (IdP) cuando los miembros acceden a recursos bajo el espacio de nombres de su organización, como modelos privados, conjuntos de datos y Spaces. Para una comparación con Managed SSO, consulte el resumen de SSO . Cómo funciona El SSO básico no reemplaza el inicio de sesión de Hugging Face. Sus miembros aún deberán iniciar sesión en Hugging Face con sus propias credenciales (correo electrónico/contraseña, Google o GitHub) antes de que se les solicite completar la autenticación SSO para acceder a los recursos de su organización. Esto es por diseño: el SSO básico protege el acceso a su organización sin tomar el control de la identidad de Hugging Face del usuario. Cuando el inicio de sesión único está habilitado, los miembros de la organización se autentican a través de su proveedor de identidad (IdP). Usted elige si el SSO es obligatorio o opcional : Obligatorio (predeterminado): Los miembros deben completar la autenticación SSO antes de acceder a cualquier elemento del espacio de nombres de la organización. Opcional : Los miembros reciben un aviso mediante un banner en la parte superior de la página para configurar SSO, pero pueden omitirlo y seguir accediendo a la organización. Esto es útil cuando se está migrando a muchos usuarios y se desea darles tiempo para organizar sus cuentas antes de aplicar SSO de forma obligatoria. El contenido público sigue siendo accesible para todos, incluidos los no miembros. Utilizamos las direcciones de correo electrónico para identificar a los usuarios de SSO. Como usuario, asegúrate de que tu dirección de correo electrónico organizativa (p. ej., el correo de tu empresa) haya sido añadida a tu cuenta de usuario . Cuando los usuarios inician sesión, se les solicitará completar el flujo de autenticación de Single Sign-On con un banner similar al siguiente: El inicio de sesión único solo se aplica a tu organización. Los miembros pueden pertenecer a otras organizaciones en Hugging Face. Primeros pasos La SSO básica se puede configurar directamente desde la configuración de su organización. Hugging Face Hub puede funcionar con cualquier proveedor de identidad compatible con OIDC o SAML, incluidos Okta, OneLogin y Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD). Consulte nuestras Guías de configuración para obtener instrucciones de configuración paso a paso. Provisionamiento de usuarios Una vez que SSO está habilitado en tu organización, se puede copiar y compartir un enlace de incorporación directo con nuevos miembros. Este enlace de incorporación SSO está disponible en las pestañas de configuración SSO y Members . Dado que las organizaciones con SSO habilitado no pueden usar enlaces de invitación clásicos, el enlace de incorporación SSO es el método principal para invitar a compañeros de equipo a tu organización. Simplemente haz clic en el botón de copiar para copiar el enlace en tu portapapeles y compártelo con los miembros que desees invitar. Cuando los destinatarios hagan clic en el enlace compartido, podrán autenticarse mediante SSO e incorporarse directamente a tu organización. Las organizaciones con el plan Enterprise también pueden usar SCIM para automatizar el aprovisionamiento basado en invitaciones desde su proveedor de identidad. Consulte la guía de SCIM para obtener más detalles. Tokens de acceso y claves SSH Para usar un User Access Token o una SSH key con una organización que aplica SSO, primero debes autorizarlo para esa organización. Hasta que lo hagas, las solicitudes realizadas con él a los recursos de la organización se rechazarán, incluidas las de Git sobre SSH. El acceso a tus otros recursos no se ve afectado. Para autorizar un token o una clave SSH: Ve a Access Tokens o SSH and GPG Keys en tu configuración. Abra el menú junto al token o la clave y haga clic en Configurar SSO . Haz clic en Authorize junto a la organización. Se te redirigirá a tu proveedor de identidad para iniciar sesión. Los tokens que creas mientras inicias sesión en la organización con SSO se autorizan automáticamente para ella. Una autorización dura hasta que la desautorices desde el mismo menú o salgas de la organización. Si vuelves a unirte, autoriza de nuevo tus tokens y claves. Los colaboradores externos no necesitan autorizar sus credenciales. Los administradores de la organización pueden ver las autorizaciones y desautorizaciones en los registros de auditoría . Funciones de SSO El SSO básico admite el mapeo de roles, el mapeo de grupos de recursos, el tiempo de espera de la sesión, el dominio de correo electrónico coincidente y los colaboradores externos . Estas funciones se pueden configurar desde la configuración de tu organización. Update on GitHub ← Inicio de sesión único (SSO) SSO administrado →

El SSO gestionado sustituye por completo el inicio de sesión de Hugging Face . Tu proveedor de identidad se convierte en el único método de autenticación para los miembros de tu organización en toda la plataforma de Hugging Face. La organización controla el ciclo de vida completo del usuario, desde la creación de la cuenta hasta su desactivación. Para una comparación con SSO básico, consulte el resumen de SSO . Cómo funciona El SSO gestionado reemplaza el inicio de sesión de Hugging Face. Tu IdP es la única forma en que los usuarios gestionados pueden autenticarse en Hugging Face; no existe un inicio de sesión separado de Hugging Face. A diferencia del SSO básico, los miembros no necesitan una cuenta de Hugging Face preexistente. Cuando un usuario se autentica a través de tu IdP por primera vez, se crea automáticamente una cuenta para él. Su IdP es la ruta de autenticación obligatoria para todos los miembros de su organización que interactúen con cualquier parte de la plataforma de Hugging Face. Los miembros deben autenticarse a través de su IdP para todos los servicios de Hugging Face, no solo al acceder a repositorios privados u organizacionales. Cuando un usuario se desactiva en su IdP, su cuenta de Hugging Face también se desactiva. Esto le otorga a su organización un control completo sobre la identidad, el acceso y la gobernanza de datos. Primeros pasos El SSO gestionado no se puede configurar de forma autónoma. Para habilitar el SSO gestionado en su organización, por favor contacte al equipo de Hugging Face . La configuración se realiza en colaboración con nuestro equipo técnico para garantizar una transición fluida para su organización. Si estás convirtiendo una organización existente, lee primero Migrating to Managed SSO : las cuentas personales existentes de los miembros no se convierten, y cada miembro debe liberar su correo electrónico de trabajo antes de que pueda ser aprovisionado. Se admiten los protocolos SAML 2.0 y OIDC, y pueden integrarse con proveedores de identidad populares como Okta, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) y Google Workspace. Provisionamiento de usuarios Managed SSO introduce la aprovisionamiento automatizado de usuarios a través de SCIM , que gestiona todo el ciclo de vida del usuario en Hugging Face. SCIM permite que tu IdP comunique la información de identidad de usuario a Hugging Face, habilitando la creación automática, las actualizaciones (p. ej., cambios de nombre, cambios de rol) y la desactivación de las cuentas de usuario a medida que ocurren cambios en tu IdP. Obtén más información sobre cómo configurar y gestionar SCIM en nuestra guía dedicada . Funciones de SSO El SSO administrado admite mapeo de roles, mapeo de grupos de recursos, tiempo de espera de sesión y colaboradores externos . Estas funciones son configurables desde la configuración de tu organización. Restricciones en las cuentas administradas Consideraciones importantes para las cuentas administradas. Para garantizar el control organizativo y la gobernanza de datos, las cuentas de usuario administradas tienen restricciones específicas: No creación de contenido personal : Los usuarios gestionados no pueden crear ningún contenido (modelos, conjuntos de datos o Spaces) en su espacio de nombres de usuario personal. Todo el contenido debe crearse dentro de la organización. Colaboración vinculada a la organización : Los usuarios gestionados están restringidos a colaborar únicamente dentro de su organización administradora. No pueden unirse a otras organizaciones ni contribuir a repositorios fuera de su organización administradora. Visibilidad del contenido : El contenido creado por usuarios gestionados reside dentro de la organización. Si bien los usuarios gestionados no pueden crear contenido público en su perfil personal, sí pueden crear contenido público dentro de la organización si la configuración de la organización lo permite. Perfil gestionado por la organización : La organización administradora se establece automáticamente como la organización principal del usuario gestionado. Los usuarios gestionados no pueden editar su perfil (nombre, avatar, organización principal, página web, biografía, enlaces sociales), cambiar su nombre de usuario o contraseña, abandonar la organización ni eliminar su cuenta. Estos elementos están controlados por la organización y su proveedor de identidad. Estas restricciones mantienen los límites de seguridad de su empresa. Para proyectos personales o para una colaboración más amplia fuera de su organización, los miembros deben utilizar una cuenta de Hugging Face separada y no gestionada. SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) es un estándar para automatizar la provisión de usuarios. Permite conectar tu Identity Provider (IdP) con Hugging Face para gestionar los miembros de tu organización. SCIM funciona de manera diferente según tu modelo de SSO. Para una comparación detallada, consulta el resumen de SSO . SSO básico: aprovisionamiento basado en invitaciones Con Basic SSO (plan Enterprise), SCIM automatiza la invitación de usuarios existentes de Hugging Face a su organización. Los usuarios deben tener ya una cuenta de Hugging Face antes de que puedan ser aprovisionados mediante SCIM Cuando su IdP aprovisiona un usuario, Hugging Face les envía un correo de invitación para unirse a la organización El usuario debe aceitar la invitación para convertirse en miembro: la aprovisionamiento no otorga acceso inmediato SCIM no puede modificar la información del perfil de usuario (nombre, correo electrónico, nombre de usuario): el usuario conserva el control total de su cuenta de Hugging Face Cuando un usuario se desprovisiona en su IdP, su invitación se desactiva y se revoca su acceso a la organización SSO administrado: aprovisionamiento del ciclo de vida completo Con Managed SSO (plan Enterprise Plus), SCIM gestiona el ciclo de vida completo del usuario en Hugging Face. SCIM crea una nueva cuenta de Hugging Face cuando se aprovisiona un usuario: no se necesita una cuenta preexistente El usuario se agrega de inmediato a la organización como miembro, sin paso de invitación SCIM puede actualizar la información del perfil de usuario (nombre, correo electrónico, nombre de usuario) a medida que se producen cambios en su IdP Cuando un usuario se desprovisiona en su IdP, su cuenta de Hugging Face se desactiva y se revoca su acceso Cómo habilitar SCIM Para habilitar SCIM, vaya a la configuración de su organización, navegue a la pestaña SSO y luego seleccione la subpestaña SCIM . Encontrará la SCIM Tenant URL y un botón para generar un SCIM token . Necesitará ambos para configurar su IdP. El token SCIM es un secreto y debe almacenarse de forma segura en la configuración de su IdP. Una vez que SCIM esté habilitado en tu IdP, los usuarios aprovisionados aparecerán en la pestaña Gestión de usuarios y los grupos aprovisionados aparecerán en la pestaña SCIM de la configuración de tu organización. Provisionamiento de grupos Además del aprovisionamiento de usuarios, SCIM admite el aprovisionamiento de grupos . Los grupos enviados desde su IdP se almacenan como grupos SCIM en Hugging Face y pueden vincularse a Resource Groups desde la pestaña SCIM en la configuración de su organización. Vincular un grupo de SCIM a un grupo de recursos Para vincular un grupo de SCIM, vaya a la pestaña SSO → SCIM de su organización. Los grupos aprovisionados se listan en una tabla. En la columna Resource Groups , cada grupo muestra un botón Link resource groups (si aún no existen vínculos) o el número de grupos de recursos vinculados actualmente (p. ej., “2 resource groups”). Al hacer clic en cualquiera de ellos se abre un modal donde puede agregar uno o más Resource Groups, cada uno con su propia asignación de roles. También puede cambiar o eliminar vínculos existentes desde el mismo modal. Antes de vincular, asegúrese de que se cumplan las siguientes condiciones: El Resource Group debe tener miembros existentes . No se permite vincular a un Resource Group que no esté vacío. El Resource Group no debe tener la opción de incorporación automática habilitada . La incorporación automática (que añade automáticamente a cada nuevo miembro de la organización al RG) es mutuamente excluyente con la gestión mediante SCIM. Desactive la incorporación automática en el RG antes de vincularlo. Un grupo SCIM puede vincularse a varios grupos de recursos, cada uno con su propio rol. Qué sucede después de vincular Una vez que un grupo SCIM se vincula a un grupo de recursos: Backfill : Cualquier miembro que ya esté en el grupo SCIM se añade inmediatamente al Resource Group con el rol configurado. Ongoing sync : Los cambios de membresía en su IdP se reflejan automáticamente: Cuando un usuario se agrega al grupo en su IdP, se agrega a todos los grupos de recursos vinculados. Cuando un usuario se elimina del grupo en su IdP, se elimina de todos los grupos de recursos vinculados, excepto aquellos a los que el usuario está vinculado a través de otros grupos SCIM. En esos casos, el rol del usuario se actualizará al rol “más alto” otorgado por los otros grupos SCIM. Cuando un grupo SCIM se elimina en su IdP, todos sus miembros se eliminan de los Resource Groups vinculados, excepto los usuarios que pertenecen a esos Resource Groups a través de otros grupos SCIM. Para cada uno de esos Resource Groups, los roles de los usuarios se actualizan al “más alto” rol otorgado por los otros grupos SCIM. Cambios de rol : Si actualizas el rol en un enlace, los roles de todos los miembros actuales del grupo en ese Resource Group se actualizan de inmediato. Grupos de recursos

Las siguientes funciones están disponibles para las organizaciones con SSO habilitado. Consulte SSO básico y SSO administrado para obtener detalles sobre cada modo. Tiempo de espera de la sesión Este valor establece la duración de la sesión para los miembros de su organización. Tras este tiempo, se solicitará a los miembros que vuelvan a autenticarse con su proveedor de identidad para acceder a los recursos de la organización. El valor predeterminado es de 7 días. Mapeo de roles Cuando está habilitado, Role Mapping te permite asignar dinámicamente roles a los miembros de la organización en función de los datos proporcionados por tu Identity Provider. Esta sección le permite definir un mapeo desde los datos del perfil de usuario de su IdP hasta el rol asignado en Hugging Face. Ruta del atributo de rol de IdP Una ruta JSON a un atributo en los datos del perfil de IdP de su usuario. Admite notación de puntos (p. ej. user.role o groups ). Para SAML, puede ser un URI (p. ej. http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/role ). Mapeo de roles Un mapeo del valor del atributo del IdP al rol asignado en la organización de Hugging Face. Los roles disponibles son admin , write , contributor y read . Consulte la documentación de roles para más detalles. Debes mapear al menos un rol admin en tu configuración. Si el atributo en la respuesta del IdP contiene varios valores (p. ej., una lista de grupos) que coinciden con varias asignaciones, al usuario se le asigna el rol coincidente con mayor privilegio . La jerarquía de roles, de menor a mayor privilegio, es read < contributor < write < admin . Si no hay coincidencia, el rol se determina de la siguiente manera: Si el usuario fue invitado a la organización con un rol específico, ese rol de invitación se utiliza como alternativa. En caso contrario, al usuario se le asigna el rol predeterminado de su organización. El rol predeterminado se puede personalizar en la sección Members de la configuración de la organización. Al invitar a un usuario cuyo rol será controlado por el mapeo de roles de SSO, el rol seleccionado en el modal de invitación solo se aplica si el usuario aún no tiene un rol asignado en su proveedor de SSO. La sincronización de roles se realiza en cada inicio de sesión. Mapeo de grupos de recursos Cuando está habilitado, Resource Group Mapping permite asignar dinámicamente miembros a grupos de recursos en su organización, basándose en los datos proporcionados por su proveedor de identidad. Ruta del atributo de IdP Una ruta JSON a un atributo en los datos del perfil de IdP de su usuario. Al igual que con el Role Mapping, esto admite la notación de puntos o URIs para SAML. Mapeo de grupos de recursos Un mapeo del valor del atributo del IdP a un grupo de recursos en su organización de Hugging Face. Puede asignar un rol específico ( admin , write , contributor , read , inherit ) para cada mapeo de grupo de recursos. A diferencia del Role Mapping, el Resource Group Mapping es aditivo . Si un usuario coincide con varios mapeos (por ejemplo, si pertenece a varios grupos en su IdP que están mapeados a diferentes Resource Groups), se le añadirá a todos los Resource Groups coincidentes. Si no hay coincidencia, el usuario no se asignará a ningún grupo de recursos. Los grupos de recursos a los que apunta una asignación aún pueden editarse manualmente desde la interfaz de usuario o la API de Hub, pero esas ediciones se sobrescriben en el próximo inicio de sesión SSO del usuario: un cambio de rol se revierte al rol asignado, y un usuario que fue eliminado manualmente se vuelve a añadir. Para cambiar de forma permanente el acceso de un usuario asignado, actualice los datos de su IdP o la configuración de la asignación. Dominios de correo electrónico coincidentes Esta función solo es relevante para Basic SSO . Con Managed SSO , las cuentas de usuario están totalmente gestionadas por la organización, por lo que la coincidencia de dominio de correo electrónico no se aplica. Cuando está habilitado, ‘Matching email domains’ solo permite a los miembros de la organización completar el SSO si el correo electrónico proporcionado por su proveedor de identidad coincide con uno de sus correos en Hugging Face. Para agregar un dominio de correo electrónico, complete el campo ‘Matching email domains’, presione enter en su teclado y guarde. Colaboradores externos Los colaboradores externos son usuarios fuera de tu organización que necesitan acceder a algunos de sus recursos sin pasar por el inicio de sesión único (SSO). Generalmente, esto significa que no están en tu proveedor de identidad (IdP). Están disponibles en los planes de pago y aparecen con la insignia “Colaborador externo” en las listas de miembros de tu organización. Sí cuentan hacia el número de asientos de pago de tu organización. Puedes agregarlos de la siguiente manera: Invitarlos a la organización : en la página Members de la configuración de su organización, marque External Collaborator al enviar la invitación. Convertir un miembro existente : en la página M

These guides help you configure SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) with your Identity Provider for Basic SSO . Hugging Face Hub can work with any SAML or OIDC-compliant Identity Provider. If you are looking to set up Managed SSO , the configuration is done in collaboration with the Hugging Face team. Please contact us to get started. OIDC token endpoint authentication method. When exchanging the authorization code, Hugging Face authenticates to your Identity Provider’s token endpoint using the client_secret_post method. If your IdP application is configured to expect a different method (such as client_secret_basic ), the login will fail with an invalid_client error. To resolve this, set your IdP application’s token endpoint authentication method to client_secret_post . Managed SSO replaces the Hugging Face login entirely . Your Identity Provider becomes the sole authentication method for your organization’s members across the entire Hugging Face platform. The organization controls the full user lifecycle, from account creation to deactivation. For a comparison with Basic SSO, see the SSO overview . How it works Managed SSO replaces the Hugging Face login. Your IdP is the only way for managed users to authenticate on Hugging Face — there is no separate Hugging Face login. Unlike Basic SSO, members do not need a pre-existing Hugging Face account. When a user authenticates through your IdP for the first time, an account is automatically created for them. Your IdP is the mandatory authentication route for all your organization’s members interacting with any part of the Hugging Face platform. Members are required to authenticate via your IdP for all Hugging Face services, not just when accessing private or organizational repositories. When a user is deactivated in your IdP, their Hugging Face account is deactivated as well. This gives your organization complete control over identity, access, and data governance. Getting started Managed SSO cannot be self-configured. To enable Managed SSO for your organization, please contact the Hugging Face team . The setup is done in collaboration with our technical team to ensure a smooth transition for your organization. If you are converting an existing organization, read Migrating to Managed SSO first: members’ existing personal accounts are not converted, and each member must free up their work email before they can be provisioned. Both SAML 2.0 and OIDC protocols are supported and can be integrated with popular identity providers such as Okta, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), and Google Workspace. User provisioning Managed SSO introduces automated user provisioning through SCIM , which manages the entire user lifecycle on Hugging Face. SCIM allows your IdP to communicate user identity information to Hugging Face, enabling automatic creation, updates (e.g., name changes, role changes), and deactivation of user accounts as changes occur in your IdP. Learn more about how to set up and manage SCIM in our dedicated guide . SSO features Managed SSO supports role mapping, resource group mapping, session timeout, and external collaborators . These features are configurable from your organization’s settings. Restrictions on managed accounts Important considerations for managed accounts. To ensure organizational control and data governance, managed user accounts have specific restrictions: No personal content creation : Managed users cannot create any content (models, datasets, or Spaces) in their personal user namespace. All content must be created within the organization. Organization-bound collaboration : Managed users are restricted to collaborating solely within their managing organization. They cannot join other organizations or contribute to repositories outside of their managing organization. Content visibility : Content created by managed users resides within the organization. While the managed users cannot create public content in their personal profile, they can create public content within the organization if the organization’s settings permit it. Organization-managed profile : The managing organization is automatically set as the managed user’s primary organization. Managed users can’t edit their profile (name, avatar, primary organization, homepage, bio, social links), change their username or password, leave the organization, or delete their account. These are controlled by the organization and its identity provider. These restrictions maintain your enterprise’s security boundaries. For personal projects or broader collaboration outside your organization, members should use a separate, unmanaged Hugging Face account. Update on GitHub ← Basic SSO Migrating to Managed SSO →

The following features are available to organizations with SSO enabled. See Basic SSO and Managed SSO for details on each mode. Session Timeout This value sets the duration of the session for members of your organization. After this time, members will be prompted to re-authenticate with your Identity Provider to access the organization’s resources. The default value is 7 days. Role Mapping When enabled, Role Mapping allows you to dynamically assign roles to organization members based on data provided by your Identity Provider. This section allows you to define a mapping from your IdP’s user profile data to the assigned role in Hugging Face. IdP Role Attribute Path A JSON path to an attribute in your user’s IdP profile data. It supports dot notation (e.g. user.role or groups ). For SAML, this can be a URI (e.g. http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/role ). Role Mapping A mapping from the IdP attribute value to the assigned role in the Hugging Face organization. Available roles are admin , write , contributor , and read . See roles documentation for more details. You must map at least one admin role in your configuration. If the attribute in the IdP response contains multiple values (e.g. a list of groups) that match several mappings, the user is assigned the most privileged matching role . The role hierarchy, from least to most privileged, is read < contributor < write < admin . If there is no match, the role is determined as follows: If the user was invited to the organization with a specific role, that invitation role is used as a fallback. Otherwise, the user is assigned the default role for your organization. The default role can be customized in the Members section of the organization’s settings. When inviting a user whose role will be controlled by SSO role mapping, the role selected in the invite modal only applies if the user does not yet have a role assigned in your SSO provider. Role synchronization is performed on every login. Resource Group Mapping When enabled, Resource Group Mapping allows you to dynamically assign members to resource groups in your organization, based on data provided by your Identity Provider. IdP Attribute Path A JSON path to an attribute in your user’s IdP profile data. Similar to Role Mapping, this supports dot notation or URIs for SAML. Resource Group Mapping A mapping from the IdP attribute value to a resource group in your Hugging Face organization. You can assign a specific role ( admin , write , contributor , read , inherit ) for each resource group mapping. Unlike Role Mapping, Resource Group Mapping is additive . If a user matches multiple mappings (e.g. they belong to multiple groups in your IdP that are mapped to different Resource Groups), they will be added to all matched Resource Groups. If there is no match, the user will not be assigned to any resource group. Resource groups targeted by a mapping can still be edited manually from the Hub UI or API, but those edits are overwritten at the user’s next SSO login: a role change is reverted to the mapped role, and a user who was manually removed is re-added. To change a mapped user’s access permanently, update your IdP data or the mapping configuration. Matching email domains This feature is only relevant for Basic SSO . With Managed SSO , user accounts are fully managed by the organization, so email domain matching does not apply. When enabled, ‘Matching email domains’ only allows organization members to complete SSO if the email provided by your identity provider matches one of their emails on Hugging Face. To add an email domain, fill out the ‘Matching email domains’ field, click enter on your keyboard, and save. External Collaborators External collaborators are users outside your organization who need access to some of its resources without going through Single Sign-On (SSO). That usually means they aren’t in your Identity Provider (IdP). They’re available on paid plans, and show up with an “External collaborator” badge in your organization’s member lists. They do count toward the number of paid seats in your organization. You can add them by: Inviting them to the organization : on the Members page of your organization’s settings, check External Collaborator when you send the invite. Converting an existing member : on the Members page, open the member’s menu and select Convert to external collaborator . Use Convert to member to switch them back. If your organization uses SSO, they’ll need to sign in through it afterward to keep access. You can also do this via the API . Sharing a resource group or repository : if external invitations are enabled, resource group admins can invite outsiders straight into a Resource Group, including from Share with external collaborators on a repository’s settings page. Those users join with the no_access organization role and only get that Resource Group. External collaborators still go through your organization’s access controls ( Resource Groups ). Audit Logs enable organization admins to easily review actions taken by members, including organization membership, repository settings and billing changes. Accessing Audit Logs Audit Logs are accessible through your organization settings. Each log entry includes: Who performed the action What type of action was taken A description of the change Location and anonymized IP address Date and time of the action You can also download the complete audit log as a JSON file for further analysis. Export via API Programmatic export is available at: Copied GET https: // huggingface.co /api/ organizations /{org}/ audit-log/export Authenticate with a user access token or service-account token that has the Export the audit log permission ( org.auditLog.write ) for the organization. The response is a JSON array of log entries, identical to the file downloaded from the settings page. Like the manual export, the API call is recorded as org.audit_log.export . The endpoint is also documented in the OpenAPI reference . What Events Are Tracked? Each action has an event name in scope.action format (e.g. repo.create , collection.delete ). This is the type field in each log entry and in the exported JSON—use it when searching or filtering logs. Basic SSO adds an access-control layer on top of the standard Hugging Face login. It allows you to enforce authentication through your Identity Provider (IdP) when members access resources under your organization’s namespace, such as private models, datasets, and Spaces. For a comparison with Managed SSO, see the SSO overview . How it works Basic SSO does not replace the Hugging Face login. Your members will still need to sign in to Hugging Face with their own credentials (email/password, Google, or GitHub) before being prompted to complete SSO authentication to access your organization’s resources. This is by design: Basic SSO secures access to your organization without taking over the user’s Hugging Face identity. When Single Sign-On is enabled, organization members authenticate through your Identity Provider (IdP). You pick whether SSO is enforced or optional : Enforced (default): Members have to complete SSO authentication before accessing anything under the organization’s namespace. Optional : Members get prompted via a banner at the top of the page to set up SSO, but can skip it and still access the organization. This is handy when you’re migrating a lot of users and want to give them time to sort out their accounts before definitely enforcing SSO. Public content is still accessible to everyone, including non-members. We use email addresses to identify SSO users. As a user, make sure that your organizational email address (e.g. your company email) has been added to your user account . When users log in, they will be prompted to complete the Single Sign-On authentication flow with a banner similar to the following: Single Sign-On only applies to your organization. Members may belong to other organizations on Hugging Face. Getting started Basic SSO can be configured directly from your organization’s settings. Hugging Face Hub can work with any OIDC-compliant or SAML Identity Provider, including Okta, OneLogin, and Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD). See our Configuration Guides for step-by-step setup instructions. User provisioning Once SSO is enabled on your organization, a direct join link can be copied and shared with new members. This SSO join link is available in both the SSO and Members settings tabs. Since organizations with SSO enabled cannot use classic invite links, the SSO join link is the primary method for inviting teammates to your organization. Simply click the copy button to copy the link to your clipboard and share it with the members you want to invite. When recipients click the shared link, they will be able to authenticate via SSO and directly join your organization. Organizations on the Enterprise plan can also use SCIM to automate invitation-based provisioning from your Identity Provider. See the SCIM guide for more details. Access tokens and SSH keys To use a User Access Token or an SSH key with an organization that enforces SSO, you first need to authorize it for that organization. Until then, requests made with it to the organization’s resources are rejected, Git over SSH included. Access to your other resources isn’t affected. To authorize a token or SSH key: Go to Access Tokens or SSH and GPG Keys in your settings. Open the menu next to the token or key and click Configure SSO . Click Authorize next to the organization. You’re redirected to your Identity Provider to sign in. Tokens you create while signed in to the organization with SSO are authorized for it automatically. An authorization lasts until you deauthorize it from the same menu or leave the organization. If you rejoin, authorize your tokens and keys again. External collaborators don’t need to authorize their credentials. Organization admins can see authorizations and deauthorizations in the audit logs . SSO features Basic SSO supports role mapping, resource group mapping, session timeout, matching email domains, and external collaborators . These features are configurable from your organization’s settings. Update on GitHub ← Single Sign-On (SSO) Managed SSO →
