SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) is a standard for automating user provisioning. It allows you to connect your Identity Provider (IdP) to Hugging Face to manage your organization’s members. SCIM works differently depending on your SSO model. For a detailed comparison, see the SSO overview . Basic SSO: invitation-based provisioning With Basic SSO (Enterprise plan), SCIM automates the invitation of existing Hugging Face users to your organization. Users must already have a Hugging Face account before they can be provisioned via SCIM When your IdP provisions a user, Hugging Face sends them an invitation email to join the organization The user must accept the invitation to become a member — provisioning does not grant immediate access SCIM cannot modify user profile information (name, email, username) — the user retains full control of their Hugging Face account When a user is deprovisioned in your IdP, their invitation is deactivated and their access to the organization is revoked Managed SSO: full lifecycle provisioning With Managed SSO (Enterprise Plus plan), SCIM manages the entire user lifecycle on Hugging Face. SCIM creates a new Hugging Face account when a user is provisioned — no pre-existing account is needed The user is immediately added to the organization as a member, with no invitation step SCIM can update user profile information (name, email, username) as changes occur in your IdP When a user is deprovisioned in your IdP, their Hugging Face account is deactivated and their access is revoked How to enable SCIM To enable SCIM, go to your organization’s settings, navigate to the SSO tab, and then select the SCIM sub-tab. You will find the SCIM Tenant URL and a button to generate a SCIM token . You will need both of these to configure your IdP. The SCIM token is a secret and should be stored securely in your IdP’s configuration. Once SCIM is enabled in your IdP, provisioned users will appear in the Users Management tab and provisioned groups will appear in the SCIM tab in your organization’s settings. Group provisioning In addition to user provisioning, SCIM supports group provisioning . Groups pushed from your IdP are stored as SCIM groups on Hugging Face and can be linked to Resource Groups from the SCIM tab in your organization’s settings. Linking a SCIM group to a Resource Group To link a SCIM group, go to your organization’s SSO → SCIM tab. Provisioned groups are listed in a table. In the Resource Groups column, each group shows either a Link resource groups button (if no links exist yet) or the number of currently linked resource groups (e.g. “2 resource groups”). Clicking either opens a modal where you can add one or more Resource Groups, each with its own role assignment. You can also change or remove existing links from the same modal. Before linking, make sure the following conditions are met: The Resource Group must have no existing members . Linking to a non-empty Resource Group is not allowed. The Resource Group must not have auto-join enabled . Auto-join (which automatically adds every new org member to the RG) is mutually exclusive with SCIM management. Disable auto-join on the RG before linking. A SCIM group can be linked to multiple Resource Groups, each with its own role. What happens after linking Once a SCIM group is linked to a Resource Group: Backfill : Any members already in the SCIM group are immediately added to the Resource Group at the configured role. Ongoing sync : Membership changes in your IdP are automatically reflected: When a user is added to the group in your IdP, they are added to all linked Resource Groups. When a user is removed from the group in your IdP, they are removed from all linked Resource Groups, except those the user is linked to through other SCIM groups. For those, the user’s role will be updated to the “highest” role granted by the other SCIM groups. When a SCIM group is deleted in your IdP, all its members are removed from the linked Resource Groups, except for users who belong to those Resource Groups through other SCIM groups. For each of those Resource Groups, users’ roles are updated to the “highest” role granted by the other SCIM groups. Role changes : If you update the role on a link, all current group members’ roles in that Resource Group are updated immediately, except for members whose role was changed manually . SCIM-managed Resource Groups A Resource Group linked to a SCIM group is considered SCIM-managed . The IdP is the source of truth for its membership. As a result: Adding or removing members manually via the Hub UI or API is blocked : any attempt returns a 403 error. Roles can still be changed per member. A manually changed role is kept when the role on the SCIM link is updated, and can be restored with Reset to SCIM role in the member’s actions (or resetToScimRole in the API). search_index.content: Medium The Person Who Truly Loves You Will Definitely Give You These 7 Things | by Hannah kim | No Time | Oct, 2026 | Medium Sitemap Open in app Sign up Sign in Get app Write Search Sign up Sign in No Time · A place to share stories about life, ideas, experiences, and the little things that matter. Member-only story Love Life Lessons Philosophy Of Mind Psychology No Time The Person Who Truly Loves You Will Definitely Give You These 7 Things How I Learned to Tell Real Love From Pretend Love: 7 Signs I Never Ignore Hannah kim 6 min read · Oct 17, 2026 -- 103 Listen Share Press enter or click to view image in full size Photo by Claudio Schwarz on Unsplash For non-medium member. Most of us have done it at least once. We make one person our whole world, while they quietly treat us as a habit, a deal or a way to pass the time. We call it love, but in reality it was only a show. That is why the hardest question is also the simplest one. How do you know whether the person you share your time, your feelings and your life with truly loves you, or is only getting through the days? I used to believe love meant big gestures, beautiful words and thoughtful gifts. Over time I learned that real love looks very different. A person who truly loves you gives you seven things that a pretender cannot keep up for long. And the seventh is so important that without it, the other six lose their meaning. The first is real attention. In this fast world, the most valuable things we own are our time and our focus. If someone sits beside you with their eyes glued to their phone, you are in the room, but you are not their priority. I know the quiet loneliness of talking to someone who is somewhere else. search_index.content: Preventing code quality issues from reaching your default branch - GitHub Docs Skip to main content Skip to content Collapse sidebar Expand sidebar In this article Preventing code quality issues from reaching your default branch Move through Code Quality findings on your pull request, including understanding severity labels, when each finding is best fixed, delegated, or dismissed, and how those choices shape your repository's code health. Copy markdown Who can use this feature? Users with write access GitHub Team or GitHub Enterprise Cloud In this article Up next Phase 3: Launch your pilot Introduction In this tutorial, you'll follow a single pull request through Code Quality's analysis, from first comment to merge. You'll learn: How to read the Code Quality comments on your pull request. How to use a finding's severity label to decide what to fix, what to dismiss, and in what order. How the choices you make on a pull request shape your repository's scores, backlog, and merge gates. By the end, you'll have resolved every blocking finding on the example pull request and merged it with a clean Code Quality check, and you'll understand why you made each choice. This is a guided walkthrough, so it favors understanding over speed. For basic steps on how to commit an autofix or dismiss a finding, see the companion how-to: Fixing code quality findings on a pull request . Before you start Code Quality is enabled on a repository you contribute to. See Enabling GitHub Code Quality . The repository uses a language supported by CodeQL so that rule-based findings and scores are generated. For a list of supported languages, see GitHub Code Quality . You have a pull request open against the default branch with at least one Code Quality finding to triage. If you don't have a pull request ready, you can follow the example below. Throughout this tutorial, we'll use a running example: a pull request that refactors some code will introduce several code quality issues into the default branch if it's merged as it is. A Code Quality scan has automatically run on the pull request and has reported several findings as comments. Why the pull request is the best place to fix a finding Every finding you don't resolve at the pull request stage becomes an action item in your repository's backlog, and technical debt is often more expensive to pay down later than to address now. Right now, while the pull request is open, the code's context and intent are still fresh in your mind, which makes each finding, and its autofix, faster to assess, apply, or confidently dismiss. Resolving findings at the pull request stage means your team spends less time triaging remediation work against feature work, and avoids the overhead of extra pull requests just to burn down a backlog. Step 1: Find the Code Quality comments on your pull request When you open a pull request, Code Quality uses CodeQL to scan your changes against a set of rules and posts findings as comments by github-code-quality[bot] . Each comment includes a suggested autofix. Open the Files changed tab of your pull request to review the findings. In our example, we'll look at three comments from github-code-quality[bot] . Note the severity labels on each. Step 2 explains what they mean. Step 2: Read the severity label to decide what matters Every finding from github-code-quality[bot] carries a severity label— Error , Warning , or Note . Find the label on one of the comments and check it against this table. Severity Definition Error Indicates a high-severity issue that is likely to cause bugs, failures, or major maintainability risks. Warning Indicates a moderate-severity issue that may impact code quality or reliability, but is not immediately critical. Note Indicates a low-severity issue, minor improvement, or recommendation. These findings are useful for ongoing code health and maintainability. The label is doing two jobs for you at once: It tells you what to fix first. Severity reflects the expected impact of a rule across typical code. In our example, you'd start with the Error , then the Warning , and treat the Note as optional polish. It may decide whether you can merge at all. A repository administrator or organization owner can configure Code Quality as a merge gate. For example, if the threshold for merging is "Warning and above", every Warning and Error -level finding must be fixed or dismissed before you can merge ( Note findings wouldn't prevent you from merging). Similarly, a stricter threshold may require you to resolve all findings before merge. To see whether a gate is in effect, scroll to the Checks section at the bottom of the pull request. If your changes fall below the required threshold, you'll see a merge block banner: "Merging is blocked: Code quality findings were detected." In our example the gate is set to "Warning and above", so the banner is present: the Error and the Warning are blocking the merge, and the Note is not. That tells you what you have to clear before this pull request can be merged. If the merge block banner doesn't specify a severity level, you must clear all findings in order to merge your pull request. Step 3: Resolve each finding For every finding, decide whether it applies to your code and, if it does, how to fix it. That leads you to one of three actions. Assessment Recommended action Notes The finding is legitimate and the suggested fix looks correct Apply the autofix suggestion Clicking Commit suggestion doesn't consume AI credits, and autofixes don't require a Copilot license. The finding is real but you want to fix several at once, or the suggested fix needs adapting Delegate to Copilot —mention @copilot in a comment to hand the work to the cloud agent. Copilot reacts with 👀, starts a new agent session, and pushes the necessary fixes to the pull request's branch Requires a Copilot license and consumes AI cred

Jetzt loslegen Häufig gestellte Fragen Wie viel kostet Code Quality? 10 USD pro Committer und Monat, zuzüglich einer nutzungsabhängigen Abrechnung für KI-gestützte Arbeiten. Deterministische CodeQL-Scans verbrauchen GitHub-Actions-Minuten. Für öffentliche Repositorys fallen keine Gebühren pro Committer an; die KI-gestützten Funktionen werden nutzungsabhängig abgerechnet. Welche Sprachen unterstützt Code Quality? Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, C# und Go. Brauche ich noch ein Tool für die Test-Abdeckung? Nein. Code Quality erstellt Abdeckungsberichte aus deinen vorhandenen Testtools im Cobertura-XML-Format und steuert dann die Merges anhand deiner Schwellenwerte über Regelsätze. Es analysiert deine Testabdeckung; es instrumentiert deine Tests nicht. Inwiefern unterscheidet sich das von GitHub Advanced Security? GitHub Advanced Security deckt den Bereich Sicherheit ab: Codesicherheit spürt Schwachstellen auf, und Secret Protection findet offengelegte Anmeldedaten. Code Quality umfasst Wartbarkeit, Zuverlässigkeit und Abdeckung. Diese beiden Bereiche ergänzen sich. In Qualitätsproblemen können sich Schwachstellen verbergen – sauberer Code bedeutet also, dass dein Sicherheitsteam weniger zu durchdenken hat. Code Quality und Codesicherheit laufen auf derselben CodeQL-Engine und beide werden in einer einzigen Übersicht zu Sicherheit und Qualität zusammengefasst. Funktioniert Code Quality mit der Copilot Code Review? Ja, als ineinander verwobene, aber dennoch eigenständige Erlebnisse. Die Code-Review-Funktion von Copilot gibt deinen Entwickler:innen während des Schreibens kontextbezogenes Feedback, und die Kommentare sind nur vorübergehend sichtbar. Code Quality liefert deinen Führungskräften dauerhafte Ergebnisse, durchsetzbare Kontrollpunkte und Berichte, die alle Repositorys und Zeiträume abdecken. Beides ist im Pull Request enthalten. Ist Code Quality ein Compliance-Produkt? Nein. Code Quality unterstützt die interne Governance und den Entwicklungs-Workflow. Es handelt sich nicht um eine Bescheinigung gemäß einer regulatorischen Anforderung oder einem Prüfungs-Framework. Kann ich die Qualität in meiner gesamten Organisation steuern? Ja, setze Code Quality organisationsweit um – mit Dashboards, Massenaktionen, APIs und Bewertungen auf Repository- und Organisationsebene. Wo kann mein Team lernen, wie man das einrichtet? Der Learning Pathway für Code Quality auf GitHub führt dich durch die Aktivierung von Prüfungen, das Festlegen von Regelsätzen, das Beheben von Fehlern mit Autofix und das Lesen der Dashboards. Lancez-vous Contacter le service commercial Restez dans le workflow GitHub Code Quality affiche les problèmes détectés directement dans les pull requests, évitant ainsi aux développeurs de devoir passer par un tableau de bord distinct. Corrigez les problèmes à mesure que vous révisez Chaque problème identifié inclut un correctif révisable que les développeurs peuvent appliquer avant le merge. Réduisez le backlog et livrez plus vite Consacrez moins de temps à trier les problèmes de qualité et davantage à examiner et livrer des correctifs. Une détection pensée pour le code à l’ère de l’IA L’analyse déterministe de CodeQL détecte ce que les règles savent traiter. La détection assistée par IA repère ce qui leur échappe. Ensemble, elles suivent le rythme d’un code que les équipes de développement génèrent plus vite qu’aucune bibliothèque de règles ne peut évoluer. Voir le fonctionnement de la détection Corriger à la source Vos équipes de développement n’ouvrent pas de tableau de bord. Elles ouvrent une pull request. Copilot Autofix suggère le correctif sur place. Elles l’examinent, le modifient ou l’ignorent. Rien ne merge tout seul. Découvrir Autofix Une norme unique, peu importe qui (ou quoi) écrit le code Les mêmes ensembles de règles encadrent le code écrit par les équipes de développement, les résultats renvoyés par la revue de code Copilot et les pull requests ouvertes par les agents de codage. Qualité et sécurité, un seul workflow. Voir le fonctionnement des ensembles de règles Code Quality La qualité dans la pull request, la gouvernance à l’échelle de l’organisation. $ 10 USD par committer / mois + utilisation Lancez-vous Contacter le service commercial Ce qui est inclus Détection hybride (CodeQL déterministe et détection assistée par IA) Autofix dans la pull request Contrôles qualité des ensembles de règles, seuils de couverture et protection au moment du merge Notation de la maintenabilité et de la fiabilité Ingestion de la couverture (Cobertura XML) Déploiement à l’échelle de l’organisation, tableaux de bord et API 10 USD par committer / mois, plus une facturation à l’usage pour les fonctionnalités d’IA et les minutes Actions. Référentiels publics : 0 USD par committer + facturation à l’usage pour les tâches alimentées par l’IA. Disponible sur GitHub Enterprise Cloud et GitHub Team. Lancez-vous Questions fréquentes Combien coûte Code Quality ? 10 USD par committer et par mois, plus une facturation à l’usage pour les tâches alimentées par l’IA. Les analyses déterministes CodeQL consomment des minutes GitHub Actions. Les référentiel publics n’entraînent aucun coût par committer, avec une facturation à l’usage pour les fonctionnalités alimentées par l’IA. Quels langages Code Quality prend-il en charge ? Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, C# et Go. Ai-je besoin d’un autre outil pour la couverture de test ? Non. Code Quality génère des rapports de couverture à partir de vos outils de test existants au format Cobertura XML, puis conditionne les merges au respect de vos seuils grâce aux ensembles de règles. L’outil lit votre couverture ; il n’instrumente pas vos tests. En quoi est-ce différent de GitHub Advanced Security ? GitHub Advanced Security couvre la sécurité : Code Security détecte les vulnérabilités, et Secret Protection détecte les identifiants exposés. Code Quality couvre la maintenabilité, la fiabilité et la couverture, et ces deux disciplines fonctionnent ensemble. Les problèmes de qualité sont souvent à l’origine des vulnérabilités : un code plus propre allège donc la charge de travail des équipes de sécurité. Code Quality et Code Security s’appuient sur le même moteur CodeQL, et les deux s’affichent dans une vue d’ensemble unique de la sécurité et de la qualité. Code Quality fonctionne-t-il avec la revue de code Copilot ? Oui, sous la forme d’expériences intégrées mais distinctes. La revue de code Copilot donne aux équipes de développement des retours contextuels pendant qu’elles rédigent le code, et ses commentaires sont éphémères. Code Quality fournit aux équipes de direction des résultats persistants, des contrôles applicables et des rapports couvrant l’ensemble des repos et des périodes. Les deux apparaissent dans la pull request. Code Quality est-il un produit de conformité ? Non. Code Quality prend en charge la gouvernance interne et le workflow de développeur. Il ne constitue pas une attestation de conformité à une norme réglementaire ou à un framework d’audit. Puis-je piloter la qualité à l’échelle de toute mon organisation ? Oui. Déployez Code Quality à l’échelle de l’organisation grâce aux tableaux de bord, aux actions groupées, aux API ainsi qu’à la notation au niveau des repos et de l’organisation. Où mon équipe peut-elle apprendre à le configurer ? Le parcours d’apprentissage GitHub Code Quality explique comment activer les vérifications, configurer les ensembles de règles, corriger les résultats avec Autofix et lire les tableaux de bord. AI 시대 코드를 위해 구축된 탐지 결정론적 CodeQL 분석은 규칙이 처리하는 부분을 포착하고, AI 지원 탐지는 규칙이 놓치는 부분을 포착합니다. 이 둘을 통해 어떤 규칙 라이브러리보다도 빠르게 개발자가 생성하는 코드의 속도를 따라잡을 수 있습니다. 탐지 작동 방식 보기 소스에서 수정 개발자는 대시보드를 열지 않고, pull request를 엽니다. Copilot Autofix가 바로 거기에서 수정 사항을 제안합니다. 개발자는 이를 검토, 편집 또는 무시합니다. 어떤 것도 자동으로 병합되지 않습니다. Autofix 살펴보기 누가 또는 무엇이 코드를 작성하든 상관없이 하나의 표준 적용 개발자가 작성하는 코드, Copilot 코드 검토에서 반환되는 결과, 코딩 에이전트가 여는 pull request에 모두 동일한 rulesets가 적용됩니다. 품질 및 보안, 하나의 워크플로. rulesets 작동 방식 보기 Code Quality pull request의 품질, 조직 전반의 거버넌스. $ 10 USD 커미터당/월 + 사용량 시작하기 영업팀에 문의 포함 내용 하이브리드 탐지(결정론적 CodeQL 및 AI 지원) pull request의 Autofix Rulesets 품질 제어, 커버리지 임곗값, 병합 보호 유지 관리 기능 및 안정성 평가 커버리지 수집(Cobertura XML) 조직 전체 배포, 대시보드 및 API 커미터당 월 10달러이며, AI 기능 및 Actions 시간에 대해 사용량에 따라 요금이 부과됩니다. 퍼블릭 리포지토리: 커미터당 0달러이며 AI 기반 작업에 대해 사용량에 따라 요금이 부과됩니다. GitHub Enterprise Cloud와 GitHub Team에서 이용 가능합니다. 시작하기 자주 묻는 질문 Code Quality 이용 요금은 얼마인가요? 커미터당 월 10달러이며, AI 기반 작업 사용량에 따라 요금이 부과됩니다. 결정론적 CodeQL 스캔은 GitHub Actions 시간을 사용합니다. 퍼블릭 리포지토리의 경우 커미터당 요금은 없으며, AI 기반 기능에 대해 사용량에 따라 요금이 부과됩니다. Code Quality는 어떤 언어를 지원하나요? Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, C#, Go를 지원합니다. 테스트 커버리지를 위해 다른 도구가 필요한가요? 아니요. Code Quality가 기존 테스트 도구의 커버리지 보고서를 Cobertura XML 형식으로 렌더링한 다음, rulesets를 통해 설정한 임곗값에 따라 병합을 제어합니다. 커버리지를 읽을 뿐 테스트를 계측하지는 않습니다. 이 기능은 GitHub Advanced Security와 어떻게 다른가요? GitHub Advanced Security는 보안을 다룹니다. Code Security가 취약점을 찾고 Secret Protection이 노출된 자격 증명을 찾습니다. Code Quality는 유지관리성, 안정성, 커버리지를 다루며, 이 두 영역은 서로 연동되어 작동합니다. 품질 문제는 취약점이 숨기 좋은 곳이므로 코드가 깔끔할수록 보안 팀이 추론해야 할 사항이 줄어듭니다. Code Quality와 Code Security는 동일한 CodeQL 엔진에서 실행되며 둘 다 하나의 보안 및 품질 개요를 통해 보고합니다. Code Quality가 Copilot 코드 검토와 연동되나요? 예, 통합되어 있으면서도 별개의 기능으로 작동합니다. Copilot 코드 검토는 개발자가 코드를 작성하는 동안 상황에 맞는 피드백을 제공하며 주석은 사용 후 삭제됩니다. Code Quality는 리더에게 지속적인 결과, 강제 적용 가능한 제어, 여러 리포지토리와 시간에 대한 보고서를 제공합니다. 둘 다 pull request에 표시됩니다. Code Quality는 규정 준수 제품인가요? 아니요. Code Quality는 내부 거버넌스와 개발자 워크플로를 지원합니다. 규제 표준이나 감사 프레임워크에 대한 증명이 아닙니다. 조직 전체의 품질을 관리할 수 있나요? 예. 대시보드, 대량 작업, API, 리포지토리 및 조직 수준의 평가와 함께 조직 전체에 Code Quality를 배포하세요. 어디에서 설정 방법을 확인할 수 있나요? GitHub Code Quality 학습 경로에서 검사 활성화, rulesets 설정, Autofix를 활용한 결과 수정, 대시보기 읽기 방법을 안내합니다. 학습 경로를 시작하세요 . You can’t perform that action at this time.

Dismiss alert {{ message }} GitHub Code Quality GitHub Code Quality GitHub Code Quality resalta los hallazgos en las pull requests con correcciones que puedes revisar antes de hacer el merge, y luego te ayuda a aplicar estándares consistentes con rulesets. Comienza Comunícate con Ventas Mantente en tu flujo de trabajo GitHub Code Quality muestra los hallazgos directamente en los pull requests, así que los desarrolladores no tienen que cambiar a otro panel. Corrige incidencias conforme revisas Cada hallazgo incluye una corrección que los desarrolladores pueden revisar y aplicar antes de hacer el merge. Reduce el backlog y lanza más rápido Dedica menos tiempo a clasificar incidencias de calidad y más a revisar y lanzar correcciones. Detección diseñada para código de la era de la IA El análisis determinista de CodeQL detecta lo que cubren las reglas. La detección asistida por IA detecta lo que estas no detectan. Juntas mantienen el ritmo del código que sus desarrolladores generan más rápido de lo que crece cualquier biblioteca de reglas. Descubra cómo funciona la detección Corrige el problema en el origen Tus desarrolladores no abren un panel. Abren una pull request. Copilot Autofix sugiere la corrección justo ahí. La revisan, la editan o la descartan. Nada se hace merge solo. Descubra Autofix Un único estándar, independientemente de quién o qué escriba el código Los mismos rulesets rigen el código que escriben sus desarrolladores, los resultados que devuelve la revisión del código de Copilot y las pull requests que abren sus agentes de programación. Calidad y seguridad, un único flujo de trabajo. Descubra cómo funcionan los rulesets Code Quality Calidad en la pull request y gobierno en toda la organización. $ 10 USD por autor de confirmaciones al mes + uso Comienza Comunícate con Ventas Qué incluye Detección híbrida (CodeQL determinista y asistencia de IA) Corrección automática en la pull request Controles de calidad de rulesets, umbrales de cobertura y protección de merges Puntuación de mantenibilidad y fiabilidad. Ingesta de cobertura (Cobertura XML) Implementación en toda la organización, paneles y API. 10°USD por autor de confirmaciones al mes, más la facturación según el uso de las funciones de IA y de los minutos de Actions. Repositorios públicos: 0 USD por autor de confirmaciones, más la facturación según el uso del trabajo basado en IA. Disponible en GitHub Enterprise Cloud y GitHub Team. Comienza Preguntas frecuentes ¿Cuánto cuesta Code Quality? 10 USD por autor de confirmaciones al mes, más la facturación según el uso del trabajo basado en IA. Los análisis deterministas de CodeQL consumen minutos de GitHub Actions. Los repositorios públicos no tienen ningún cargo por autor de confirmaciones; solo se factura según el uso de las capacidades basadas en IA. ¿Qué lenguajes admite Code Quality? Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, C# y Go. ¿Necesito otra herramienta para la cobertura de pruebas? No. Code Quality muestra los informes de cobertura de las herramientas de prueba que ya utiliza en formato Cobertura XML y, después, condiciona los merges según los umbrales definidos en Rulesets. Lee los datos de cobertura; no instrumenta las pruebas. ¿En qué se diferencia de GitHub Advanced Security? GitHub Advanced Security se centra en la seguridad: Code Security detecta vulnerabilidades y Secret Protection encuentra credenciales expuestas. Code Quality abarca la mantenibilidad, la fiabilidad y la cobertura, y ambas disciplinas se complementan. Los problemas de calidad suelen ocultar vulnerabilidades, por lo que un código más limpio reduce el trabajo de tu equipo de seguridad. Code Quality y Code Security se ejecutan en el mismo motor CodeQL, y ambos se reportan a través de un solo resumen de seguridad y calidad. ¿Code Quality funciona con la revisión del código de Copilot? Sí, como experiencias integradas, pero independientes. La revisión del código de Copilot ofrece comentarios en contexto a sus desarrolladores mientras escriben código, y esos comentarios son efímeros. Code Quality proporciona a sus responsables resultados persistentes, controles aplicables e informes que abarcan todos los repositorios y periodos. Ambos aparecen en la pull request. ¿Code Quality es un producto de cumplimiento? No. Code Quality facilita el gobierno interno y el flujo de trabajo de los desarrolladores. No constituye una certificación de cumplimiento con estándares regulatorios ni con un marco de auditoría. ¿Puedo gestionar la calidad en toda mi organización? Sí. Implemente Code Quality en toda la organización con paneles, acciones masivas, API y puntuaciones a nivel de repositorio y de organización. ¿Dónde puede mi equipo aprender a configurarlo? El itinerario de aprendizaje de GitHub Code Quality explica cómo activar las comprobaciones, configurar rulesets, corregir resultados con Autofix e interpretar los paneles. Comience el itinerario . Dismiss alert {{ message }} master Branches Tags Go to file Code Open more actions menu Latest commit History 25 Commits 25 Commits Folders and files Name Name Last commit message Last commit date deploy deploy public public server server tests tests .gitignore .gitignore README.md README.md View all files Repository files navigation nGIS nGIS е малка уеб ГИС система за управление на данни от проучване и проектиране, организирани по обекти. Всеки обект съдържа GeoJSON файлове: оси на пътища, сгради, граници на имоти, надлези и подлези на железопътни линии и други слоеве. Те се разглеждат на интерактивна карта, може да се преглеждат атрибутите им и да се управлява кой има право да ги чете и променя. Интерфейсът е на български, а приложението поддържа използваните в България координатни системи (BGS2005, UTM, ETRS89), както и WGS84 и Web Mercator. Функционалност Карта: карта на цял екран с подложки OpenStreetMap, сателитна и хибридна и странично меню с всички обекти и файлове: включване и изключване на слоеве и приближаване до обект или файл; легенда само с типовете геообекти, които се виждат в момента; при клик върху геообект изскача прозорец с всичките му атрибути. Обекти: списък с търсене, година и брой файлове. Администраторите създават обекти (с проверка на въведеното директно във формата) и ги изтриват (след потвърждение). Страница на обект: файлове с брой геообекти, размер и дата на качване. Може да се качват няколко GeoJSON или CAD файла наведнъж чрез влачене или избор от компютъра, с резултат за всеки файл. CAD файлове: файловете във формата за обмен на кадастрални данни ( .cad ) се преобразуват в GeoJSON при качване (вижте CAD файлове ). Страница на файл: карта за преглед с легенда на съдържанието и таблица с атрибути с филтър. Клик върху ред приближава картата до съответния геообект. Показва се и разпознатата координатна система, файлът може да се изтегли, а GeoJSON кодът може да се види. Координатни системи: файловете се преобразуват към проекцията на картата в браузъра (вижте Координатни системи ). Потребители: няма свободна регистрация. Акаунтите се създават от администратор в страницата „Потребители“: системата генерира временна парола, която се показва веднъж. Оттам се генерира и нова парола при забравена, изтрива се акаунт и се дават права за четене, запис и админ. Всеки потребител има профил с име, URL на снимка и смяна на парола. Роли Роля Може Без права Да влезе и да види профила си. Администраторът избира правата при създаване на акаунта и може да ги сменя по всяко време. Четене Да разглежда обекти, файлове и картата Запис Всичко от „Четене“, плюс качване и изтриване на файлове Админ Всичко, плюс създаване и изтриване на обекти и управление на потребителите Технологии Фронтенд Едностранично приложение (SPA) от статични файлове в public/ , без стъпка за компилиране. Библиотека Версия За какво се използва OpenLayers 10.11.0 Изобразяване на картата, четене на GeoJSON, стилове, изскачащи прозорци proj4js 2.22.0 Преобразуване на данни в BGS2005 / UTM / ETRS89 Bootstrap + Bootswatch Cyborg 5.3.3 Оформление, компоненти, тъмна тема jQuery 4.0.0 Работа с DOM и събития Handlebars 4.7.10 HTML шаблони в public/views/ toastr 2.1.4 Известия Moment.js 2.31.0 Форматиране на дати Font Awesome 4.7.0 Икони Roboto (@fontsource/roboto) 5.3.0 Шрифт на темата (латиница и кирилица, 400 и 700) Всички библиотеки, стилове и шрифтове са локални, в public/libs/ (по една папка за библиотека, с версията в името), така че сайтът не зависи от външни CDN-и. Всеки файл е свален от cdnjs и проверен срещу публикувания там SRI хеш. Шрифтът е проверен срещу хеша на npm пакета. Единствената промяна в тях: от темата Bootswatch е махнат @import към Google Fonts, защото Roboto се зарежда от libs/roboto-5.3.0/roboto.css . Маршрутизацията по адреса след # ( #/map , #/projects , …) е собствена, в public/app/router.js . Ползва събитието hashchange на браузъра. Подложките са от OpenStreetMap и Esri World Imagery . Това е единственото, което се зарежда от интернет. Без връзка интерфейсът и слоевете работят, но подложката не се вижда. Бекенд Python 3 (3.8+), само стандартната библиотека: http.server сервира статичните файлове и JSON API. SQLite ( sqlite3 , режим WAL) пази потребителите, сесиите, обектите и файловете. GeoJSON се съхранява като текст. Удостоверяване: паролите се пазят като PBKDF2-SHA256 хешове, а сесиите са в бисквитка с HttpOnly и SameSite=Lax . Първоначално приложението работеше на Firebase (Realtime Database, Auth и Hosting). Вижте Миграция от Firebase . search_index.description: O GitHub Code Quality revela descobertas nos pull requests com correções que podem ser revisadas antes de fazer o merge e ajuda a impor padrões constantes com rulesets.

Dismiss alert {{ message }} GitHub Code Quality GitHub Code Quality O GitHub Code Quality revela descobertas nos pull requests com correções que podem ser revisadas antes de fazer o merge e ajuda a impor padrões constantes com rulesets. Comece a usar Fale com a equipe de vendas Mantenha-se no fluxo de trabalho O GitHub Code Quality revela descobertas diretamente nos pull requests, para que os desenvolvedores não tenham que usar outro painel para isso. Corrija issues durante a revisão Cada descoberta inclui uma correção que pode ser revisada e aplicada pelos desenvolvedores antes de fazer o merge. Reduza o acúmulo de trabalho e entregue código mais rápido Gaste menos tempo na triagem de issues de qualidade e mais tempo na revisão e envio de correções. Detecção integrada para código na era da IA A análise determinística do CodeQL identifica quais regras são aplicadas. A detecção assistida por IA identifica o que elas não percebem. Juntas, elas acompanham o ritmo do código gerado pelos seus desenvolvedores, mais rápido do que qualquer biblioteca de regras cresce. Veja como a detecção funciona Corrija na origem Seus desenvolvedores não abrem um painel. Eles abrem um pull request. O Copilot Autofix sugere a correção ali mesmo. Eles a revisam, editam ou descartam. O merge não acontece sem supervisão. Conheça o Autofix Um único padrão, independentemente de quem ou o que escreve o código Os mesmos rulesets regem o código que seus desenvolvedores escrevem, as descobertas retornadas do code review do Copilot e os pull requests abertos por seus agentes de codificação. Qualidade e segurança, um único fluxo de trabalho. Veja como os rulesets funcionam Code Quality Qualidade no pull request, governança em toda a sua organização. $ 10 USD por committer/mês + uso Comece a usar Fale com a equipe de vendas O que está incluído Detecção híbrida (CodeQL determinístico com auxílio de IA) Autofix no pull request Limites de qualidade de rulesets, limites de cobertura e proteção de merge Pontuação de manutenção e confiabilidade Ingestão de cobertura (Cobertura XML) Implantação em toda a organização, painéis e APIs US$ 10 por committer/mês, mais cobrança baseada no uso para recursos de IA e minutos do Actions. Repositórios públicos: US$ 0 por commiter + cobrança baseada no uso para atividades baseadas em IA. Disponível no GitHub Enterprise Cloud e no GitHub Team. Comece a usar Perguntas frequentes Quanto custa o Code Quality? US$ 10 por committer ao mês, mais cobrança baseada no uso para atividades baseadas em IA. As verificações determinísticas do CodeQL consomem minutos do GitHub Actions. Repositórios públicos não têm cobrança por committer, com faturamento baseado no uso para recursos baseados em IA. Quais linguagens o Code Quality suporta? Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, C# e Go. Preciso de outra ferramenta para cobertura do teste? Não. O Code Quality renderiza relatórios de cobertura de suas ferramentas de teste existentes no formato Cobertura XML e faz o merge em seus limites por meio de rulesets. Ele lê a sua cobertura, mas não instrumenta os seus testes. Qual a diferença entre ele e o GitHub Advanced Security? O GitHub Advanced Security oferece recursos de segurança: o Code Security encontra vulnerabilidades e o Secret Protection encontra credenciais expostas. O Code Quality abrange a manutenibilidade, a confiabilidade e a cobertura, e as duas disciplinas trabalham em conjunto. Os issues de qualidade podem se esconder nas vulnerabilidades; portanto, um código mais limpo reduz as preocupações da sua equipe de segurança. O Code Quality e o Code Security são executados no mesmo mecanismo CodeQL, e as duas funcionalidades são apresentadas em uma visão geral única de segurança e qualidade. O Code Quality funciona com o Code Review do Copilot? Sim, como experiências integradas, porém distintas. O Code Review do Copilot fornece aos seus desenvolvedores feedback contextual enquanto eles escrevem o código, e seus comentários são efêmeros. O Code Quality oferece aos seus líderes descobertas persistentes, limites de qualidade obrigatórios e relatórios abrangendo repositórios e períodos. Ambos aparecem no pull request. O Code Quality é um produto de conformidade? Não. O Code Quality dá suporte a governança interna e fluxo de trabalho do desenvolvedor. Não se trata de padrões regulatórios ou estrutura de auditoria. Posso governar a qualidade em toda a minha organização? Sim. Implemente o Code Quality em toda a organização com painéis de controle, ações em massa, APIs e pontuação em nível de repositório e organização. Onde minha equipe pode aprender a configurá-lo? O roteiro de aprendizagem do GitHub Code Quality aborda a habilitação de verificações, a configuração de rulesets, a correção de descobertas com o Autofix e a leitura dos painéis de controle. Inicie o roteiro . You can’t perform that action at this time.

search_index.title: Apps can run OpenAI batches through Kaeso, checked against their key and charged at the batch price by dvnold · Pull Request #1243 · logicplanes/kaeso · GitHub
search_index.description: Self-hosted AI gateway in Rust: one OpenAI-, Anthropic-, Gemini- and ElevenLabs-compatible API for chat, images, video, speech and music on every provider, with SSO, roles, budgets, alias routes, request logs, a playground and an MCP portal. - Apps can run OpenAI batches through Kaeso, checked again
search_index.content: Apps can run OpenAI batches through Kaeso, checked against their key and charged at the batch price by dvnold · Pull Request #1243 · logicplanes/kaeso · GitHub Skip to content You signed in with another tab or window. Reload to refresh your session. You signed out in another tab or window. Reload to refresh your session. You switched accounts on another tab or window. Reload to refresh your session. Dismiss alert {{ message }} Conversation dvnold commented Nov 16, 2026 Copy link Copy Markdown Member What changes /v1/files and /v1/batches answered 404. Teams ran their batch jobs, often most of their tokens, with a raw provider key outside Kaeso's keys, model access and usage. This is step 1 of the issue: OpenAI-format batches at providers whose batch API takes them as they are, today OpenAI. Upload: POST /v1/files Takes multipart/form-data with purpose=batch (other purposes are refused) within the model API's body limit ( body_limits.model_api ). Every line is checked before anything reaches the provider: custom_id present and unique, method POST , no stream ; one url for the whole file ( /v1/chat/completions , /v1/responses or /v1/embeddings ) and one model, as OpenAI requires ("each input file can only include requests to a single model"); the body decodes with that endpoint's codec; the model resolves like a live request's (name, provider/model , id), the key's model access allows it, an alias is refused, the provider runs batches ( cost::batch_percent ), the endpoint's format suits the model (embeddings vs generation, a format the provider takes) and the project's key is an API key. The first line that breaks a rule refuses the whole file with its number ("Line 2 of the file: …"). At most 50,000 lines. The file goes on to the provider with each line's model written as the provider names it ( upstream_model ). The upload counts as one request against the key's rates. Records and endpoints Migration 20261116220000_batches.sql : batch_files and batches , with Kaeso ids ( file_… , batch_… ), the provider's ids, org, project, key, member or service account, provider key, endpoint, model, prices and the provider's last view. Both cascade with the project. GET / DELETE /v1/files/{file_id} , GET /v1/files/{file_id}/content (input, output and error files), POST / GET /v1/batches (list newest first, after , limit ), GET /v1/batches/{batch_id} and POST /v1/batches/{batch_id}/cancel . Every endpoint answers only to keys of the project that made the object; any other key gets 404 and nothing reaches the provider. An object whose provider key the project no longer uses gets 409. A batch's view is the provider's object with Kaeso's ids for the batch and its files, and the model as the app named it. Completion and cost Batch price: kaeso_core::cost::BATCH_PRICES ( openai : 50 %, from OpenAI's Batch guide) and cost::at_share , which scales every price of the model's Fields (token, image, audio, tiers, unit prices). The prices are stored with the batch when it's created. When a batch ends ( completed , failed , expired , cancelled ), Kaeso reads its output file once. A guard ( accounted_at ) keeps two gateways from both recording it. Each line becomes an outcome through the sink: usage from the line's body (decoded by the endpoint's codec), status, model, custom_id as the upstream request id, and the batch prices. Usage, cost and a request log row are written per line. A job ( batches , every 5 minutes, under the jobs' advisory lock) asks about open batches; GET /v1/batches/{id} asks too, as the SDK's polling does. Docs (en/de/zh-CN) New api/batches.md (with the API index), and the endpoints table in api/model-api.md . The other API pages' order moves by one. Tests kaeso-core : batch_percent , and at_share halves every kind of price, so a batch costs half. Try Online First Try typstyle instantly in your browser: 🎮 Playground The playground runs the latest version of typstyle with live formatting. Perfect for testing formatting behavior before installing locally. Installation and Usage Use as a CLI Installation You can install typstyle using any of the following methods: Download the binary from the release page . Install it from your package manager: https://repology.org/project/typstyle/versions . Notably, typstyle is available in Archlinux CN repo. Install using cargo-binstall : cargo binstall typstyle Install it with cargo : cargo install typstyle --locked CLI Usage Beautiful and reliable typst code formatter Usage: typstyle [OPTIONS] [INPUT]... Arguments: [INPUT]... List of files or directories to format [default: stdin] Options: -i, --inplace Format the file in place --check Run in 'check' mode. Exits with 0 if input is formatted correctly. Exits with a non-zero status code if formatting is required --diff Run in 'diff' mode. Shows unified diff of what formatting changes would be made. Exits with 0 if input is formatted correctly. Exits with a non-zero status code if formatting is required --line-ending <LINE_ENDING> Line-ending policy for formatted source output [default: preserve] [possible values: lf, crlf, preserve] -h, --help Print help -V, --version Print version Format Configuration: -l, --line-width <LINE_WIDTH> Maximum width of each line [default: 80] [aliases: column] [short aliases: c] -t, --indent-width <INDENT_WIDTH> Number of spaces per indentation level [default: 2] [aliases: tab-width] --no-reorder-import-items Disable alphabetical reordering of import items --wrap-text[=<WRAP_TEXT>] Text wrapping mode: none (default), fill (wrap to line width), sentence (one per line), or fill-sentence (both) [default: none] [possible values: none, fill, sentence, fill-sentence] Debug Options: -a, --ast Print the AST of the input file -p, --pretty-doc Print the pretty document --timing Show elapsed time taken by the formatter Log Levels: -v, --verbose Enable verbose logging -q, --quiet Print diagnostics, but nothing else The selected line-ending policy controls generated layout before the formatted source is written, printed, checked, or diffed. Diff control lines keep their normal LF output: lf always generates LF breaks. crlf always generates CRLF breaks. preserve (default) generates CRLF breaks when the input contains at least one CRLF and has no bare LF or bare CR. Mixed endings, bare CR, and inputs without newlines fall back to LF. All policies preserve newlines in strings, verbatim raw spans, and format-disabled source. Raw-block boundary breaks follow the layout policy. Range formatting detects against the entire original document. To enforce LF in CI, use typstyle --check --line-ending=lf explicitly. Examples Format a file in place: typstyle -i file.typ Format a file and print the result to stdout: typstyle file.typ Format multiple files in place: typstyle -i file1.typ file2.typ dir/ Format all files in a directory: typstyle -i dir Read from stdin and print the result to stdout: cat file.typ | typstyle > file-formatted.typ Use in your editor Typstyle has been integrated into tinymist . You can use it in your editor by installing the tinymist plugin and set tinymist.formatterMode to typstyle . Use in typst.app Checkout typstyle-tampermonkey , a userscript that integrates typstyle into the typst.app editor. Use as a web app Try the playground at: https://typstyle-rs.github.io/typstyle/playground The playground integrates the latest version of typstyle. If you encounter formatting issues, please verify them in the playground first before reporting bugs. Use as a Library Rust : https://crates.io/crates/typstyle-core WebAssembly : https://www.npmjs.com/package/@typstyle/typstyle-wasm-bundler Use as a GitHub Action The typstyle-action maintained by @grayespinoza can install and run typstyle in a GitHub Action. Use with pre-commit Add this to your .pre-commit-config.yaml : - repo : https://github.com/typstyle-rs/pre-commit-typstyle rev : ' ' # The revision or tag you want to use hooks : - id : typstyle Use with Jujutsu Configure typstyle as a jj fix tool: [ fix . tools . typstyle ] command = [ " typstyle " ] patterns = [ " glob:'**/*.typ' " ] # Optional: format only the lines changed by each commit line-range-args = [ " --lines=$first:$last " ] jj fix passes each file's content on stdin and reads the formatted content from stdout, so use the plain typstyle command without -i or a path argument. --lines FIRST:LAST formats only the selected 1-based, inclusive line ranges and prints the complete file. Features & Design Design Goals Opinionated : We want to have a consistent style across all codebases. Code only : We want to format only the code. Contents should be left untouched as much as possible. Convergence : Running

Dismiss alert {{ message }} main Branches Tags Go to file Code Open more actions menu Latest commit History 17 Commits 17 Commits Folders and files Name Name Last commit message Last commit date cartblanche cartblanche configs configs docs docs tasks tasks tests tests .env.example .env.example .gitignore .gitignore AGENTS.md AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md CLAUDE.md README.md README.md pyproject.toml pyproject.toml View all files Repository files navigation CartBlanche A personalized shopping agent that decides BUY / ALTERNATIVE / SKIP for a user's request, using their purchase history, and stays robust to seller-side manipulation (fake reviews, hidden instructions, fake "user approved" text). Built on Amazon Reviews 2023 (McAuley Lab; Beauty & Personal Care). The evaluation harness comes first, and every component is switchable so its effect can be measured (configs E0–E8). Setup python3.12 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate pip install -e " .[dev] " cp .env.example .env # add your GEMINI_API_KEY pytest python -m cartblanche.env.build_db # real store (~15 min, see below) python -m cartblanche.eval.run configs/e0_rules.yaml # results in runs/E0/ python -m cartblanche.eval.run configs/e1_generic.yaml --call-gap 4 # Gemini free tier: 4 s between calls python -m cartblanche.eval.run configs/e1_generic.yaml --tasks tasks/beauty.jsonl --split dev --call-gap 4 # real tasks Layout Path Owner Contents cartblanche/schemas.py shared Contracts: Product, Review, User, Task, AgentResult cartblanche/config.py shared Run config: one YAML per run, component switches cartblanche/llm.py shared LiteLLM wrapper: disk cache, token / cost / latency logging cartblanche/env/ A · Environment & attacks Store tools, beauty fake store + 11 tasks, attack injector cartblanche/agent/ B · Agent & personalization E0 rules baseline, E1 tool-calling agent, E2 intent parser; next: retrieval, history RAG cartblanche/defenses/ C · Defenses Fact extractor, untrusted-text labeling, verifier cartblanche/eval/ C · Evaluation Harness ( run ), code-checked metrics and scorecard; next: judge configs/ shared E0–E8 experiment configs Running on the free tier Runs resume: rerunning the same command skips tasks that already have a valid result and retries the ones that failed, so a run cut short by rate limits just continues. Rate limits and timeouts are retried with backoff; when the daily quota runs out, the run stops and tells you to rerun later. After changing a prompt or the code, pass --fresh so old results aren't reused. The real store python -m cartblanche.env.build_db streams Amazon Reviews 2023 Beauty & Personal Care from Hugging Face (about 14 GB) and keeps only what the tasks need in data/cartblanche.sqlite ; no raw files are saved. It samples 10,000 users with 8+ reviews and keeps their full histories, the 10 most helpful reviews of each product that has 5+ reviews, and those products' metadata. --spot-check 20 compares 20 stored products with the source. SqliteCatalog reads it through the same interface as the fake store. python -m cartblanche.env.taskgen --buy 150 then builds buy tasks from it into tasks/beauty.jsonl (committed): a user's later 4–5★ purchase is the gold, an LLM writes a general request with a budget, and the shelf mixes the gold with 9 hard distractors and same-category fillers. How the store works The agent never touches a real website. It calls five tools ( search_products , get_product , get_reviews , get_history , check_owned ) against a TaskStore , the view of the catalog one task sees: search only covers the task's shelf (~50 products; gold, hard distractors, fillers); history and reviews are cut at the task's as_of time, so the held-out gold purchase never leaks; an attacked task's injected reviews/text appear on the target product's page. Injected review IDs look exactly like genuine ones; only the evaluator sees TaskStore.injected_ids . Development plan: https://claude.ai/artifact/HvaZZ4H3KXXnRKuuWHnvTP Working on the repo Read AGENTS.md for conventions and docs/CONTEXT.md for the decisions so far, where the build stands, and the open questions. Both apply to people and AI coding agents alike ( CLAUDE.md points Claude Code at AGENTS.md ). About No description, website, or topics provided. Copy link Copy Markdown Collaborator What With a deck open, the AI knows which slide the person is on, so "make the corrections on this slide" works. The deck view tells the host the slide it shows in a new small message, deck/current-slide : the slide's place, id: and title: , and nothing else (the protocol refuses any other field), once it settles (150 ms). The current slide is the one the strip picked, the stage shows, or whose handout part holds the caret, by the view's existing rule. deck/current (the Slide library's insert point) is unchanged. Every message sent while the deck view is the tab in front carries one line , for Claude, ChatGPT and OpenCode through one shared helper ( activeFileLines ): [Current slide: The person is on slide 5 of 13 ("Why talk about agents?", id g001) in "AI assistants and agents".] The message carries the slide its chip showed when it was sent ( slideAtSend ), also when it waits in the queue; none when the chip showed none (×, or the deck attached whole as a path chip), and none for the deck's raw text view or a diff. The DECKS instructions say "this slide", "here" or "siin" means that slide, found by its id: . The composer's chip names the slide , by the Experience lead's look (the task card's precedent, 2.0: an opened task card's tab and AI chip show its file name (m4d7r2-draft-modul…), not its title #477 ): "Slide 5 · <title>" with the deck's icon, "Slide 5" with no title; tooltip ", slide 5 of 13. Claude reads 'this slide' as this one." with the composer's AI's name (Claude, ChatGPT or OpenCode). The × drops the deck and the slide for that one message. All the words are in src/decks/currentSlide.ts , including the lead's several-slides forms ("Slides 3–5", "Slides 2, 5, 7", "6 slides"). Why Jarmo, 17 November: the chip read "Active: " and nothing more, so there was no way to say "make the corrections on this slide". Risk REVIEW.md tier: Standard (AI context; extension-tier paths only). The DeckView edit is the current-slide message only. Privacy: only a slide's number, id and title travel; its words reach the AI through the deck tools when it reads. A title is quoted and its brackets turned round, so it can't end the context line. Proof docs/development/releases/v2.3.0/sprint-159-decks-training/research/proof/ai-current-slide/ (README there): the chip with its tooltip, the caret in a handout part moving the chip, Claude's captured request at a local stand-in (placeholder key, no network) carrying the slide line, a Text document's and the deck's raw text view's requests carrying none. Tests: src/decks/currentSlide.test.ts (the chip's words, the AI's line and its quoting, the sent slide), webview/src/components/decks/currentSlideMessage.test.ts (the message for the stage, the strip and the handout caret; hand-written ids; nothing else travels), deckProtocol.test.ts , capabilityContext.test.ts (all three runtimes), promptQueueStore.test.ts (a queued message keeps its slide), and the three runtimes' own tests ( AgentRunner.test.ts , CodexRuntime.test.ts 15b, AcpRuntime.test.ts 9b): the line is there for a deck and absent for a Text document. Not verified Several slides selected on the strip : the strip has no multi-select, so nothing sends more than one slide yet; the words and the protocol take a list. Building multi-select is a product call for its own PR. The chip while presenting (it should stay, since the deck view's slide doesn't move until Stop) was not looked at live. Live ChatGPT and OpenCode turns (unit-tested only); Windows. Copy link Copy Markdown Owner An agent can now write a game's music as people always have: as sheet music. It writes an ABC score with one voice per instrument and gets one song with a cue per tune. What changes importABCBook . A file of ABC tunes becomes one song, each tune a cue. %%cue , %%stinger , %%intro and %%layer lines name the game's cues, stingers, intros and layers. A part named Intro plays once before the loop. Voices with the same instrument share a lane across cues. importScore and tools/convert.mjs read such a file as a songbook. Scores as a composer writes them. Voices are written line by line ( [V:2] ... ). Each voice's instrument comes from its name ("Violins", "Electric Bass", "Synth Pad", "Pulse", "Drums") or from its %%MIDI program . Drum voices play General MIDI notes, unaffected by the key signature. Parts ( P:A ) play in the header's order ( P:Intro A2 B ). Tremolo, marcato and ornament decorations are read. The words "^pizz." , "^sul pont." and "^flz." become playing techniques. Lower threshold for acceptance. A bar that miscounts its beats is padded or cut at the bar line, with a warning that names the voice, part and bar, instead of breaking the score. Eleven calibrated band, synth and chip presets , played in the roll call. A score made only of them gets a room, a master and a drum kit to suit (the noise channel for chips). Chord symbols are accompanied in the song's style. songs/lantern_road.mjs . An original five-cue orchestral score written in ABC: title with an intro, town waltz, dungeon, battle, and a victory stinger. No warnings and no critic notes. Its cues are also added to CI's ears job and to the demo page, together with the three cue sets. Docs. docs/AI_GUIDE.md now starts with "Write it as sheet music (ABC)", with a template test/guide.test.mjs renders through the ears. HANDOFF gains M7. It ticks M4's mix box at the owner's lowered Audiobox target (enjoyment 6.0, quality 7.5); beethoven5 measures 6.84 / 7.84 and ode 6.24 / 7.59. Fixes Cue loop peak. A cue's loop could peak above the limiter's ceiling in its last milliseconds, because the limiter looks ahead and the mastering buffer ended there. The guide's band template went from -0.28 to -1.57 dBTP. Damped plucks. Plucked strings that are damped were given 8 s of ring, so band cues rendered slowly. The template's cue now renders in 5.6 s instead of 13.5 s. Measured Each cue of lantern_road as a game hears it: the head, then the loop twice. Audiobox scores the first minute. Cue LUFS True peak Key and tempo heard Audiobox enjoyment / quality title -16.2 -4.4 dBTP D major, 89 7.10 / 7.96 town -16.2 -2.0 dBTP G major, 140 6.85 / 8.13 dungeon -16.0 -4.0 dBTP D minor 5.79 / 7.46 battle -16.0 -2.3 dBTP A minor, 152 7.31 / 8.25 The code-written set_orchestral title scores 7.22 / 7.96 the same way, so a score written as sheet music does as well as one written as code. The dungeon carries two deliberate balance warnings: muddy (its low cello melody) and dull. It is a dark cue. Rendered output Cues change at their loop's last milliseconds and in their head lengths when they use damped plucks. The roll call has new bars. Golden hashes of existing songs are unchanged: their excerpts do not reach the changes. lantern_road is added. Checks npm test : 271 pass, 0 fail. npm run check : all checks passed. npm run page:test : all page checks passed, including a dropped ABC tune and no console errors. npm run ears -- songs/lantern_road.mjs : every cue passes. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code https://claude.ai/code/session_014hPughoDwRr2WZdKQ5TYaG --> Sorry, something went wrong. Все прочие запросы сканеров и ботов сбрасываются соединением return 444; без передачи HTTP-заголовков. It is a UEFI boot program with an arm64-to-x86-64 translator, a Metal driver for NVIDIA GPUs and a model of Apple silicon hardware. Stela currently presents itself as an M2 Mac mini. Warning Stela is still in development. It is slow and still may not boot on supported hardware. Fixes are on the way, please submit a GitHub Issue with your boot logs if you encounter an error! Translator An ahead-of-time and just-in-time compiler translates arm64e code to x86-64. It covers more than 3,000 AArch64 instruction encodings, maps guest registers to host registers and caches translated code. NVIDIA driver The Metal driver compiles AIR, Metal's shader IR, directly to NIR, Mesa's IR, and supports the Metal3 and Apple7 GPU families. Hardware requirements Part Requirement CPU Intel or AMD x86-64-v2 (Intel Nehalem, AMD Bulldozer or newer). AVX2 and AVX-512 are used when present. Memory 8 GB or more. Firmware 64-bit UEFI with Secure Boot off. GPU NVIDIA GeForce GTX 16 or RTX 20, 30, 40 or 50 series. Disk NVMe, or SATA in AHCI mode. 60 GB or more for macOS: a GPT partition or a whole disk to erase. USB stick 8 GB for the Online installer, 32 GB for the Offline installer. Ethernet Intel I225, I226, I210, I211, I350, 82574L, 82575, 82576, 82579, 82580, I217, I218, I219. Realtek RTL8111, RTL8168, RTL8169, RTL8411, RTL8125, RTL8126, Killer E2600, E3000. Broadcom BCM5720, BCM5761, BCM5762. Aquantia AQC100, AQC107, AQC108, AQC109, AQC111, AQC112, AQC113, AQC114, AQC115C, AQC116C. Qualcomm Atheros AR8131, AR8132, AR8151, AR8152, AR8161, AR8162, AR8171, AR8172, Killer E2200, E2400, E2500. USB: Realtek RTL8152, RTL8153, RTL8156, ASIX AX88179, AX88178A, AX88772, CDC ECM and NCM. Wi-Fi None currently supported. Bluetooth None currently supported. Audio None currently supported. USB xHCI (USB 3) and EHCI controllers, hubs, USB disks. Input USB keyboards and mice. PS/2 keyboards, mice and Synaptics or Elantech touchpads. Install Download stela from the releases page . Run sudo ./stela (Linux, macOS) or double-click stela.exe (Windows). Choose the USB stick and the installer, then confirm. This erases the USB stick. Boot the PC from the USB stick. Update Download the new stela , plug the USB stick in and run: sudo ./stela update On Windows, open Terminal with Run as administrator and run: .\stela.exe update Logs If Stela does not work, plug the USB stick into the computer that made it and save the boot log. Include log.txt in your GitHub Issue. sudo ./stela log --output log.txt On Windows, open Terminal with Run as administrator and run: .\stela.exe log --output log.txt Build You need Rust , git, Python 3.10 or newer, and LLVM 21, 22 or 23 with Clang, LLD and libclang. On macOS, Xcode's Apple clang 21 or newer also works. git clone https://github.com/tylertms/Stela cd Stela cargo xtask dist This writes target/release/stela . The first build fetches and compiles Linux, Mesa and LLVM sources and takes a long time. Legal Stela contains no Apple software. This is especially useful when interacting external APIs, remote services, or file system calls. Table of Contents Requirements Upgrading Installation Usage Defaults Options Configuring Which Options to Retry With :on Advanced Retry Matching With :retry_if Configuration Override Example Usage Custom Interval Array Unbounded Retries (Opt-in) Turn off Exponential Backoff Callbacks Disabling a Configured Callback Per Call Ensure/Else Contexts Kernel Extension Testing Credits Development Running Specs Requirements Ruby 3.2+ If you need Ruby 2.3.0-3.1.x support, use the 3.8.x branch by specifying ~> 3.8 in your Gemfile. If you need Ruby 2.0.0-2.2.x support, use the 3.1 branch by specifying ~3.1 in your Gemfile. If you need Ruby 1.9.3 support, use the 2.x branch by specifying ~2.1 in your Gemfile. If you need Ruby 1.8.x to 1.9.2 support, use the 1.x branch by specifying ~1.4 in your Gemfile. Upgrading Retriable 5.0 changes one thing for existing users: Retriable.config is now a frozen snapshot, so direct writes raise FrozenError . Retriable . config . sleep_disabled = true # => FrozenError Retriable . configure { | c | c . sleep_disabled = true } # do this instead Test setup files such as spec_helper and rails_helper are the likeliest place this bites. For the full 4.x to 5.x and 3.x to 4.0 guides, see docs/migration.md . Installation Via command line: gem install retriable In your ruby script: require 'retriable' In your Gemfile: gem 'retriable' , '~> 5.0' Usage Code in a Retriable.retriable block will be retried if an exception is raised. require 'retriable' class Api # Use it in methods that interact with unreliable services def get Retriable . retriable do # code here... end end end Defaults By default, Retriable will: rescue any exception inherited from StandardError make 3 tries (including the initial attempt) before raising the last exception use randomized exponential backoff to calculate each succeeding try interval. The default interval table with 10 tries looks like this (in seconds, rounded to the nearest millisecond): Retry # Min Average Max 1 0.25 0.5 0.75 2 0.375 0.75 1.125 3 0.563 1.125 1.688 4 0.844 1.688 2.531 5 1.266 2.531 3.797 6 1.898 3.797 5.695 7 2.848 5.695 8.543 8 4.271 8.543 12.814 9 6.407 12.814 19.222 10 stop stop stop Options Here are the available options, in some vague order of relevance to most common use patterns: Option Default Definition tries 3 Number of attempts to make at running your code block (includes initial attempt). Pass Float::INFINITY to keep retrying until success or until max_elapsed_time is reached. on [StandardError] Type of exceptions to retry. Read more . retry_if nil Callable (for example a Proc or lambda) that receives the rescued exception and returns true/false to decide whether to retry. Read more . on_retry nil Proc to call after each try is rescued. Pass false to disable a callback set in #configure for a single call. Read more . on_give_up nil Proc to call when Retriable stops retrying after a rescued retriable exception. Read more . sleep_disabled false When true, disable exponential backoff and attempt retries immediately. base_interval 0.5 The initial interval in seconds between tries. max_elapsed_time 900 (15 min) The maximum amount of total time in seconds that code is allowed to keep being retried. Set to nil to disable the time limit and retry based solely on tries . max_interval 60 Caps the interval before rand_factor is applied. A randomized interval may reach max_interval * (1 + rand_factor) . multiplier 1.5 Each successive interval grows by this factor. A multipler of 1.5 means the next interval will be 1.5x the current interval. rand_factor 0.5 The percentage to randomize the next retry interval time. The next interval calculation is randomized_interval = retry_interval * (random value in range [1 - randomization_factor, 1 + randomization_factor]) intervals nil Skip generated intervals and provide your own array of intervals in seconds. Read more . Timing options are validated before retrying. tries must be a positive integer when Retriable generates intervals, or Float::INFINITY for unbounded retries. base_interval , max_interval , multiplier , and max_elapsed_time must be non-negative numbers, with max_elapsed_time also accepting nil . rand_factor must be a number from 0 through 1 . If provided, intervals must be an array of non-negative numbers; because it replaces generated intervals, it also overrides tries , base_interval , max_interval , rand_factor , and multiplier validation. intervals cannot be combined with tries: Float::INFINITY . search_index.description: “DIY isn’t dead.” How to make a haunted house, lessons from LEGOs, and more DIY projects. (Issue #451) “As far as I could tell, my parents made the world,” writes Allisonn Church. They were …
search_index.content: Medium “DIY isn’t dead.”. How to make a haunted house, lessons… | by The Medium Newsletter | The Medium Blog | Oct, 2026 | Medium Sitemap Open in app Sign up Sign in Get app Write Search Sign up Sign in The Medium Blog · The official source of news and updates about Medium DIY Makers Home Improvement Arts And Crafts “DIY isn’t dead.” How to make a haunted house, lessons from LEGOs, and more DIY projects. (Issue #451) The Medium Newsletter Sent as a Newsletter · 5 min read · Oct 21, 2026 -- 7 Listen Share Press enter or click to view image in full size Festival Nacional Artesanal Aguascalientes in 2022, via Isra Rulowsinsky / Wikimeida Commons “As far as I could tell, my parents made the world,” writes Allisonn Church . They were major do-it-yourself-ers , handling everything from repairs to Halloween costumes and decorations with their own bare hands. Her childhood was filled with memories of working on projects together. “All things considered, my do-it-yourself story is more of a do-it-together story in the end,” Church writes. “Lucky me! I wouldn’t have it any other way.” Lucky for us, there’s a thriving scene of DIYers on Medium to help us go out and create things in the physical world together instead of spending all our time online — like decorations, crafting supplies, even LEGOs. In this issue, we’re sharing some interesting recent projects that you can do at home. Let’s get building. For me, the heart of DIY is having control over an idea. — Danny Edmunds , DIY Isn’t Dead. It’s Ready for a Comeback. Lessons from a fixer-upper When Jason DeCourcy Barefoot and his wife purchased a fixer-upper apartment back in 2021, he was inspired by decades of home improvement television shows. His wife was less sure . Years later, at the precipice of moving on to a new apartment, DeCourcy Barefoot looks back at their home improvement projects like building shelving units, redoing the bathroom, and updating the fireplace. But the most important lesson they learned was how to be a team. “It forced us into the right kind of collaboration,” he writes, “the kind where you have to trust each other, laugh at your mistakes, divide roles honestly, and learn when to step back and let the other person’s strengths lead.” Programming a haunted house Halloween is coming soon, and by his own admission, writer Anže Kravanja is not particularly artistic. Beautiful jack-o-lanterns might be out of the question for his home — but he does know how to code. “So, I asked myself the classic programmer’s question,” he writes, “‘What can I control with a computer in my house?’” Using a web camera, smart lightbulbs, and an API to link it all together, he created a house who spoke to treat or treaters and eventually became a “digital poltergeist.” See how he put it together . Homemade arts “My curiosity is always piqued when I realize that I might be able to make something instead of buying it,” writes Celeste Wilson in The DIY Diaries . “It may not always work out, but I have fun trying.” When she found someone who was selling homemade watercolor paints, she decided to find a way to make them herself. After much trial and error, she shares her recipe , which can be made with items commonly found around a kitchen, but she encourages experimentation. “Play around with it,” she writes. “See what works.” These days, I’m doing my best to see the “good” that comes from “negative” experiences like these. In other words, what are they trying to teach me? What lessons do I need to learn from them? — Patrice Walker in The DIY Diaries , An “Imperfect” Cat Bed Leads To Some Important Lessons LEGOs for learning LEGOs are the ultimate DIY toy. It doesn’t matter if you buy a big box of parts or a specialized kit — you will always need to put it together. Attila Vágó ’s publication, Bricks n’ Brackets , combines the iconic bricks with engineering fundamentals. For example: His recent piece on LEGO blind boxes shares how they can teach kids the fundamentals of mechanics: “44 pieces of fun and learning for the price of a coffee!” A review of the late-90s LEGO Barcode Computer showed how this basic form of programming inspired an entire generation of engineers and software developers. Vágó built a demonstration of synesthesia (where stimulating one sense leads to the sensation of another, such as associating certain letters with colors) using LEGO bricks and QR codes. Check it out for some engineering-brained projects. A tiny ecosystem Armando Rodrigues is fascinated by enclosed terrariums, or miniature gardens that are created inside glass. He finds the most interesting thing about them is just how self-sufficient they can be. “You do not need expensive equipment, rare plants or much experience with gardening,” he writes. “In fact, one of the things I like most about them is how much room there is for experimentation. Every terrarium I build ends up looking and behaving slightly differently.” Armando shares how to build one , including a good soil composition and how to pick out the right plants. Upcycling a chest When Michael Rhodes and his wife were newlyweds in Japan, budgets were extremely tight — so they became experts in the art of low-cost, DIY furniture. He shares how he used two Chabako (boxes used to ship Japanese tea) he found for less than $20 as a wooden chest. “They made beautiful rustic-looking storage boxes, which we use to this day and which made nice end tables some 45 years ago,” he writes. He’s so pleased with the results that he’s even purchased more for his current home, even adding brass hardware to give it a sleeker look. Learn more about them. A final thought John Kruse MD, PhD is a psychologist, so he often works with patients who have invisible illnesses , or diseases that don’t have any outwardly visible symptoms. These diseases can be deadly — Kruse points out that many “silent killers,” such as hypertension, diabetes, or infections like tertiary syphilis, don’t actually manifest symptoms until it’s very late

search_index.description: Pumpkin vampires and (un)dead actors Horror stories and our own Spooky Storytime on October 29. (Issue #452) Did you know that Japan has multiple bloodsucking demon myths, including the half-woman …
search_index.content: Medium Pumpkin vampires and (un)dead actors | by The Medium Newsletter | The Medium Blog | Oct, 2026 | Medium Sitemap Open in app Sign up Sign in Get app Write Search Sign up Sign in The Medium Blog · The official source of news and updates about Medium Horror Horror Fiction Mythology Halloween Pumpkin vampires and (un)dead actors Horror stories and our own Spooky Storytime on October 29. (Issue #452) The Medium Newsletter Sent as a Newsletter · 5 min read · Oct 28, 2026 -- 3 Listen Share Press enter or click to view image in full size Vintage Halloween card, via ewan traveler/Wikimedia Commons Did you know that Japan has multiple bloodsucking demon myths, including the half-woman, half-snake Nure-onn ? Or that in Ethiopia, a bloodsucking sorcerer known as a bouda is thought to be able to transform into a monstrous hyena? Or that among certain Muslim Romani villages in Kosovo in the 1930s, it was believed that pumpkins could become vampires ? There’s a chill in the air and it’s not just the weather. Halloween is this weekend — an excellent time to revisit horror’s place in our culture. In this issue, we take a look at the genre’s impact on Medium writers, from worldwide myths to low-budget movies. While the fictional Dracula struck fear in the hearts of his victims, Vlad was, literally, running a huge poles through those hearts. And this sadist relished every moment of his depravity. — Ds Traylor in Mythology Journal , The Real Dracula: Vlad the Impaler Learning from blood-suckers “The change was said to occur if they were kept for more than ten days after harvest,” James Cheney writes. “At that point, the pumpkins would begin to stir, shaking and making a sound, described in the oral accounts as a low, rolling rumble. Sometimes, even a drop of blood would appear on its rind.” Cheney’s publication, The Night Visitor Chronicles , showcases all things vampires — and not just ones inspired by Bram Stoker. Almost every culture on Earth has a legend about a blood-sucking monster (with some prominent exceptions ), and often those stories can tell us more about the cultures they come from. For example, in the 1970s a Slavic researcher claimed that recent Kashub immigrants in Wilno, Ontario, were opening graves and beheading the dead . The “vampire-slaying in rural Ontario” became a media sensation in the Canadian papers. But beyond the tabloids is the story of a displaced people bringing their culture to a new home: The traditions themselves, from the vjesci crossing the Atlantic to the caul being ground and given to a child on their seventh birthday just as it would have been done in Kashubia, are worth considering. It’s one of the most striking examples I know of how deep vampire belief runs, and how human beings cling to the stories that help them make sense of the world. For all their dark and less than sensitive sides, there’s something about 80s slashers that make you want to raid your local 7-Eleven’s candy and Jiffy Pop stash, sink into the nearest cavelike dwelling (with a couch), and press play. — Brandon Lennan in The Ugly Monster , Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma — Love Letter to 80s Slashers and Queer Freedom Raising the dead In 1997, Loren Kantor was hired to be in the props and art department during the three-day shoot of a low-budget zombie horror film. Two problems: Kantor had never worked on a film before. The film was starring actor John Carradine, who actually passed away a decade earlier. In Three Days on a Zombie Horror Film , Kantor recounts the misadventures from a truly undead shoot, from a script written around Carradine’s pre-recorded dialogue to snake handling. On the second day, Kantor was charged with creating the set for the film’s climax: “a horde of naked female vampire zombies rise from their graves and attack the mafia bosses responsible for their un-deaths.” That, of course, meant he was literally digging graves: At sundown, the prop man checks my progress. He’s incensed at my slow pace. “What’s your problem, buddy? You’re moving like a four-year old girl.” “I’ve never dug graves before,” I tell him. “You’re going to be digging your own grave if you don’t start hustling.” The shoot is a comedy of errors. Blood and mood are everywhere — he even has to wear a zombie suit after his clothing gets soaked on the final day, and the cash he’s paid in is covered in dried blood. In the comments, Kantor writes that the movie was released “but I never saw it.” Instead, after the shoot, he got some much-needed sleep. But have you ever wondered if you were in a horror movie, would you survive? Like, is there one monster or villain who you know you could take in a one-on-one fight? I’ve been thinking about this, and I am pretty certain that there are some villains I could take on if I found myself confronted by them. — Nick Howard in Hot List Energy , Horror Villains, I’m Pretty Sure I Can Take In a Fight Spooky stories Halloween is always a prime time to revisit some horror. On October 29, Medium will be hosting an online Spooky Storytime that you can sign up for here — but if you want some chills and thrills before then, the Medium community has you covered. Medium is host to a wide range of original horror fiction. In Evan Purcell ’s Death Squirrel: A Gay Horror Story , a man meets Death next to his partner’s hospital bed. A loner comes over for a meal with some people who may be just like them in LeonineLibra ’s Sweeter than Most . Red Mist Morning by Chantelle Atkins describes a mysterious red mist that overcomes a small Georgia town. A publisher learns the dark secret behind his former schoolmate’s writing in Marc Barham ’s The Devil is Always in the Detail . More interested in finding something to watch instead? Publications like The Ugly Monster feature culture writing specifically about horror; use them as starting off points for conversations about everything from the film Backrooms to the remake of the video game Dead Space.
