In its roles as journal archive, funder repository, and open science hub, PMC collects and distributes content under numerous participation agreements, funder policies, private-public partnerships, and initiatives. This page provides an overview of the resulting browsable collections, ordered by general size of the collection from largest to smallest. PMC Journal List Browse the PMC journal list to access the journals for which NLM has agreements with publishers and scholarly societies who deposit articles directly to PMC. Learn More PMC Article Datasets PMC includes several subsets of articles where files for text mining and other purposes are made available under Creative Commons or similar licenses. Learn More Author Manuscripts PMC is a repository for peer-reviewed accepted author manuscripts supported by the NIH as well as other public and private funders from around the globe. Learn More Selective Deposit Collections Encompassing a number of publishers in the biomedical and life sciences, this list of publisher-based collections spans thousands of journals that deposit select articles to PMC. Learn More COVID-19 Collection A collaboration between NLM and more than fifty publishers to make coronavirus-related articles accessible in PMC under license terms that facilitate re-use and secondary analysis. Search PMC Full-Text Archive Search in PMC Journal List User Guide For Publishers PubMed Central® (PMC) is a free full-text archive of biomedical and life sciences journal literature at the U.S. National Institutes of Health's National Library of Medicine (NIH/NLM). A publisher may be interested in submitting content to PMC in order to increase discoverability of and access to its content; ensure a long-term, publicly accessible archive of a journal; help authors comply with the policies of funding agencies that require articles to be made available in PMC; or comply with the MEDLINE Policy on Indexing Electronic Journals Submission Options To support these goals, PMC offers three submission options for publishers to consider: Journal Participation: A journal deposits the final published version of every article or its NIH-funded articles if the journal meets NLM's standards for inclusion in PMC. Interested journals should review the current Participation Agreements . To learn more, see the PMC Application and Evaluation webpage. Selective Deposit Participation: A publisher deposits select articles from a collection of MEDLINE journals and/or articles that have support from a PMC-partner or Europe PMC-partner funder. Interested publishers should review the current Selective Deposit Participation Agreement . Author Manuscript Deposit: A publisher initiates deposit of the author manuscript version of an article to the NIH Manuscript Submission (NIHMS) system on an author's behalf to support compliance with a number of funder policies (see NIHMS Funders ). There are no formal agreements between publishers and NLM for author manuscript deposit. See the NIHMS FAQ for more information. Participating journals and selective deposit publishers are required to deposit full-text XML for every article and meet PMC's other technical quality requirements . Author manuscript deposit does not require full-text XML. To be eligible for any of the above options, NLM expects a publisher to conform with guidelines and best practices established by relevant professional publishing organizations. Please see Expectations for PMC Participants on our Policies page for details. PMC Publisher Services PMC provides participating journals and publishers access to the Publisher Services website , where a suite of tools and reports are available for applying to PMC, tracking deposits, and obtaining usage statistics. Participants can visit the Publisher Services website for more information. Stay Current To stay current on updates to PMC, please subscribe to New in PMC . For additional general and publisher-related information, see the resources linked in the right hand column. Search PMC Full-Text Archive Search in PMC Journal List User Guide Journal Selection for PMC The National Library of Medicine (NLM) decides whether the scientific and editorial character and quality of a journal merit its inclusion in PMC. In making this decision NLM considers the suitability of the journal for the NLM collection (based on the criteria in the Collection Development Guidelines ), as well as the recommendations of external, expert consultants. The current scientific and editorial quality review process for journals that apply to participate in PMC has been in place since November 2014. At least two consultants, usually one scientist (i.e., doctoral-level researchers or physicians) and one medical librarian review each journal. The consultants generally review articles from the last two years of journal content and evaluate them primarily based on scientific and editorial quality. Their recommendations are taken into consideration by NLM in reaching a final decision on selecting a title for inclusion in PMC. PMC's scientific and editorial quality evaluation is a rigorous, multi-step process (see PMC Application and Evaluation Process for step-by-step details) in which many factors are assessed. NLM views each journal comprehensively, rather than basing a decision on a defined list of criteria. Each title is reviewed by multiple individuals, both inside and outside of NLM, and final decisions are based on input from all these sources. To maintain the quality of the archive, NLM performs ongoing review of current PMC journals for conformance with these standards. A description of possible considerations during Scientific Quality Review is given below. For an overview of the PMC pre-application requirements as well as a step-by-step breakdown of the PMC application and review process, please see PMC Application and Evaluation Process . Journals that already are fully indexed for MEDLINE generally will not require further scientific review for PMC. Scientific and Editorial Quality Assessment The scientific quality assessment for PMC focuses on the scientific rigor of the articles examined. NLM uses the definition of scientific rigor provided by the NIH Office of Extramural Research , which defines scientific rigor as "the strict application of the scientific method to ensure robust and unbiased experimental design, methodology, analysis, interpretation and reporting of results." This includes full transparency in reporting experimental details so that others may reproduce and extend the findings. NLM also looks for journals to demonstrate good editorial quality and elements that contribute to the objectivity and credibility of the content in deciding whether to select a journal for PMC. Examples of the types of questions PMC consultants may consider when performing their evaluations include: Category Possible Considerations Journal policies Are the journal's aims and scope clearly stated and adhered to? Is the peer review process explicit and sufficiently detailed? Does the journal have a policy for the review of articles authored by editors and editorial board members (if applicable)? Are the journal's ethical policies clearly stated and adhered to? Are commercial sponsorships clearly addressed (i.e., do not raise questions about objectivity of published content)? Do authors consistently disclose financial conflicts of interest? Article content Does the abstract provide a complete and accurate description of the content of the article? Are the study aims clearly stated and logical? Is the rationale/justification for conducting the study clear? Are the methods described in sufficient detail so that the experiment could be reproduced? Does the article/study adhere to relevant reporting guideline(s) ? Is the study design robust and appropriate to the stated aim? Are the conclusions drawn supported by the data? Is the discussion section critical and comprehensive? Are the references appropriate in number and up-to-date? Are statements supported appropriately by parenthetical citations? Is the writing clear (i.e., does not impede scientific meaning or cause confusion), concise, and logical? Figure and table quality Are figures and tables well-constructed and of sufficiently high resolution (i.e., not blurry)? Are figures and tables well-annotated and easy to read and interpret? Writing quality (i.e., English editing) Is the writing clear, concise, and logical? Does the writing impede scientific meaning or cause confusion? Formatting and organization Do articles of the same type (e.g., original research) follow a consistent structure, outlined in the instructions for authors? Are there indicators of sufficient editorial attention, as evidenced by the elimination of editorial errors (e.g., incorrectly numbered sections, mislabeled tables/figures)? Editorial board and authorship Are full names and affiliations of journal’s editors provided? Do editors and authorship accurately reflect journal scope? Is there sufficient variation in the editorial board and the authorship of articles? Publication schedule Does the journal keep to its stated publication schedule? Does the publication frequency and volume demonstrate long-term sustainability? In addition to the above, as outlined in the Collection Development Guidelines , review articles should generally contain substantive summaries and analysis of recent research in a field. Case reports should include thorough and detailed case presentations, as well as substantial discussions about the relevance to clinical practice and research. search_index.title: Medicare Part B Drugs: Action Needed to Reduce Financial Incentives to Prescribe 340B Drugs at Participating Hospitals | U.S. GAO
search_index.description: What GAO Found Certain providers, including hospitals that serve a disproportionate number of low-income patients, have access to discounted prices on...
search_index.content: Medicare Part B Drugs: Action Needed to Reduce Financial Incentives to Prescribe 340B Drugs at Participating Hospitals | U.S. GAO Skip to main content GAO-15-442 Published: Jun 05, 2015. Publicly Released: Jul 06, 2015. Jump To: Skip to Highlights Highlights What GAO Found Certain providers, including hospitals that serve a disproportionate number of low-income patients, have access to discounted prices on outpatient drugs through the 340B Drug Pricing Program, which is administered by the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) within the Department of Health & Human Services (HHS). In 2012, these hospitals—referred to as 340B disproportionate share hospitals (DSH) because they are eligible for the program based on their serving a disproportionate share of low-income patients and other specified criteria—were generally larger and more likely to be teaching hospitals compared with non-340B hospitals. They also tended to provide more uncompensated and charity care than non-340B hospitals; however, there were notable numbers of 340B hospitals that provided low amounts of these types of care. For example, 12 percent of 340B DSH hospitals were among the hospitals that reported providing the lowest amounts of charity care across all hospitals in GAO's analysis. Overall financial margins for 340B DSH hospitals tended to be lower compared with non-340B hospitals, which could be attributable, in part, to the tendency for 340B DSH hospitals to provide more uncompensated and charity care. GAO found that in both 2008 and 2012, per beneficiary Medicare Part B drug spending, including oncology drug spending, was substantially higher at 340B DSH hospitals than at non-340B hospitals. This indicates that, on average, beneficiaries at 340B DSH hospitals were either prescribed more drugs or more expensive drugs than beneficiaries at the other hospitals in GAO's analysis. For example, in 2012, average per beneficiary spending at 340B DSH hospitals was $144, compared to approximately $60 at non-340B hospitals. The differences did not appear to be explained by the hospital characteristics GAO examined or patients' health status. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), which administers the Medicare program, uses a statutorily defined formula to pay hospitals for drugs at set rates regardless of hospitals' costs for acquiring the drugs. Therefore, there is a financial incentive at hospitals participating in the 340B program to prescribe more drugs or more expensive drugs to Medicare beneficiaries. Unnecessary spending has negative implications, not just for the Medicare program, but for Medicare beneficiaries as well, who would be financially liable for larger copayments as a result of receiving more drugs or more expensive drugs. In addition, this raises potential concerns about the appropriateness of the health care provided to these beneficiaries. HRSA and CMS have limited ability to counter this incentive because the 340B statute does not restrict covered entities from using drugs purchased at the 340B discounted price for Medicare Part B beneficiaries and the Medicare statute does not limit CMS reimbursement for such drugs. In commenting on a draft of this report HHS noted some concerns with GAO's conclusions and suggested that further analysis may be needed to examine patient outcomes and differences in health status. GAO believes its methods appropriately support its conclusions as further discussed in the report. Why GAO Did This Study Approximately 40 percent of all U.S. hospitals participate in the 340B Drug Pricing Program, and the majority of 340B discounted drugs are sold to hospitals. Medicare reimburses hospitals for Part B drugs under a statutory formula regardless of the prices hospitals paid for the drugs. Stakeholders have questioned the increase in hospital participation in the 340B program, and the implications for Medicare and its beneficiaries, especially regarding cancer care; and whether certain of the program's hospital eligibility criteria target hospitals appropriately. GAO was asked to review hospitals' participation in the 340B and Medicare programs. This report (1) compares 340B hospitals with non-340B hospitals in terms of financial and other characteristics and (2) compares spending for Medicare Part B drugs at 340B hospitals, for all drugs and for oncology drugs, with spending at non-340B hospitals. To examine hospital participation using the most recent data available, GAO analyzed 2008 and 2012 data from HRSA and CMS to compare characteristics and Medicare Part B drug spending for 340B hospitals and non-340B hospitals. Recommendations Congress should consider eliminating the incentive to prescribe more drugs or more expensive drugs than necessary to treat Medicare Part B beneficiaries at 340B hospitals. Matter for Congressional Consideration Matter Status Comments To help ensure the financial sustainability of the Medicare program, protect beneficiaries from unwarranted financial burden, and address potential concerns about the appropriateness of the health care provided to Part B beneficiaries, Congress should consider eliminating the incentive to prescribe more drugs or more expensive drugs than necessary to treat Medicare Part B beneficiaries at 340B hospitals. Open In May 2025, the SMART Health Care Act (H.R.3222) was introduced in the House of Representatives. The bill requires the establishment of a mechanism to adjust reimbursement rates for covered entities for certain outpatient prescription drugs provided by hospitals to Medicare patients, and if enacted, could potentially address this Matter for Congressional Consideration. As of February 2026, this bill remains in committee. search_index.description: Since January 1, 2026, the Maximum Fair Price (MFP) has been available to pharmacies and other dispensing entities (collectively, “pharmacies”) dispensing a subset of ten selected drugs to beneficiaries covered by Medicare Part D.
search_index.content: Update on Effectuation of the Maximum Fair Price in 2026 and Outlook for 2027 | Insights | BRG Insights Share publication | BRG Update on Effectuation of the Maximum Fair Price in 2026 and Outlook for 2027 April 2026 back to top Intelligence That Works BRG is home to renowned thought leaders and experts considered authorities in their fields of work. Our timely research and perspectives provide analysis and insights on the most important issues facing the industries and organizations we serve. Please note: A prior version of this report incorrectly stated that the study was funded by the Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America. The study was self-funded by BRG. Since January 1, 2026, the Maximum Fair Price (MFP) has been available to pharmacies and other dispensing entities (collectively, “pharmacies”) dispensing a subset of ten selected drugs to beneficiaries covered by Medicare Part D. The MFP has been offered in the market through the following process: The pharmacy acquires the drug from a wholesaler or distributor or directly from the manufacturer, dispenses it to the Part D beneficiary, and bills the beneficiary’s Part D plan. The beneficiary’s Part D plan reimburses the pharmacy at the MFP plus a dispensing fee and transmits data on the dispense to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). CMS, through a contractor known as the Medicare Transaction Facilitator (MTF), transmits the dispense data to the manufacturer and its rebate processing partner, the Beacon MFP platform.1 Per CMS guidance, the manufacturer has fourteen days from receipt of data to 1) determine if the price paid by the pharmacy to acquire the drug exceeds the MFP, and 2) transmit the data back to CMS indicating whether a rebate will be paid to bring the pharmacy’s net acquisition cost to the MFP. The MTF disburses manufacturer rebates to pharmacies. Where pharmacies have opted in, the disbursement is done using electronic funds transfer (EFT). search_index.content: About PMC - PMC Skip to main content Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you've safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. Search PMC Full-Text Archive Search in PMC Journal List User Guide About PMC PubMed Central ® (PMC) is a free full-text archive of biomedical and life sciences journal literature at the U.S. National Institutes of Health's National Library of Medicine (NIH/NLM). In keeping with NLM's legislative mandate to collect and preserve the biomedical literature, PMC is part of the NLM collection, which also includes NLM's extensive print and licensed electronic journal holdings and supports contemporary biomedical and health care research and practice as well as future scholarship. Available to the public online since 2000, PMC was developed and is maintained by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) at NLM. About the Content Since its inception in 2000, PMC has grown from comprising only two journals, PNAS: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences and Molecular Biology of the Cell, to an archive of articles from thousands of journals. In addition, PMC also contains author manuscripts deposited through the NIH Manuscript Submission System (NIHMS), and preprints collected through the NIH Preprint Pilot . The PMC archive contains more than 10 million full-text article records spanning several centuries of biomedical and life science research (late 1700s to present). This content includes articles that have been formally published in a scholarly journal, author manuscripts that have been peer-reviewed and accepted for publication in a journal, and preprint versions of articles that have been made public prior to peer review. Content is deposited in the PMC archive through collaborations with publishers, societies, research funders, and international organizations. Our Collections page provides an overview of the collections that result from these content collaborations. For more information on content in PMC, see our Policies page and the PMC Disclaimer . About the Archive NLM has a statutory mission to collect, index, preserve, and make available biomedical and health-related literature of the present-day and from the past. As such, PMC is designated to provide permanent access to all of its content, even as technology evolves. (Learn more in the Collection and Preservation Policy of the NLM .) PMC makes all content free to read (in some cases, following an embargo period), as NLM believes that the best way to ensure the accessibility and viability of digital material over time is through consistent and active use of the archive. However, free access does not mean that there is no copyright protection (see the PMC Copyright Notice ). PMC stores content in eXtensible Markup Language (XML), which represents the structure and meaning of a document in a relatively simple and human-readable form. All PMC content is converted to and stored in the NISO Z39.96-2015 JATS XML format. This standard format is the most effective and widely used archival format for journal articles. NLM operates the PMC International network, which provides a framework to maintain copies of the PMC corpus in other reliable international archives that share the goals of PMC and operate on the same principles. Because PMC has the capacity to store and cross reference data from diverse sources in a common format within a central repository, a PMC user can quickly search the entire collection of full-text articles and locate all relevant material. The structure of the PMC archive also supports the integration of the literature with other resources. Bulk retrieval of files for text mining and other purposes is permitted within certain collections or subsets of the PMC archive. An overview of these subsets of the archive is available at PMC Article Datasets . About PMC Archive Use In addition to ensuring the long-term preservation of the scientific literature, PMC provides access to the archive in human- and machine-readable formats. Use of PMC has increased as the archive has grown. Numbers reported below for FY13-FY21 reflect access to the PMC website in the last month of each fiscal year (September). search_index.description: /PRNewswire/ -- What information should patients review on a prescription bottle before taking their medication? HelloNation published an article that answers...
search_index.content: Prescription Label Guidance Explained in HelloNation Featuring Pharmacy Expert Sheldon Birch Accessibility Statement Skip Navigation The article outlines how understanding prescription directions and safety information can help prevent medication errors. MAGNA, Utah , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What information should patients review on a prescription bottle before taking their medication? HelloNation published an article that answers this question, featuring insights from pharmacist Sheldon Birch of Oquirrh Mountain Pharmacy in Magna, Utah. The article explains how understanding a prescription label can help patients use medications safely, follow treatment plans correctly, and avoid common mistakes that may interfere with their health. Continue Reading Dr. Sheldon Birch, Pharmacist The HelloNation article emphasizes that every prescription label serves as a personalized guide for medication use. While many patients focus only on the medication itself, the article notes that the information printed on a prescription bottle contains essential details about dosage, timing, and medication safety. Reviewing these instructions carefully can reduce confusion and support better health outcomes. According to the article, one of the most important sections of a prescription label is the medication name and strength. The medication name identifies the prescribed drug, while the strength indicates the amount of medication contained in each dose. The article explains that patients should verify this information each time they receive a prescription, especially if they take multiple medications or notice changes in their prescription bottle. The article also highlights the importance of following prescription directions exactly as written. Prescription directions explain how much medication to take, how often to take it, and whether to take it with food or on an empty stomach. Some medications may also require specific timing, such as morning or bedtime use. The article advises patients to ask a pharmacist for clarification whenever prescription directions include unfamiliar terms or abbreviations. Another section of the article covers refill information. Understanding remaining refills can help patients avoid treatment interruptions. The article explains that remaining refills indicate how many times a medication can be dispensed without requiring a new authorization from the prescribing provider. Patients who monitor their remaining refills can better plan ahead and avoid gaps in therapy. Medication safety warnings are another key focus of the article. These warnings may include instructions about avoiding alcohol, limiting certain activities, or taking medication with food. The article notes that medication safety information is tailored to the specific medication and should always be reviewed before use. Ignoring these warnings can increase the risk of side effects or reduce treatment effectiveness. The article focuses on older adults, who often manage several prescriptions at once. For older adults, medication management can become more complex due to multiple dosing schedules and similar-looking prescription bottles. The article explains that reviewing the prescription label carefully before each use can support safer medication management and reduce the likelihood of errors. Parents caring for children can also benefit from carefully reviewing prescription directions and medication safety instructions. The article notes that pediatric medications frequently include age-specific or weight-based dosing requirements. A pharmacist can clarify unclear instructions, helping families administer medications correctly. Throughout the article, the pharmacist is presented as an important patient resource. The article encourages individuals to ask a pharmacist questions whenever they are uncertain about a prescription label, refills remaining, or medication safety instructions. Pharmacists can help patients understand their medication management responsibilities and ensure they use medications as intended. The article concludes that understanding a prescription label is an important step in preventing medication errors. By reviewing prescription directions, monitoring refills remaining, and paying attention to medication safety warnings, patients of all ages can make more informed decisions about their care and improve medication management practices. How to Read a Prescription Label and Avoid Common Mistakes features insights from Sheldon Birch, a Pharmacist Expert in Magna, Utah, on HelloNation. About HelloNation HelloNation is America's Good News Network, a premier media platform built on the idea that good news travels faster when real people tell real stories. Through its community-focused publications and innovative "edvertising" approach, HelloNation delivers content that informs, inspires, and spotlights the leaders making a meaningful impact in their communities. search_index.content: Radnostix, Inc. Reports FY2026 3rd Quarter and Nine Months Results - Theranostics Sales Up 15% Year-over-Year, Signs Agreement to Sell Fluorine Products/DUF6 Assets to Nano Nuclear Energy, Submits Type II DMF for Sodium Iodide I-131 API Accessibility Statement Skip Navigation IDAHO FALLS, Idaho , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Radnostix, Inc. (formerly International Isotopes Inc.) (OTCQB: INIS ) ("Radnostix" or the "Company"), a manufacturer of radioisotope-focused technologies for medical, industrial, and research applications, today announced its financial results for the third quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and the filing of its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Third Quarter and Nine Months 2026 Financial and Operational Summary Total revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $2.57 million, a 22% decrease from $3.28 million in the prior-year period. Revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $7.62 million, down 25% from $10.17 million in the first nine months of 2025. The third-quarter decline was driven primarily by delays in large Cobalt Products contracts, which are awaiting NRC amendments to the Company's registered sealed source devices, and lower Calibration & Reference Products sales due to a global interruption of cobalt-57 raw material supply, partially offset by a 15% increase in Theranostics Products sales. The nine-month decline also reflects the additional effects of the two voluntary product recalls initiated in the first quarter and the first-quarter Cobalt hot-cell shutdown. Gross profit for the quarter was $1.51 million (59% margin) compared with $1.94 million (59% margin) in Q3 2025. Nine-month gross profit was $4.02 million (53% margin) versus $6.11 million (60% margin) in the prior-year period, stemming largely from the two voluntary Theranostics Product recalls. Total operating expenses for the quarter were $2.30 million, up 8% from $2.12 million in Q3 2025, primarily reflecting higher professional services and license costs and increased Medical Devices development activity. Nine-month operating expenses were $6.95 million, up 7% from $6.49 million. Net loss for the quarter was $0.84 million compared with $0.20 million in Q3 2025. Nine-month net loss was $3.07 million versus $0.48 million in the first nine months of 2025. Cash and cash equivalents were $0.71 million at September 30, 2026, compared with $1.70 million at December 31, 2025. In addition, the Company held $1.53 million of restricted cash supporting its NRC financial assurance. In October 2026, the Company entered into a $1.0 million revolving line of credit with Bank of Commerce to provide additional working capital and liquidity. The facility has a 12-month term and bears interest at the prime rate. Borrowings limits under the facility are subject to eligible accounts receivable and inventory and are secured by the Company's accounts receivable, inventory, and equipment. Shahe Bagerdjian, President and Chief Executive Officer, commented: "The third quarter showed the recovery of our core Theranostics business, with volumes restored in July and revenue up 15% over last year, and we took an important step to support a customer's NDA with our Type II DMF submission for Sodium Iodide I-131 API. Our Cobalt and Calibration & Reference results were held back by contract timing tied to NRC sealed source amendments and by a global cobalt-57 supply interruption, but we have since begun shipping Gd-153 products for the first time since the global outage. The agreement to sell our Fluorine Products/DUF6 assets to Nano Nuclear Energy, which remains subject to NRC approval and other closing conditions, would allow us to focus on our core radioisotope and medical device businesses. We are still focused on developing our medical devices and building stronger OEM relationships with camera companies for our Calibration & Reference products. Our priorities for the fourth quarter and into 2027 are clear: grow core revenues, convert our Cobalt and Calibration & Reference Products backlog, finalize launch of our Medical Devices products, and control costs." Segment Highlights Theranostics Products: Q3 revenue of $1.71 million (up 15% year-over-year) and nine-month revenue of $4.18 million (down 19%). Segment income was $0.67 million in the quarter compared with $0.63 million in Q3 2025, with gross margin of approximately 67% in both periods. The three-month increase reflects growth in customers compared to prior year. The nine-month decline reflects lost capsule-related revenue of an estimated $850,000 during the first half of the year as a result of the voluntary recalls. FDA Actions: Both voluntary recalls have been fully executed and all required documentation was submitted to the FDA in June 2026; the Company is awaiting formal recall close-out. A request for close-out of the April 2025 FDA Form 483 inspection was submitted by the Company. Type II Drug Master File: In October 2026, the Company submitted a Type II Drug Master File (DMF) to the FDA for Sodium Iodide I-131 active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) in support of a customer's efforts to gain approval of its own New Drug Application. The Company anticipates a period of FDA review and potential requests for additional information. Calibration & Reference Products: Q3 revenue of $0.74 million (down 23%) and nine-month revenue of $2.68 million (down 19%). A global interruption of cobalt-57 raw material supply beginning in July 2026 reduced third-quarter sales by an estimated $250,000, and the Company had a backlog of approximately $300,000; prior-year results also included catch-up demand following the 2024 cobalt-57 shortage. The outage may also affect fourth-quarter cobalt-57 product sales if global suppliers are unable to catch up on deliveries. search_index.title: Yale School of Medicine Receives $10M Gift to Cure Type 1 Diabetes
search_index.description: /PRNewswire/ -- Yale School of Medicine received a $10 million gift, funding a five-year, multi-investigator research program focused on reversing and...
search_index.content: Yale School of Medicine Receives $10M Gift to Cure Type 1 Diabetes Accessibility Statement Skip Navigation NEW HAVEN, Conn. , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Yale School of Medicine received a $10 million gift, funding a five-year, multi-investigator research program focused on reversing and ultimately curing type 1 diabetes. The gift was given by Anastasia and Igor Bukhman, through the Bukhman Foundation . Continue Reading Credit: Anastasia Bukhman, courtesy Bukhman Foundation "We are grateful to Anastasia and Igor Bukhman for their generosity and for the trust they have placed in our investigators," says Nancy J. Brown, MD , the Jean and David W. Wallace Dean of Yale School of Medicine. "This philanthropic support will enable these researchers to transform how type 1 diabetes is treated by developing precision therapies to modify its course and eventually prevent it." For the Bukhman's, diabetes is personal, affecting their family members, including Anastasia's daughter, who was diagnosed at 3 years old. "It's a condition that has been in our family for a long time," she says, "and one that has played a big role in shaping the work we do today." Kevan Herold, MD , the C.N.H. Long Professor of Immunobiology and of Medicine (Endocrinology), leads work focused on halting the immune attack on beta cells and developing personalized treatment approaches based on each patient's genetic and immunologic profile. "The gift funds a number of projects which are all focused on stopping the immune-mediated pathogenesis of type 1 diabetes and restoring lost insulin-producing beta cells," says Herold. "The research is very goal-directed, and that goal is the prevention or reversal of disease. The studies will develop personalized approaches to treatment involving analyses of gene signatures, immunologic features, and beta cells from individuals with and at risk for diabetes." In addition to Herold, the program will support the work of the following scientists: Esen Sefik, PhD , assistant professor of immunobiology, contributes research that strengthens disease modeling and characterizes variation among patients' immune cells. Richard Flavell, PhD , Sterling Professor of Immunobiology, brings expertise in engineering mice to study the immune system. Nikhil Joshi, PhD , professor of immunobiology and co-leader of Cancer Immunology at Yale Cancer Center, applies insights from cancer immunology to questions of immune cell behavior and tolerance in type 1 diabetes. Richard Kibbey, MD, PhD , Ensign Professor of Medicine (Endocrinology and Metabolism) and professor of molecular and cellular physiology, focuses on beta-cell biology and the survival and enhancement of function of replacement insulin-producing cells. John Tsang, PhD , Anthony N. Brady Professor of Immunobiology and Biomedical Engineering and director of Yale's Center for Systems and Engineering Immunology, applies computational modeling to analyze complex immune data that can capture patient-specific features across the program. About Yale School of Medicine Yale School of Medicine educates leaders in medicine and science, fostering curiosity and critical inquiry. It is a global leader in biomedical research, clinical care, and medical education. With over 1,700 physicians, Yale provides compassionate care to patients worldwide. The Yale System of Medical Education emphasizes critical thinking and independent research, producing leaders in academic medicine. search_index.title: DANA FOUNDATION ANNOUNCES 2026 NEUROSCIENCE & SOCIETY CHAMPION AWARD RECIPIENTS
search_index.description: /PRNewswire/ -- The Dana Foundation has named Jennifer French, MBA, and Eric H. Chudler, Ph.D., recipients of its second annual Neuroscience & Society Champion...
search_index.content: DANA FOUNDATION ANNOUNCES 2026 NEUROSCIENCE & SOCIETY CHAMPION AWARD RECIPIENTS Accessibility Statement Skip Navigation Jennifer French and Eric H. Chudler recognized for bringing community perspectives and ethical considerations into neuroscience NEW YORK , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Dana Foundation has named Jennifer French, MBA, and Eric H. Chudler, Ph.D., recipients of its second annual Neuroscience & Society Champion Awards. Each award includes a $55,000 unrestricted grant to support work that advances neuroscience in ways that reflect and serve societal needs. French and Chudler were honored Saturday at the Foundation's reception during the Society for Neuroscience annual meeting. Continue Reading Jennifer French, MBA Eric H. Chudler, Ph.D. "Jennifer French and Eric Chudler clearly demonstrate how listening to people and incorporating their perspectives and experiences can shape neuroscience for the better," said Caroline Montojo, president and CEO of the Dana Foundation. "Through patient engagement, neuroscience outreach and education, and the integration of neuroethics, they have opened new paths for collaboration and helped more people participate in neuroscience and see its relevance to their lives. These awards recognize their leadership and support bold, creative ideas that strengthen neuroscience's benefits to society." Jennifer French: Patient engagement in research French is a champion of patient engagement in the development of neurotechnology to make the process more inclusive, collaborative, and responsive to societal needs. As founder and executive director of Neurotech Network, a nonprofit focused on neurotechnology education and advocacy, she has elevated the role of lived experience in shaping neurotechnology. French brings personal experience to this work. She lives with tetraplegia following a spinal cord injury and is an early user of an experimental implanted neural prosthesis for paralysis. She is also a founding member and past president of the North American Spinal Cord Injury Consortium. As board chair of the American Brain Coalition, French has led the creation of practical tools for collaboration among patients, federal agencies, policymakers, researchers, and industry developers. She also spearheaded the formation of the Implantable Brain-Computer Interface Collaborative Community (iBCI-CC) with Leigh Hochberg, M.D., Ph.D., and Jochen Lennerz, M.D., Ph.D., bringing diverse stakeholders together to advance regulatory science for implantable brain-computer interfaces. French's leadership in the neurotechnology and spinal cord injury communities has been recognized with the 2024 Craig H. Neilsen Foundation Visionary Prize and the Brooke Ellison Community Visionary Award. Eric H. Chudler: Public education and neuroethics Chudler has helped make neuroscience more accessible and responsive to communities through listening, public engagement, and the integration of neuroethics. A research neuroscientist and associate professor emeritus in the University of Washington's department of bioengineering, he also serves as executive director of the university's Center for Neurotechnology, where he championed the early integration of neuroethics into research, education, and career development. From his early outreach efforts, Chudler shaped learning experiences around participants' interests and questions, embracing a reciprocal approach to education. He has collaborated with classroom teachers and fellow neuroscientists to develop materials, programs, and activities that help people of all ages learn about the brain. He founded the Neuroscience for Kids website in 1997 and has led educational programs such as the Northwest Regional Emmy-winning "BrainWorks" video series. His contributions to neuroscience education and public engagement were recognized in 2003 with the Society for Neuroscience's Science Educator Award. With a 2023 Dana Foundation grant, Chudler created the Brain Health Learning Network, a program that helps older adults learn about neuroscience, make informed health decisions, and communicate their concerns to family, friends, and health care providers. About the Neuroscience & Society Champion Awards Now in their second year, the Dana Foundation's Neuroscience & Society Champion Awards draw on external nominations and internal canvassing to identify candidates. Recipients are selected for their outstanding contributions through a structured review by the Foundation's awards team. The Dana Foundation is a private philanthropic organization dedicated to advancing neuroscience and society, a human-centered neuroscience paradigm that connects brain research to real-world needs, values, and experiences. It brings together students, scientists, practitioners, and communities to reflect on assumptions, share expertise, and ensure that neuroscience serves people in meaningful and socially responsible ways. search_index.content: Better Life Science's STD Hero's At-Home STI Testing Draws AVN Spotlight Accessibility Statement Skip Navigation ALPHARETTA, Ga. , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Better Life Science 's STD Hero is featured in a new AVN report examining its at-home STI testing services for performers and the public, including new technology designed to simplify secure work-clearance verification. In "STD Hero Brings STI Testing Home for Performers & Public" , journalist Joanne Cachapero speaks with CEO Alan Brock about the PASS Certified Ultimate Hero kit, remotely supervised sample collection and identity verification safeguards. The feature also highlights STD Hero's digital Health Pass, which allows performers to store verified clearance in their phone's wallet and share results through a scannable QR code, with the pass automatically expiring after the 14-day clearance window. Brock also discusses the laboratory's speed and efficiency, reporting an average turnaround time of approximately 11 hours once samples arrive for processing. "We want to make sure that that's lightning fast so that we reduce that anxiety." The interview also explores Brock's commitment to expanding reliable testing access for independent creators, traveling performers and individuals living outside major production hubs, where convenient testing locations may be limited. Read the full feature at AVN.com . More information about STD Hero's at-home testing services is available at STDHero.com . ABOUT STD HERO: STD Hero is a sexual health and wellness brand providing professional STI and STD testing services. ABOUT BETTER LIFE SCIENCE: Better Life Science is a CLIA-certified laboratory providing direct-to-consumer at-home health testing designed to improve access to reliable diagnostics while maintaining clinical accuracy, privacy and regulatory compliance. Founded by a team of scientists, medical professionals and entrepreneurs, the company developed its model to reduce delays and barriers commonly associated with traditional healthcare systems. Through its direct-to-consumer platform, Better Life Science offers at-home testing across multiple categories, including sexually transmitted infection testing, food intolerance testing and food and inhalant allergy testing, supported by a portfolio of consumer-facing brands such as STD Hero, Rx Hero, Allergy Hero, Tick Bite Hero, Pet Test Hero and Fight Night Hero. The company also maintains an education-first approach, providing resources that help individuals better understand health risks, testing timelines and preventive considerations. Better Life Science is led by CEO Alan Brock and COO Daniel Fontenot, with laboratory oversight from Dr. David Eagerton and Dr. William Budd, and operates with core values center on accuracy, accessibility, integrity, empathy, innovation, partnership and community, as it continues advancing a modern diagnostic model focused on clarity, trust and practical health access. search_index.content: LifeNet Health Today Announced that Rony Thomas has Resigned Accessibility Statement Skip Navigation VIRGINIA BEACH, Va. , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LifeNet Health today announced that Rony Thomas has resigned as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of its Board of Directors, effective November 13, 2026. Mr. Thomas led LifeNet Health since 2004. During his tenure, the organization grew into a global leader in organ and tissue procurement and regenerative medicine. "On behalf of the Board, I thank Rony for his years of service to LifeNet Health and its mission," said Dr. John Herre, Chairman of the Board. "We wish him well in his future endeavors." "After more than two decades of service, I have stepped down as President and Chief Executive Officer of LifeNet Health," said Rony Thomas. "It has been a privilege to lead an organization so committed to honor the gift of donation and to improve the lives of patients around the world. I am proud of what the entire team, community and partners have accomplished during this time. I wish the organization continued success. I look forward to my next chapter." Douglas B. Wilson will continue to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. LifeNet Health's operations and its commitment to donors, families, and patients continue without interruption. About LifeNet Health As a global leader in regenerative medicine, LifeNet Health continues to push the boundaries to give healing every advantage. The organization offers groundbreaking transplantation and cellular solutions that support healthcare providers and powers scientific research. This forward-focused approach has improved life for millions of patients, all while honoring donor heroes and their families. For more information, visit: www.lifenethealth.org . search_index.content: Frontage Announces Proposed Privatization and Asset Restructuring to Unlock Shareholder Value and Fuel Strategic Growth Accessibility Statement Skip Navigation EXTON, Pa. , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Frontage Holdings Corporation ("Frontage") (HKEX: 1521) announced a proposal by an investor consortium for (i) the privatization of Frontage from the HKEX, and (ii) a subsequent asset restructuring (together, the "Transaction"). For further details regarding the Transaction, please refer to Frontage's announcement dated November 9, 2026, available on the Frontage website: www.frontagelab.com . As part of the asset restructuring, Frontage's business is expected to be divided among an investor consortium, comprising Charles River Laboratories, Tigermed, and Dr. Song Li, Frontage's Chairman. Specifically, upon completion of the restructuring, (i) Frontage's Exton, Pennsylvania-based bioanalysis and drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics (DMPK) business is expected to be owned and operated by Charles River Laboratories, (ii) Frontage's business in the People's Republic of China (the "PRC") and the business currently owned and operated by Acme Bioscience, Inc. and/or its subsidiaries are expected to be owned and operated by Tigermed, and (iii) Frontage's remaining business outside of the PRC, including bioanalysis and DMPK outside of Exton, Pennsylvania, is expected to be owned and operated by Dr. Song Li. "The Transaction aims to unlock shareholder value and position Frontage for future long-term growth." Dr. Wentao Zhang and Dr. Zhongping Lin, Executive Directors and Co-CEOs of Frontage, commented, "The proposed privatization will allow management to redeploy resources directly into core operations, while the subsequent restructuring of Frontage's business will empower local business units to navigate evolving regulatory frameworks, market conditions and client dynamics with greater focus and agility." The Transaction remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals, as well as customary closing conditions. Until the Transaction closes, Frontage will continue its business operations in the ordinary course. The same Frontage team will continue to support our clients on all ongoing projects, studies, and contracts with the same quality and timelines. Further details regarding the Transaction, including the expected schedule for the shareholder meetings, will be set out in a shareholder document to be dispatched to Frontage shareholders in due course. Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati is serving as the legal advisor to Frontage in this Transaction. About Frontage Frontage is a global Contract Research, Development, and Manufacturing Organization offering fully integrated, science-driven solutions across the drug discovery and development journey. For more information, visit www.frontagelab.com . search_index.content: United Airlines and the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority Unveil First New Concourse in Two Decades at Washington Dulles International Airport Accessibility Statement Skip Navigation At 435,000 square feet, Concourse E includes 14 new gates, direct AeroTrain access, new dining and retail options and a new, nearly 40,000-square-foot United Club℠, one of the largest airline clubs in the Western Hemisphere Concourse E marks a major milestone in Dulles' broader transformation, a multi-year, $20 billion capital investment program that includes new and modernized concourses, additional gates, an enhanced Main Terminal, expanded AeroTrain service and a new U.S. Customs facility United's newest plane, the Airbus A321XLR, expects to launch international service from Dulles to Amsterdam and Dublin in December United continues to grow at Dulles – with departures up 30% since 2022 – and has added six new international destinations this year and announced two more long-haul destinations for next year: Toulouse, France and Milan, Italy DULLES, Va. , Nov. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- United Airlines and the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority today previewed Concourse E at Washington Dulles International Airport, a 435,000-square-foot facility and the airport's first new concourse in nearly two decades, ahead of its opening to the public tomorrow. Continue Reading United Airlines and the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority Unveil First New Concourse in Two Decades at Washington Dulles International Airport New United Club in Concourse E Concourse E opens to travelers Nov. 10 with 14 new United gates, direct AeroTrain access, expansive new dining and retail options, and a new, nearly 40,000-square-foot United Club, one of the largest airline clubs in the Western Hemisphere. This new concourse builds on United's long-term investment to elevate the customer experience and support continued flight growth at its Washington Dulles hub. The opening marks a major milestone in Dulles' broader transformation as the Airports Authority, United Airlines and the U.S. Department of Transportation continue to collaborate on Dulles Global Gateway, a more than $20 billion capital investment program that will modernize the airport over the next decade. "Washington Dulles is a critical part of United's global network and growth strategy as it connects our nation's capital to the world," said United CEO Scott Kirby . "Concourse E delivers the kind of elevated experience our travelers and employees deserve today, and it's only the beginning as we work with the Airports Authority and the U.S. Department of Transportation to transform Dulles into one of the greatest airports in the world." "The Airports Authority is making strategic investments today to transform Dulles International into the National Capital Region's 'airport of the future,'" said Airports Authority President and CEO Jack Potter . "Opening Concourse E is the first step in expanding the airport's capacity and enhancing the passenger experience, building momentum for the broader modernization efforts that will shape Dulles and serve the traveling public for generations to come." "The Trump Administration's transformation of Washington Dulles International is key pillar of President Trump's efforts to make Washington D.C the greatest capital city in the world," said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy . "Today's unveiling of Concourse E is a sneak peek into the incredible international gateway IAD will become once the multi-year, multi-billion collaboration between USDOT, MWAA, and United Airlines is complete. This project will enhance the travel experience for millions of travelers and generate economic opportunity for the Capital region for years to come." More Gates and a Modern Travel Experience Concourse E adds 14 new United gates, which will allow the airline to fly more than 300 daily departures next summer – and grow its connectivity to other markets by nearly 30% during peak travel times – giving customers more flights and new destinations from Dulles. "Under President Trump, America is building again. So far, the construction of United's new Concourse E has supported 2,700 good paying jobs and brought $1.3 billion in local economic activity to the national capital region. USDOT's broader partnership with MWAA and United on the Dulles Airport transformation is just beginning, with many more milestones on the horizon. The ultimate winner will be the American people who will enjoy a stunning new gateway to America's capital for generations to come. Congratulations to MWAA and United for today's grand unveiling, and we look forward to even greater results in the near future," said Deputy Secretary of Transportation Steven Bradbury. The concourse features bright, spacious gate areas with natural light, in-seat power outlets and wireless charging pads, as well as enhanced restrooms. Direct AeroTrain access to Concourse E makes it easier for travelers to move between the Main Terminal and their gate and creates a more efficient pathway for travelers to move through the airport. Each gate has the flexibility to support domestic and international flights, with configurations that can accommodate one widebody plane or two narrowbody planes. This concourse opening is the first of four planned Concourse E construction phases, with future Concourse E phases expected to add up to 36 more United gates and a new international customs processing area for connecting travelers, along with plans for one of the largest United Polaris® lounges in the world. United's Second-Largest Club Spanning nearly 40,000 square feet with seating for more than 600 customers, the new United Club in Concourse E is the airline's second-largest club and increases United's club and lounge space at Dulles by approximately 70 percent, further elevating the experience for United customers traveling through the hub. search_index.content: IBM and Microsoft Announce a New AI Agent Platform Designed for Industry-Specific Transformation Accessibility Statement Skip Navigation IBM Consulting brings more than 6,000 pre-built AI agents and assets, the experience building them, and industry expertise, while Microsoft provides AI, cloud, and security technologies New platform comes with forward-deployed engineering support from both Microsoft and IBM Consulting SEI's enterprise transformation illustrates the types of business needs that agentic AI can help address ARMONK, N.Y. and REDMOND, Wash. , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- IBM (NYSE: IBM ) and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT ) today announced Imagine Enterprise, an agentic platform designed to help enterprises build, run, and govern AI agents that help people execute industry-specific processes. IBM Consulting and Microsoft have combined their technologies and expertise with forward-deployed engineering support for qualifying engagements to help enterprises accelerate AI deployment. Continue Reading IBM Imagine Enterprise aims to help organizations—especially in regulated industries—combine human expertise with AI agents and connect them to unique enterprise data and daily processes. The platform is built to help organizations govern AI agents with controls, observability, and AI-compliance support designed to help secure industry-specific AI deployment. IBM Consulting brings AI transformation expertise and a fleet of more than 6,000 AI agents and assets built on IBM Consulting Advantage , the company's AI-powered delivery platform. Microsoft provides the AI, data, cloud, and security foundation that is designed to help the agents operate securely across the enterprise, while forward-deployed engineers from both companies can help customers move from experimentation to production. Instead of organizations having to start from scratch, replace the platforms they already depend on, or spend months assembling the pieces themselves, Imagine Enterprise is designed around three simple advantages: Instant Expertise: More than 6,000 AI agents and assets Starting with pre-built AI agents, assets, and deep industry expertise from day one. Organizations can begin with capabilities already built for their industry and adapt them to the unique needs of their business. Fits the Enterprise: A platform that adapts Imagine Enterprise is designed to connect with an organization's existing data, processes, systems, and technology environment. Enterprises can start where they are, build on what they already have, and scale over time, with enterprise security, identity, AI governance, and control built into the experience. Intelligence Multiplier: Puts the knowledge of the business behind people and AI agents Imagine Enterprise brings IBM Consulting's hands-on experience building and running more than 6,000 AI agents together with the Microsoft technologies to connect enterprise knowledge, data, and context across the organization. People and agents can operate with richer enterprise knowledge and context behind them, helping put what they already know to work across people and agents. Supporting these advantages, Microsoft and GitHub technologies including Microsoft Foundry, GitHub Copilot, and Microsoft Copilot Studio help coordinate AI agents and enterprise systems, while Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft 365 infrastructure, Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Defender, and Microsoft Azure provide the data, identity, AI governance, security, and cloud foundation. IBM Consulting Advantage's Process Studio, Context Studio, and Advantage Core help organizations design, deploy, and govern tailored AI agents. From Emerging Technology to Business Opportunity SEI, a leading global provider of financial technology, operations, and asset management services within the financial services industry, is looking to advance its enterprise transformation by exploring emerging and agentic technologies with IBM Consulting, with the support of Microsoft, and is leveraging other technologies from IBM Consulting and Microsoft to help improve how the company operates and enhance the experiences it delivers to employees and clients, supporting SEI's commitment to sustainable growth. "AI is evolving quickly, and our focus at SEI is on applying it with intention in ways that strengthen trust, enhance human decision-making, and create meaningful value across our business," said Sneha Shah, Chief AI Strategist and Head of SEI Next . "Our work with IBM Consulting and Microsoft is helping us explore how emerging capabilities could support critical processes and be responsibly scaled over time, with the goal to create better experiences for our employees and clients. By combining emerging technology with SEI's deep industry and operational expertise, we can move faster, scale more effectively, and create new opportunities for growth." "Clients are no longer looking for AI that simply helps people do the same work a little faster. They want to build an agentic business," said Mohamad Ali, Senior Vice President and Head of IBM Consulting . "Microsoft and IBM are helping organizations bring human expertise and digital labor together in a way that can scale across the enterprise, to turn AI from a productivity aid into a real competitive advantage." "Enterprise AI will be won by organizations that can turn their data, industry expertise, and AI into action," said Rodrigo Kede Lima, President, Microsoft Frontier Company . "Together, Microsoft and IBM Consulting are bringing the best of our technology and expertise, to help customers move from AI ambition to business impact faster and with confidence." Imagine Enterprise's industry-specific frameworks initially include financial services, insurance, and retail, and are designed to establish a repeatable blueprint for potential additional industries such as manufacturing, energy, public sector, mobility and more in the future. search_index.content: AT&T Breaks Ground on New Global Headquarters: America's Most Connected Corporate Campus Accessibility Statement Skip Navigation AT&T Lays the First Fiber at Its 54-Acre Plano Campus, Reinforcing Its Long-Term Investment in North Texas PLANO, Texas , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AT&T (NYSE: T ) today broke ground on its new global headquarters in Plano, Texas, marking the start of construction with a distinct AT&T milestone: the installation of the campus's first fiber connection. Continue Reading PLANO, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 12: (L-R) Jason Morrissey, Craig Ackerman, AT&T CEO John Stankey, Christopher Kim, Mayor of Plano John Muns, Stephen Zarate, Russell Jackson, Cecilia McDonald, and Connor Fry lay the first fiber at the groundbreaking for AT&T's new global headquarters on November 12, 2026 in Plano, Texas. (Photo by Rick Kern/Getty Images for AT&T) New AT&T global headquarters rendering. New AT&T global headquarters rendering. The new headquarters represents a strategic investment in AT&T's people, culture, and employee experience. Spanning 54 acres and 2.2 million square feet, the seven-building campus will bring AT&T's Dallas-Fort Worth teams together in an integrated, horizontal headquarters designed to foster collaboration and innovation. With workspaces and amenities shaped around employees' needs, the campus will also help AT&T attract, develop, and retain talent for the future. Engineered as a workplace of the future, the new headquarters will demonstrate what AT&T connectivity makes possible at scale. AT&T fiber and wireless will provide the speed, capacity and low latency needed for AI, real-time collaboration, and emerging workplace technologies. An approximately 250-foot working cell tower, together with fiber and 5G throughout the campus, will provide advanced connectivity for employees and improve wireless connectivity in the surrounding community. The tower will also serve as a recognizable Plano landmark and symbol of AT&T's commitment to a more connected future. To celebrate the first fiber connection, AT&T executives and employees were joined by Plano Mayor John Muns; Scott Armstrong, principal at Gensler; Eric Hage, president of KDC; and Andy Leatherman, vice chairman at CBRE. John Stankey, chairman and CEO of AT&T, spoke about what the campus will mean for the company: "Our new headquarters in Plano is an investment for our current and future employees, and our North Texas community. With this new campus, we're creating the environment that makes life better, drives collaboration and serves our customers for decades to come." John Muns, mayor of Plano, said, "Today marks an exciting milestone for AT&T and the City of Plano," said Mayor John Muns. "This new global headquarters represents a significant investment in our community and reinforces Plano's reputation as a place where businesses can grow and succeed. We're proud to see this project taking shape and the opportunities it will bring to Plano." Scott Armstrong, principal at Gensler, said, "Great workplaces do more than support the way people work. They create connections, strengthen culture, and provide a sense of belonging. The vision for AT&T's new headquarters creates a world-class destination where innovative workplaces, exceptional amenities, and thoughtfully designed experiences come together to support people in new ways. It is a forward-looking campus that honors the strength of AT&T's legacy while creating an environment designed to inspire connection, innovation, and the possibilities of what comes next." Eric Hage, president of KDC, said, "We are proud to partner with AT&T on a project that is raising the bar for the corporate campus of the future. With a long history of developing large scale developments in this market, KDC brings the experience to deliver on a vision of this scale and ambition. Our partnership combines AT&T's forward thinking with KDC's development and construction expertise to create a headquarters in Plano that we believe will help shape how the next generation of office is planned and built." Andy Leatherman, vice chairman at CBRE, said, "From day one, AT&T demonstrated an unwavering commitment to its people and a clear vision for the future of work. The result is a best-in-class environment designed to inspire collaboration, enhance productivity, and support employee well-being, creating a model that other organizations will look to as they shape their own workplace strategies." AT&T has called North Texas home since 2008 and expects to welcome its first employees to the new campus in the second half of 2028. search_index.content: The Conference Board Employment Trends Index™ (ETI) Increased Year-on-Year in October Accessibility Statement Skip Navigation NEW YORK , Nov. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Conference Board Employment Trends Index™ (ETI) edged down to 108.36 in October—a 0.1% m/m decline from an upwardly revised reading of 108.43 in September—but increased by 2.4% from a year ago. The ETI is a leading composite index for future payroll employment. When the Index increases, payroll employment may grow as well, and vice versa. Turning points in the Index indicate that a change in the trend of job gains or losses might occur in the coming months. "In October, nonfarm payrolls added 165,000 jobs , and the unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1%," said Conrad Qi, Economic Data Scientist Associate at The Conference Board. "Despite the minor m/m downtick in the ETI, the measure increased by 2.4% y/y in October, up from 1.9% y/y in September and -1.0% y/y in October 2025. The annual growth rate of the ETI has been edging higher over the last six months." Three of the ETI's eight components contributed positively to the index in October. Ranked by the magnitude of their positive contribution, they were: Percentage of Firms with Positions Not Able to Fill Right Now , which rose to 36% from 32% in September, indicating demand for workers in small firms is rising; Number of Employees Hired by the Temporary-Help Industry , which increased by 18,600 in October; and Initial Claims for Unemployment Insurance . Four of the ETI's eight components contributed negatively to the index in October. Ranked by the magnitude of their negative contribution, they were: Ratio of Involuntarily Part-time to All Part-time Workers , which rose to 17.6% from 16.5% in September; Real Manufacturing and Trade Sales , which fell by an estimated 0.3%; Job Openings , estimated to have decreased by 73,000 to 7.45 million; and Industrial Production , which edged down by 0.1%. One of the ETI's eight components, Percentage of Respondents Who Say They Find 'Jobs Hard to Get , ' was unchanged in October. About the Employment Trends Index™ The eight leading indicators of employment aggregated into the Employment Trends Index include: Percentage of Respondents Who Say They Find "Jobs Hard to Get" (The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Survey ® ) Initial Claims for Unemployment Insurance (U.S. Department of Labor) Percentage of Firms with Positions Not Able to Fill Right Now (© National Federation of Independent Business Research Foundation) Number of Employees Hired by the Temporary-Help Industry (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics) Ratio of Involuntarily Part-time to All Part-time Workers (BLS)† Job Openings (BLS)* Industrial Production (Federal Reserve Board)* Real Manufacturing and Trade Sales (U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis)** *Statistical imputation for the recent month **Statistical imputation for the two most recent months † The October 2025 part-time ratio is based on estimated part-time employment figures. The Conference Board publishes the Employment Trends Index monthly, at 10 a.m. ET, on the Monday that follows each Friday release of the Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation report. The technical notes to this series are available on The Conference Board website: http://www.conference-board.org/data/eti.cfm . About The Conference Board The Conference Board is the Member-driven think tank that delivers Trusted Insights for What's Ahead®. Please check chat.fhir.org/confluence for updates. --> HL7 Edit space details Pages Space shortcuts HL7 Essentials HL7.org HL7 Work Groups & Projects HL7 Documentation & Help Project Scope Statements Project Proposals Zoom WGM Information and Agendas - May 2026 Page tree Browse pages Configure Space tools Jira links A t tachments (1) Page History Highlight Page Terms Export Glossary terms Page Information Resolved comments View in Hierarchy View Source Export to Word Hide Inline Comments HL7 Balloting Created by Lloyd McKenzie , last updated on Jan 08, 2026 8 minute read Quick Links Importing ballot results from spreadsheets Request Help Uploading Ballot Spreadsheets Jira Ballot Process Coordinating Ballot Submissions HL7 Ballot Desktop How to Guide for Balloting using Jira Jira Ballot Administrative Processes JIRA Balloting FAQs Reconciliation spreadsheets Jira Balloting Pilot Information Webinar Slide Deck Overview Balloting is the formal process that HL7 uses to get feedback and comments on specifications prior to publication. Rules governing balloting are defined in both HL7's Governance and Operations Manual and in the HL7 Essential Requirements . These, in turn, are governed by the expectations of the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) which accredits HL7 as a standards development organization and enforces rules around the openness and fairness of approval processes. The objective of balloting is to actively seek feedback on a proposed standard and to ensure that the community that will be governed by that standard is in agreement with the expectations set by the standard. In the balloting process, a "frozen" version of a specification is subjected to review during a scheduled time window. Reviewers who have registered for the ballot can submit comments about the specification that raise issues and propose changes. They also cast an overall vote indicating whether they believe the specification should be published in its current form. The sponsoring Work Group(s) then review the comments provided and address them through a process called reconciliation. Based on the response of the Work Group(s), the balloter may choose to adjust their vote by "withdrawing" negative votes. The final determination of whether the specification can proceed to publication as a 'standard' is driven by the balance of affirmative votes received and varies depending on the type of ballot. Ballot Levels HL7 specifications can be balloted at one of four levels: For Comment ballots are used early in the development cycle to solicit feedback from the community. Such ballots never result in the authorization to publish a specification. They are intended to give guidance and direction to the Work Group developing the specification by soliciting review from the community outside the participants performing the development work. These ballots have the least onerous requirements in terms of response to feedback. There isn't really a notion of "pass" or "fail" for comment ballots. Informative ballots are used to vet content that is not intended to be binding on implementers. It is often used for specifications that guide internal HL7 processes or that give non-binding recommendations/guidance to the implementer community. Because the specification resulting from such a process is non-binding, requirements for consensus and limitations on substantive change between review and final publication are lower than other ballot types. Standard for Trial Use (STU) ballots are used to vet content that is eventually intended to be binding on implementers. It is used to vet content that is deemed "ready to implement" by the sponsoring work group, but where there has not yet been significant implementation experience. STU specifications are time-limited and give an opportunity for the community to exercise the specification in real-world implementation before the specification is "locked down" and forward and backward compatibility rules come into play. STU specifications are also non-binding and therefore requirements for consensus and limitations on substantive change between review and final publication are also lower. Normative ballots are used for final review of specifications that are intended to be binding on the implementer community and where there are strict rules around future changes to preserve a degree of forward and/or backward compatibility. The specifications that result from this process are considered authoritative. As such, the rules for consensus are highest and any issues raised during the review process receive the greatest degree of scrutiny by the community. There are strict limits on the types of changes that can be made between the ballot review process and eventual publication. It is common for specifications to undergo multiple cycles (where content is submitted for ballot, feedback is received and applied and the content is returned to ballot) before the community is satisfied and the specification can be published as an official standard. If consensus cannot be reached (i.e. agreement between some balloters and the authoring Work Group(s) cannot be achieved), a recirculation ballot is held. Under ANSI rules, most Normative-balloted content is subject to periodic review to confirm that the specification is still relevant. This review takes the form of a Reaffirmation ballot. Such ballots are subject to the same rules as a Normative ballot. In addition, Recirculation ballots are a special process invoked at the conclusion of some Normative ballots. They are limited to the pool of voters who submitted votes as part of the original Normative ballot process. search_index.content: Foundation-module - FHIR v5.0.0 Release 5 Foundation This page is part of the FHIR Specification (v5.0.0: R5 - STU ). This is the current published version. For a full list of available versions, see the Directory of published versions . Page versions: R5 R4B R4 R3 Work Group FHIR Infrastructure Standards Status : Informative 2.0 Foundation Module The Foundation Module is responsible for the overall infrastructure of the FHIR specification. Every implementer works with the content in the foundation module whichever way they use FHIR. The Foundation Module maintains most of the basic documentation for the FHIR specification. In addition, the Foundation Module includes the following resources: Foundation Framework Resource DomainResource Basic Binary Bundle Content Management Resources. Questionnaire QuestionnaireResponse List Composition DocumentReference Data Exchange Resources. OperationOutcome Parameters Subscription SubscriptionStatus SubscriptionTopic MessageHeader 2.0.1 Relationships with other modules All the other modules depend on the foundation module The Exchange module builds on the foundation model by defining the recognized methods for exchange of resources The Terminology module provides the formal basis for using Concepts defined in Code Systems in the definitions The Conformance module provides the basis for extending the foundation for national and local use The Security & Privacy provides the linking framework to external standards for security and privacy The Implementation Support module builds on the foundation to provide testing and reference implementations 2.0.2 Developmental Roadmap Several components of the foundation module have now reached normative status. The focus over the next 18-24 months as the 6th release of FHIR is prepared is to focus on some of the non-normative elements and move them towards normative status, such as Questionnaire, List, DocumentReference and Subscription. Exactly which resources will be candidates for normative release will be driven, in part, by the degree of implementation - and whether that implementation is communicated back to HL7. These resources are stable, normative, and widely used. No additional scope or features have been proposed: Resource DomainResource Binary Bundle Parameters OperationOutcome These resources have been widely used, and are considered stable, but some new features are still in trial: Questionnaire QuestionnaireResponse List DocumentReference (note that here have been significant redesigns in this version). These resources have been used, and the use led to a significant redesign that is undergoing trial use: Subscription : SubscriptionStatus : SubscriptionTopic : These resources have not been widely used: Basic (note that no additional requirements have been identified since R2) MessageHeader FHIR ®© HL7.org 2011+.
